checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：高度符合需求，明确使用负荷数据与拓扑标签作为输入，面向不同运行模式/拓扑变化下的 AC-OPF 快速求解，并先预测电压幅值与相角，再通过潮流计算恢复完整 OPF 解。 / English: Strongly consistent with the requirement; it explicitly uses load data plus topology labels as inputs, targets fast AC-OPF solving under different operating patterns/topology changes, and predicts voltage magnitudes and phase angles before reconstructing the full OPF solution via power flow.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：主要局限在于依赖已聚类的运行模式标签，且验证规模偏小；对更大系统、完全未知拓扑或标签外模式的泛化能力可能受限。 / English: Main limitation is reliance on clustered operating-pattern labels and relatively small validation scale; generalization to larger systems, fully unknown topologies, or out-of-label patterns may be limited.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：总体可行，属于快速数据驱动 AC-OPF 近似模型，输入包含网络拓扑与负荷场景，适合在拓扑变化或不同工况下进行快速推断。 / English: Feasible overall; it is a fast data-driven AC-OPF approximation with inputs including network topology and load scenarios, suitable for rapid inference under topology changes or varying operating conditions.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：它更偏向模仿最优解的近似推断，而不是显式识别历史运行模式；对训练分布之外的拓扑变化，性能可能下降。 / English: It is more of an imitation-based approximation than an explicit operating-pattern discovery model; performance may drop when topology changes go beyond the training distribution.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：部分符合“先预测电压幅值和相角，再通过网络方程恢复其余变量”的思路，但核心任务是安全约束 OPF，且更偏向固定网络下的快速近似，不是面向不同拓扑/未知结构的专门模型。 / English: It partially matches the idea of predicting voltage magnitudes and angles first and recovering the remaining variables via network equations, but the core task is security-constrained OPF and it is mainly a fast approximation for a fixed network rather than a model specifically designed for different topologies/unknown structures.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：未突出使用拓扑标签来适配网络结构变化，因此与“不同网络拓扑/未知网络结构下快速预测”的要求存在明显偏差。 / English: It does not emphasize topology labels for adapting to network-structure changes, so it deviates materially from the requirement for fast prediction under different/unknown network topologies.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：能够快速预测 AC-OPF 相关变量，并在扩展模型中输出电压角与无功发电，符合“先预测电压/相角再恢复完整解”的部分思路。 / English: It can quickly predict AC-OPF-related variables and, in the extended model, outputs voltage angles and reactive generation, which partially fits the workflow of predicting voltages/angles first and then recovering the full solution.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：它更依赖热启动/相似历史状态，且主要面向单时段快照；对未知或频繁变化拓扑的显式建模与泛化不够贴合。 / English: It relies more on hot-start/similar historical states and is mainly a single-snapshot model; explicit modeling and generalization for unknown or frequently changing topologies are not well aligned.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：具备数据驱动 AC-OPF 快速近似、预测电压幅值与相角、再通过校准与潮流重构获得可行解的能力，和需求中的求解流程有较强一致性。 / English: It has a strong match with the requested workflow by providing data-driven AC-OPF approximation, predicting voltage magnitudes and angles, and then using calibration plus power-flow reconstruction to obtain feasible solutions.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：更偏向固定拓扑下的物理信息学习与可行性校准，没有明确把“网络结构未知或变化”作为输入建模重点，因此对拓扑切换场景的针对性不足。 / English: It is more focused on physics-informed learning and feasibility calibration under fixed topologies, without explicitly targeting unknown or changing network structure as an input modeling focus, so it is less tailored to topology-switching scenarios.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：属于数据驱动、物理约束的 OPF 快速近似方法，也能输出电压幅值/相角与机组出力，说明在快速求解 AC-OPF 方面具备一定可行性。 / English: It is a data-driven, physics-informed OPF approximation that can output voltage magnitudes/angles and generator dispatch, so it has some feasibility for fast AC-OPF solving.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：虽然强调多拓扑、多负荷条件和电网基础模型预训练，方向上与“利用历史数据适应不同工况”有关，但它不是一个已完成的 AC-OPF 快速求解模型。 / English: Although it emphasizes multi-topology, multi-load pretraining and is directionally related to adapting to varying conditions from historical data, it is not a completed fast AC-OPF solving model.

ranked_candidates.recommendation_reason: 该模型与用户需求高度一致：明确面向不同运行模式与拓扑变化下的 AC-OPF 快速求解，直接使用负荷数据和拓扑标签作为输入，并先预测电压幅值与相角，再通过潮流计算恢复完整 OPF 解。 / This model matches the requirement very closely: it is explicitly designed for fast AC-OPF under different operating patterns and topology changes, uses load data and topology labels as inputs, and predicts voltage magnitudes and phase angles before reconstructing the full OPF solution via power flow.
ranked_candidates.matched_needs: 支持历史数据驱动的运行模式识别 / Supports data-driven operating-pattern handling；使用负荷数据与拓扑标签输入 / Uses load data plus topology labels as inputs；可在拓扑变化时快速预测电压并恢复完整解 / Quickly predicts voltages and reconstructs the full solution under topology changes；面向 AC-OPF 而非仅静态潮流 / Targets AC-OPF rather than only static power flow.
ranked_candidates.strengths: 直接对应“不同运行模式/不同拓扑”场景 / Directly addresses varying operating patterns and topologies；输出电压幅值与相角，符合用户希望先预测状态量再做潮流重构 / Outputs voltage magnitudes and angles, matching the desired two-stage workflow；速度提升显著，适合快速推断 / Large speedup makes it suitable for fast inference；CNN + 聚类标签有助于从历史样本中提取模式 / CNN plus clustered labels helps extract patterns from historical data.
ranked_candidates.limitations: 依赖已识别的运行模式标签，面对完全未见过的拓扑或超出训练分布的工况时，精度与稳定性可能下降 / Relies on identified operation-pattern labels, so accuracy and stability may drop on unseen topologies or out-of-distribution operating conditions；验证主要集中在较小规模系统，向更大电网扩展时需要额外泛化验证 / Validation is mainly on a smaller system, so larger-grid deployment needs additional generalization checks.
ranked_candidates.simple_model_explanation: 先把历史工况按模式分组，再用 CNN 根据负荷和拓扑标签预测各母线电压幅值与相角，最后用潮流方程补全发电机出力与完整 OPF 解 / First groups historical cases into operating patterns, then uses a CNN to predict bus voltage magnitudes and angles from load and topology labels, and finally uses power-flow equations to recover generator outputs and the complete OPF solution.

ranked_candidates.recommendation_reason: 该模型也是很强的匹配项，适合在网络拓扑和负荷场景变化时快速近似 AC-OPF。它使用图神经网络和局部消息传递，天然适合图结构电网，并且推理速度快、可扩展性好。 / This is also a strong match for quickly approximating AC-OPF when network topology and load scenarios change. It uses a graph neural network with local message passing, which is naturally suited to graph-structured power grids, and it offers fast inference and good scalability.
ranked_candidates.matched_needs: 支持拓扑输入与负荷场景输入 / Supports topology and load-scenario inputs；可快速近似 AC-OPF / Can quickly approximate AC-OPF；适合电网图结构建模 / Well suited to graph-structured power networks；对大规模网络具有可扩展性 / Scales to larger networks.

top_rows.Requirement text: I need a data-driven model that can quickly solve AC-OPF under different operating patterns / different network topologies. Traditional AC-OPF methods usually model only a fixed operating pattern. When line outage states, network topology, or operating conditions change, the model needs to be adjusted again, which significantly reduces computational efficiency. In real grids, due to renewable energy fluctuations, equipment state changes, and line interruptions, operating patterns are not fixed. Therefore, an AC-OPF solution method is needed that can use historical data to identify operating patterns and use load data plus network topology labels as inputs. In this way, even when the network structure is unknown or changing, the model can quickly predict voltage magnitudes and phase angles, and then obtain the complete OPF solution through power flow calculation.

requirement.requirement_text: I need a fast and reliable ACOPF solver for modern smart grids. Due to renewable energy integration, electric vehicle growth, and increasingly unpredictable loads, system operation requires more fine-grained and more frequent ACOPF calculations. However, ACOPF itself is non-convex and NP-hard, and traditional solvers are limited in speed. Although data-driven methods can directly predict OPF solutions from load demand, it is difficult to guarantee both optimality and feasibility, especially because hard constraints, power flow balance constraints, and line constraints may be violated. Therefore, a model combining physics-informed learning and feasibility calibration is needed. It should first use machine learning to predict voltage magnitudes and angles, and then use a calibration algorithm to correct power flow imbalance, so that the final result is close to optimal and satisfies ACOPF physical constraints as much as possible.

Due to renewable energy integration, electric vehicle growth, and increasingly unpredictable loads, system operation requires more fine-grained and more frequent ACOPF calculations. However, ACOPF itself is non-convex and NP-hard, and traditional solvers are limited in speed. Although data-driven methods can directly predict OPF solutions from load demand, it is difficult to guarantee both optimality and feasibility, especially because hard constraints, power flow balance constraints, and line constraints may be violated. Therefore, a model combining physics-informed learning and feasibility calibration is needed. It should first use machine learning to predict voltage magnitudes and angles, and then use a calibration algorithm to correct power flow imbalance, so that the final result is close to optimal and satisfies ACOPF physical constraints as much as possible.

data_properties.hasModelName: Data driven ACOPF Physics informed Learning Calibration
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Data-driven AC Optimal Power Flow with Physics-informed Learning and Calibrations
data_properties.hasAuthor: Junfei Wang; Pirathayini Srikantha
data_properties.hasInstitution: York University
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Generate ACOPF solutions using physics-informed deep learning and feasibility calibration.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Need for a more efficient and reliable ACOPF solver because ACOPF is nonconvex, NP-hard, and difficult to solve quickly in modern grids.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: AC optimal power flow on IEEE bus-14 and bus-118 benchmark systems.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a data-driven ACOPF model produce near-optimal solutions while improving feasibility without relying on traditional solvers?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal bus voltage magnitudes and phase angles, generator active/reactive power dispatch, and calibrated feasible ACOPF solutions.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Two-stage physics-informed DNN prediction followed by iterative feasibility calibration.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with complex bus injections and Y-bus network model.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Generator buses, load buses, voltage magnitude/phase angle limits, and line flow limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Physics-informed loss, cycle-consistency reconstruction, and Gauss-Seidel-style calibration with warm starts.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported 0.67% optimality gap on IEEE 14-bus and 0.15% on IEEE 118-bus; calibration converged on all 14-bus tests and 92.2% on 118-bus.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uses active and reactive power demand at all buses as input.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator cost functions Cg(PGg) typically convex quadratic in active power generation.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Generator active/reactive limits; AC power-balance equations at each bus; voltage magnitude and phase-angle bounds; line apparent-power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Active and reactive demand PDi, QDi; generator outputs PGg, QGg; bus voltages |Vi|, ϕi; Y-bus admittance matrix; voltage and flow bounds; calibration stop threshold ρ and maximum epochs E.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: A CNN predicts voltages and angles from demand; power-flow equations reconstruct generator outputs and demand; an iterative calibration loop updates load-bus voltages and generator injections until imbalance is below ρ or E is reached.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Trained and tested on 100K MATPOWER-generated samples for IEEE 14-bus and 118-bus systems, using 80/20 split; compared against supervised learning and DeepOPF-V.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method achieved lower feasibility error and smaller optimality gaps than baselines, with strong convergence on both benchmark systems.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: improved feasibility with near-optimal solutions and no traditional solver in the prediction stage. Limitation: calibration did not converge for all 118-bus test cases.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Future work mentions robust learning under input uncertainties and unsupervised or semi-supervised learning without labeled ACOPF solver data.
data_properties.hasSourceFileName: Data-driven AC Optimal Power Flow with.pdf

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Machine Learning-Aided Security Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Jubeyer Rahman; Cong Feng; Jie Zhang
data_properties.hasInstitution: The University of Texas at Dallas
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve security-constrained AC optimal power flow efficiently using a machine-learning-aided approach.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Full AC OPF is highly nonlinear and non-convex, making large-scale security-constrained solving computationally challenging.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained AC optimal power flow with switched shunt security constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a machine-learning-aided method predict key OPF variables and avoid running a physics-based OPF solver while preserving feasibility?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Bus voltage magnitudes and voltage angles; derived current injections, complex/real power injections, generator dispatch settings, and branch power flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid machine-learning-aided OPF using multi-input multi-output random forest plus physics-based network equations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with bus admittance matrix, current injection, apparent power, and nodal power balance.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period steady-state OPF.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Not specified; load samples from hourly ERCOT profile used for training/testing.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per case.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: No explicit uncertainty model; trained on sampled load cases.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC transmission OPF with generators, buses, branches, and switched shunts.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Multi-input multi-output random forest predicts voltages, then network equations recover remaining variables.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported zero constraint violation for the proposed method and much faster solution time than MATPOWER MIPS.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Load demand inputs Pd and Qd are used as predictors; no demand response model.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator costs represented by individual piece-wise linear cost functions.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Voltage magnitude and angle bounds; generator active/reactive power bounds; switched shunt susceptance bounds; real and reactive nodal power balance equations; branch apparent power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes vi and angles θi; generator outputs pg and qg; switched shunt susceptance bcs; real/reactive demands pd and qd; branch flow limit sf; bus admittance matrix Y; generator cost cg.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: RF is trained on converged MATPOWER solutions; case I predicts v and θ then computes injections and costs via network equations; case II predicts all OPF variables directly.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on a 500-bus GO competition network using 8,760 load samples; compared against MATPOWER MIPS and a pure ML baseline.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method closely matches MIPS voltage solutions, satisfies network constraints, and reduces total solution time from 2030.4 s to 35.26 s.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: fast and feasible OPF approximation without running a physics-based solver. Limitation: pure end-to-end ML still causes many equality-constraint violations.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Potentially useful for post-contingency analysis with many network topologies and load profiles.

requirement.requirement_text: I need a physics-informed data-driven OPF model that can replace traditional iterative OPF calculation. Under high renewable penetration and probabilistic analysis scenarios, OPF needs to be solved repeatedly, in large quantities, and in real time. Traditional model-driven methods have high computational burden, while ordinary neural networks require extensive hyperparameter tuning, and directly learning the complex mapping from system operating status to OPF solutions is very difficult. Therefore, a machine learning framework incorporating the physical structure of OPF is needed. It should decompose the complex OPF mapping into multiple stages, gradually learn branch flows, voltages, generator outputs, and objective function values, and use active constraint identification for sample pre-classification, so as to reduce learning complexity, improve generalization ability, and obtain high-quality OPF solutions in a short time.

selected_candidates.why_matched: 中文说明：该模型明确以物理约束神经网络求解受物理方程约束的问题，符合“引入物理结构、降低黑箱学习难度”的核心诉求；其连续/离散时间物理约束训练也契合用物理信息提升泛化与数据效率的需求。 / English explanation: This model explicitly uses physics-informed neural networks to solve physics-constrained problems, matching the need to inject physical structure and reduce black-box learning difficulty. selected_candidates.main_risk_or_gap: 中文说明：它面向通用非线性 PDE，而不是专门为 OPF 设计；没有直接体现分阶段学习支路潮流、电压、机组出力和目标值，也没有主动约束识别机制。 / English explanation: It targets general nonlinear PDEs rather than OPF specifically; it does not directly implement staged learning of branch flows, voltages, generator outputs, and objective values, nor active constraint identification.
supporting_evidence: hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve forward and inverse problems governed by nonlinear partial differential equations using physics-informed neural networks.

data_properties.hasModelName: Data Driven Physics Informed SELM OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Data-Driven Optimal Power Flow: A Physics-Informed Machine Learning Approach
data_properties.hasAuthor: Xingyu Lei; Zhifang Yang; Juan Yu; Junbo Zhao; Qian Gao; Hongxin Yu
data_properties.hasInstitution: Chongqing University; Mississippi State University; State Grid Chongqing Electric Power Company Electric Power Research Institute
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Learn OPF solutions directly from operating conditions using a physics-informed data-driven regression framework.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Reduce the high computational burden of repeated OPF solves and improve real-time applicability.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Nonlinear, nonconvex OPF calculation for large-scale power systems with renewable uncertainty and many samples.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can SELM-based physics-informed decomposition and sample pre-classification accurately approximate OPF solutions faster than model-based and deep-learning methods?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generator active/reactive dispatch, bus voltage magnitudes/angles, branch active/reactive flows, and objective function value.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Three-stage SELM regression with reinforcement mode and sample pre-classification by active constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with branch-flow and voltage-state learning stages.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Monte Carlo-generated training samples with renewable and load fluctuations.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: IEEE 39, 57, 118-bus and Polish 2383-bus benchmark systems with wind and photovoltaic integration.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Feature decomposition, reinforcement-mode SELM, and active-constraint sample clustering.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Fast training and testing with improved accuracy over original SELM and deep-learning alternatives.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Power demand inputs PDi and QDi; renewables treated as negative loads.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation operating cost, modeled as the sum of quadratic generator cost functions over generator buses.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power balance equations; branch active/reactive flow equations; generator active/reactive limits; bus voltage magnitude limits; branch flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients a2i, a1i, a0i; admittance conductance Gij and susceptance Bij; demand PDi, QDi; limits on PGi, QGi, Vi, PFk; penalty factor C.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Training samples are generated by Monte Carlo simulation and an interior-point OPF solver, then used to train SELM networks in three stages with reinforcement and classification.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 39/57/118-bus and Polish 2383-bus systems; compared against original SELM, deep learning, and model-based OPF.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed approach achieved the best accuracy and much faster computation, and direct learning with original SELM was intractable for OPF.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: fast, few hyperparameters, extensible across systems. Limitation: direct deep learning and original SELM struggle with OPF complexity; future work targets field-data validation.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Sample pre-classification uses active-constraint critical regions to cluster similar OPF samples.

evidence_package.why_matched: 中文说明：该模型直接面向用机器学习替代物理求解器的OPF加速，输出母线电压、相角、发电出力和支路潮流，并通过网络方程恢复其余变量，符合“快速重复求解、减少计算负担”的核心需求。 / English explanation: This model directly targets replacing the physics-based solver with a machine-learning-aided OPF workflow. It predicts bus voltages/angles, generator dispatch, and branch flows, then uses network equations to recover remaining variables, matching the need for fast repeated OPF solving with reduced computational burden.
evidence_package.main_risk_or_gap: 中文说明：它是单阶段随机森林+物理方程的混合框架，不是明确的多阶段物理结构神经网络；也未专门针对高可再生概率场景的主动约束识别分层学习。 / English explanation: It is a single-stage random-forest plus physics-equation hybrid, not an explicit multi-stage physics-structured neural framework. It also does not specifically implement active-constraint identification or staged learning for probabilistic high-renewable OPF.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Machine Learning-Aided Security Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Jubeyer Rahman; Cong Feng; Jie Zhang
data_properties.hasInstitution: The University of Texas at Dallas
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve security-constrained AC optimal power flow efficiently using a machine-learning-aided approach.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Full AC OPF is highly nonlinear and non-convex, making large-scale security-constrained solving computationally challenging.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained AC optimal power flow with switched shunt security constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a machine-learning-aided method predict key OPF variables and avoid running a physics-based OPF solver while preserving feasibility?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Bus voltage magnitudes and voltage angles; derived current injections, complex/real power injections, generator dispatch settings, and branch power flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid machine-learning-aided OPF using multi-input multi-output random forest plus physics-based network equations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with bus admittance matrix, current injection, apparent power, and nodal power balance.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period steady-state OPF.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Not specified; load samples from hourly ERCOT profile used for training/testing.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per case.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: No explicit uncertainty model; trained on sampled load cases.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC transmission OPF with generators, buses, branches, and switched shunts.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Multi-input multi-output random forest predicts voltages, then network equations recover remaining variables.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported zero constraint violation for the proposed method and much faster solution time than MATPOWER MIPS.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Load demand inputs Pd and Qd are used as predictors; no demand response model.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator costs represented by individual piece-wise linear cost functions.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Voltage magnitude and angle bounds; generator active/reactive power bounds; switched shunt susceptance bounds; real and reactive nodal power balance equations; branch apparent power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes vi and angles θi; generator outputs pg and qg; switched shunt susceptance bcs; real/reactive demands pd and qd; branch flow limit sf; bus admittance matrix Y; generator cost cg.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: RF is trained on converged MATPOWER solutions; case I predicts v and θ then computes injections and costs via network equations; case II predicts all OPF variables directly.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on a 500-bus GO competition network using 8,760 load samples; compared against MATPOWER MIPS and a pure ML baseline.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method closely matches MIPS voltage solutions, satisfies network constraints, and reduces total solution time from 2030.4 s to 35.26 s.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: fast and feasible OPF approximation without running a physics-based solver. Limitation: pure end-to-end ML still causes many equality-constraint violations.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Potentially useful for post-contingency analysis with many network topologies and load profiles.

data_properties.hasModelName: Neural Networks Encoding Dynamic Security Constrained AC OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Neural Networks for Encoding Dynamic Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Ilgiz Murzakhanov; Andreas Venzke; George S. Misyris; Spyros Chatzivasileiadis
data_properties.hasInstitution: Technical University of Denmark
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Encode dynamic security constraints into a tractable optimization model for AC optimal power flow.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Directly including dynamic security constraints makes AC-OPF intractable; the paper seeks a scalable alternative.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: AC optimal power flow with N-1 security and small-signal stability constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can neural networks encode the feasible space of dynamic security-constrained AC-OPF so it can be solved as a MILP?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Cost-optimal generator dispatch satisfying N-1 security and small-signal stability, with corresponding bus voltages and line flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Classification neural network encodes feasible operating points; exact mixed-integer reformulation with ReLU activations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow balance for the intact system; contingency-wise AC constraints for N-1 security.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single operating point; no multi-period horizon.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single snapshot dispatch.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: None explicit; random cost-function test instances only.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: N-1 security and small-signal stability constraints on an IEEE 14-bus system.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Neural-network feasibility encoding, exact MILP reformulation, and iterative linearization of power losses.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported 99% test accuracy; feasibility improved to 100% with epsilon adjustment.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost of the intact system state.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Generator active/reactive limits, voltage magnitude limits, line-flow limits, AC power balance, preventive generator set-point equality across contingencies, eigenvalue-based small-signal stability damping ratio constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator active and reactive limits, voltage limits, line-flow limits, contingency set C, damping threshold gamma_min, neural-network weights and biases, ReLU bounds, epsilon conservativeness parameter, loss-linearization threshold rho.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Train a ReLU classification network on feasible/infeasible operating points, reformulate it exactly as MILP, and iteratively linearize AC losses to solve MILPs with Gurobi.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 14-bus system with 45,000 labeled samples; 99% test accuracy; compared against AC-OPF and N-1 security-constrained AC-OPF.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach obtained cost-optimal solutions satisfying both static and dynamic security constraints; epsilon increased feasibility to 100% with small cost increase.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: tractable MILP approximation and improved feasibility. Limitations: approximation error may cause optimality loss and separate networks are needed for different grids.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses a conservative feasibility margin epsilon to trade off feasibility and optimality.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：高度一致，明确是物理信息驱动的数据驱动 OPF，并采用三阶段分解逐步学习支路潮流、电压、机组出力和目标值，还包含基于主动约束的样本预分类，几乎完整贴合需求。 / English explanation: Highly consistent. It is a physics-informed data-driven OPF model with explicit three-stage decomposition that progressively learns branch flows, voltages, generator outputs, and the objective value, and it also includes active-constraint-based sample pre-classification, matching the requirement very closely.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：主要缺口是更偏离线训练与样本覆盖，面对强分布外工况时实时泛化能力可能受限。 / English explanation: The main gap is reliance on offline training and sample coverage, so real-time generalization may weaken under strong out-of-distribution operating conditions.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：部分符合快速替代传统求解的目标，也能输出电压、相角、机组出力和支路潮流，但它是单阶段随机森林与物理方程混合框架，不是用户要求的物理结构神经网络多阶段学习框架。 / English explanation: It partially fits the goal of replacing traditional solvers quickly and can output voltages, angles, generator dispatch, and branch flows, but it is a single-stage random-forest plus physics-equation hybrid rather than the requested physics-structured neural multi-stage learning framework.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：缺少明确的多阶段分解、主动约束识别和面向高可再生概率场景的分层学习，因此与核心方法要求不一致。 / English explanation: It lacks explicit multi-stage decomposition, active constraint identification, and staged learning for probabilistic high-renewable scenarios, so it does not align with the core methodological requirement.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：它体现了物理信息约束学习的思想，但面向通用非线性 PDE，而不是 OPF；也没有体现支路潮流、电压、机组出力、目标值的分阶段学习或主动约束识别。 / English explanation: It captures the idea of physics-informed learning, but it is aimed at general nonlinear PDEs rather than OPF, and it does not implement staged learning of branch flows, voltages, generator outputs, objective values, or active constraint identification.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：与 OPF 专用、可替代迭代求解、以及多阶段物理结构学习这几个关键要求差距较大。 / English explanation: It falls short on the key requirements of being OPF-specific, replacing iterative solving, and using multi-stage physics-structured learning.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：总体符合物理信息驱动的 ACOPF 快速近似求解方向，能生成可行解并减少对传统迭代求解器的依赖，也输出电压、相角和机组出力。 / English explanation: Overall it fits the physics-informed ACOPF fast-approximation direction, can generate feasible solutions while reducing reliance on traditional iterative solvers, and outputs voltages, angles, and generator dispatch.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：它采用两阶段预测加可行性校准，而不是用户强调的多阶段逐步学习与主动约束预分类；此外，校准在部分大系统测试中并非总能收敛。 / English explanation: It uses two-stage prediction plus feasibility calibration rather than the requested multi-stage progressive learning and active-constraint pre-classification; additionally, calibration does not always converge on larger systems.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：它确实是面向 ACOPF 的数据驱动快速近似模型，也能显著加速推理，但主要是模仿学习的单阶段近似器，输出重点偏向机组有功出力。 / English explanation: It is indeed a data-driven fast approximation model for ACOPF and can greatly accelerate inference, but it is mainly a single-stage imitation-learning approximator with emphasis on generator active power outputs.

ranked_candidates.matched_needs: 物理结构嵌入 / physics-informed structure；三阶段逐步学习 branch flows、voltages、generator outputs、objective value / three-stage progressive learning of branch flows, voltages, generator outputs, and objective value；主动约束样本预分类 / active-constraint sample pre-classification；替代传统迭代 OPF / replacing iterative OPF；适合高可再生与概率场景下的大量重复求解 / suitable for repeated solves under renewable uncertainty and probabilistic scenarios.
ranked_candidates.strengths: 三阶段 SELM 回归把复杂 OPF 映射拆解为更易学习的子任务，降低训练难度并提升泛化效率；主动约束分区预分类有助于把相似工况聚类，减少样本混杂；输出覆盖发电机出力、电压、支路潮流和目标值，和用户需求高度一致。/ The three-stage SELM regression decomposes the complex OPF mapping into easier subproblems, reducing learning difficulty and improving efficiency; active-constraint region pre-classification clusters similar operating states and reduces sample ambiguity; outputs cover generator dispatch, voltages, branch flows, and objective value, closely matching the user's needs.
ranked_candidates.limitations: 主要技术边界在于依赖离线训练样本覆盖，面对强分布外工况或极端运行点时精度与可行性可能下降；作为近似求解器，它不提供传统优化器那种严格全局最优保证。/ Main technical boundary is dependence on offline training coverage, so accuracy and feasibility may degrade under strong out-of-distribution or extreme operating conditions; as an approximate solver, it does not provide the strict global-optimality guarantee of a classical optimizer.

requirement.requirement_text: I need a dispatch model that can be applied to both day-ahead OPF and real-time OPF, in order to handle rapid variations of wind power, solar power, and load within the scheduling period. Traditional DA-OPF is usually calculated based on a one-hour static snapshot, and RT-OPF is usually calculated based on a 5- to 15-minute static snapshot. However, between two consecutive scheduling points, wind power, solar power, and load continue to change, causing additional regulation costs and security risks. Re-optimizing at every shorter time scale would be accurate, but computationally too expensive. Therefore, a method based on “best-fit participation factors” is needed. It should optimize only once at the beginning of the scheduling period, while considering minute-level variations in RT-OPF and 15-minute-level variations in DA-OPF, and include voltage, reactive power, and line flow constraints in all sub-intervals, so that economy and system security can be improved without increasing the dimension of optimization variables.

prefilter_result.user_requirement: I need a dispatch model that can be applied to both day-ahead OPF and real-time OPF, in order to handle rapid variations of wind power, solar power, and load within the scheduling period. Traditional DA-OPF is usually calculated based on a one-hour static snapshot, and RT-OPF is usually calculated based on a 5- to 15-minute static snapshot. However, between two consecutive scheduling points, wind power, solar power, and load continue to change, causing additional regulation costs and security risks. Re-optimizing at every shorter time scale would be accurate, but computationally too expensive. Therefore, a method based on “best-fit participation factors” is needed. It should optimize only once at the beginning of the scheduling period, while considering minute-level variations in RT-OPF and 15-minute-level variations in DA-OPF, and include voltage, reactive power, and line flow constraints in all sub-intervals, so that economy and system security can be improved without increasing the dimension of optimization variables.

selected_candidates.why_matched: 直接针对日 ahead 与实时 OPF，并明确用一次优化和“best-fit”参与因子处理区间内风、光、负荷波动。/ Directly targets day-ahead and real-time OPF, and explicitly uses one optimization with “best-fit” participation factors to handle intra-interval wind, solar, and load variation.
selected_candidates.main_risk_or_gap: 主要是静态区间内近似，依赖预测与固定参与因子；对更复杂的多时段耦合或更强不确定性并非完整随机/鲁棒建模。/ Mainly an intra-interval approximation that depends on forecasts and fixed participation factors; it is not a full stochastic/robust multi-period formulation for stronger uncertainty or coupling.
supporting_evidence: hasPrimaryPurpose: "To schedule generation economically while maintaining security in day-ahead and real-time OPF with renewable variability."
hasModelFeature: "Single optimization with 'best-fit' participation factors over sub-interval variability."
hasTemporalResolution: "RT-OPF: 1 min sub-intervals within 10-min intervals; DA-OPF: 15 min sub-sub-intervals within 1 h intervals."

selected_candidates.why_matched: 中文说明：该模型直接对应多时段调度，明确包含“hourly day-ahead plus quarter-hour flexibility intervals”，并输出 day-ahead dispatch 与 flexibility market dispatch，适合在一次优化中覆盖 DA-OPF 与更细时间尺度的运行变化。/ English explanation: This model directly targets multi-period scheduling, explicitly includes hourly day-ahead plus quarter-hour flexibility intervals, and produces day-ahead dispatch and flexibility market dispatch, fitting a single optimization over DA-OPF and finer operating intervals.
selected_candidates.main_risk_or_gap: 中文说明：它强调灵活性市场与 TSO-DSO 协调，而不是专门用 best-fit participation factors 来处理分钟级 RT-OPF 变化；且文中指出 reactive power flexibility 仍未纳入。/ English explanation: It focuses on flexibility market clearing and TSO-DSO coordination rather than specifically using best-fit participation factors for minute-level RT-OPF variation; reactive power flexibility is also not yet included.
supporting_evidence: "hourly day-ahead plus quarter-hour flexibility intervals"
"Optimal day-ahead dispatch and flexibility market dispatch"
"reactive power flexibility not yet included"

selected_candidates.why_matched: 中文说明：该模型直接面向多时间步安全约束 OPF，包含 AC 潮流、爬坡、备用与时序耦合，最接近“在调度周期内一次优化、覆盖多个子间隔”的需求。/ English explanation: This model directly targets multi-step security-constrained OPF with AC power flow, ramping, reserves, and temporal coupling, closely matching the need to optimize once over a scheduling period while covering multiple sub-intervals.
selected_candidates.main_risk_or_gap: 中文说明：它强调多步 SCOPF 与安全约束，但没有明确“best-fit participation factors”式的单次起始优化机制，也未专门说明分钟级 RT 与 15 分钟级 DA 两种分辨率的统一处理。/ English explanation: It emphasizes multi-step SCOPF and security constraints, but does not explicitly describe a best-fit participation-factor mechanism or a unified treatment of minute-level RT and 15-minute DA resolutions.

hasTimeHorizonFeature: Multiple time steps; sequential stage-wise optimization for large horizons.

usesParameter: ParticipationFactorParameter; TimePeriodParameter; ScenarioSetParameter; UncertaintySetParameter.

hasTimeHorizonFeature: Sequential multi-step dispatch with future load forecasts and ramping-coupled time dependence.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Day-Ahead and Real Time Optimal Power Flow considering Renewable Energy Resources
data_properties.hasAuthor: S. Surender Reddy; P.R. Bijwe
data_properties.hasInstitution: Woosong University; Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To schedule generation economically while maintaining security in day-ahead and real-time OPF with renewable variability.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Conventional DA-OPF and RT-OPF use static snapshots and ignore renewable/load variability within scheduling intervals.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Optimal power flow for thermal-wind-solar systems with renewable variability, voltage, reactive power, line-flow, and ramp constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can participation factors evaluated once at the start of each interval capture intra-interval renewable variability without increasing optimization dimensionality?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generator dispatch schedules, renewable generation schedules, interval costs/profits, and voltage stability index values.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Single optimization with 'best-fit' participation factors over sub-interval variability.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with voltage magnitude/angle, reactive power, and line-flow constraints.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Day-ahead and real-time multi-interval scheduling with 15-min and 1-min sub-intervals.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: RT-OPF: 1 min sub-intervals within 10-min intervals; DA-OPF: 15 min sub-sub-intervals within 1 h intervals.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: RT-OPF over 60 min; DA-OPF over 24 h.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses forecasted solar, wind, and load variability within intervals; no explicit stochastic or robust formulation.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Thermal generators with wind and solar PV injections, AGC participation factors, ramp limits, and voltage stability index.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Evaluates 'best-fit' participation factors once to avoid separate optimization for every sub-interval.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported lower total cost and improved voltage stability versus conventional interval-by-interval OPF.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Forecasted load demand varies within sub-intervals and is included in imbalance calculations.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost over RT sub-intervals; maximize total profit over DA intervals as revenue minus generation cost.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Active and reactive nodal power balance, generator output limits with ramp-up/down limits, renewable output caps, bus-voltage limits, line-flow limits, and demand-supply balance constraint in DA-OPF.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients; energy price; wind and solar direct cost coefficients; bus admittance Gij/Bij; ramp limits; voltage and line-flow limits; forecasted load, wind, and solar outputs; participation factors.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: MATLAB Optimization Toolbox FMINCON was used on the IEEE 30-bus system with wind at bus 11 and solar PV at bus 13.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Compared conventional and proposed RT-OPF/DA-OPF on IEEE 30-bus test system using 60-min RT and 24-h DA schedules.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed approach reduced RT total cost and increased DA profit while keeping optimization size unchanged and improving voltage stability.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: captures intra-interval variability with little added computational burden. Limitation: relies on forecast availability and fixed participation factors within each interval.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Voltage stability was assessed using the L-index/VSEI.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Model flexibility market clearing and TSO-DSO coordination using a hybrid AC/DC optimal power flow formulation.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Need to unlock consumer-side flexibility and coordinate DSO and TSO operations to address congestion, voltage, and balancing challenges.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Seamless coordination of transmission and distribution grid operation in a local flexibility market with multi-period flexibility procurement.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a multi-period hybrid AC/DC-OPF model accurately clear flexibility and coordinate TSO-DSO actions across transmission and distribution grids?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal day-ahead dispatch and flexibility market dispatch, including generation, flexible load, battery charging/discharging, load shedding, bus voltages, and line power flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid SOC-ACOPF for distribution grid and DC-OPF for transmission grid; multi-period formulation; AC-DC connection constraint.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: SOC-ACOPF for distribution; DC-OPF for transmission; convex relaxation with auxiliary variables.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Multi-period; hourly day-ahead plus quarter-hour flexibility intervals; rolling horizon in operation.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: 24 hours with quarter-hour subperiods.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Scenario-based planning mentioned, but probabilistic scenarios are not developed in this paper.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: TSO-DSO coordination in a local flexibility market with transmission and radial distribution grids.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Pyomo implementation solved with Gurobi; two-stage optimization for day-ahead and flexibility market clearing.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Validated on standard test grids; reported high accuracy and applicability; compared with standalone AC and DC OPF.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Flexible loads, load shifting, load shedding, distributed generation, and batteries.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total operating cost of transmission and distribution generation, flexibility activation, battery operation, and load shedding across all periods.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: SOC-ACOPF power balance and conic relaxation constraints; AC-DC coupling constraint; DC power balance, line flow limits, slack angle; flexible generation/load bounds; zero-net load shifting; battery SoC, charge/discharge, and terminal SoC constraints; load shedding equals served load.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generation cost coefficients, flexibility prices, battery cost, load-shedding cost, network susceptance matrices, active/reactive load limits, generation limits, line flow limits, slack angle, battery SoC bounds, charge/discharge limits, efficiencies, and initial SoC.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Implemented in Python with Pyomo and solved using Gurobi on a 33-bus distribution grid and 9-bus transmission grid test case.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated against standalone SOC-ACOPF and DC-OPF results and tested on flexibility, voltage, and congestion cases.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: Flexibility reduced costs, improved voltages, lowered imported transmission power and distribution losses, and could also relieve transmission congestion.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: unified multi-period TSO-DSO coordination and flexibility clearing. Limitation: single-optimization formulation may become computationally heavy for multiple DSOs; reactive power flexibility not yet included.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Future work extends the model with ADMM for multiple DSOs and reactive power flexibility exchange.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve large-scale security-constrained optimal power flow with multiple time steps efficiently under strict time limits.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Large SCOPF instances contain millions of continuous/integer variables and nonlinear nonconvex constraints, making them difficult to solve within challenge time limits.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained optimal power flow with multiple time steps, including AC power flow, contingencies, reserves, device switching, and ramping constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a decomposition-based hybrid solver scale multi-timestep SCOPF to very large grids while maintaining high-quality feasible solutions?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generation and consumption dispatch, device switching status, bus voltage angles, AC power-flow feasible operating point, and reserve allocations.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Two-stage DC/AC decomposition with sequential optimization for large networks.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: DC module uses linearized/MILP approximations; AC module solves full nonlinear AC power-flow equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Multiple time steps; sequential stage-wise optimization for large horizons.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Time-step based control horizon; exact interval length not specified.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Control horizon divided into stages for networks over 2000 buses.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Contingency constraints included; no stochastic or robust uncertainty model stated.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC OPF with reserves, ramping, device uptime/downtime, and switching constraints.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Problem reformulation, McCormick relaxation, slack variables, clique constraints, analytical derivatives, vectorization, and sequential bound updates.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Designed for scalability and strict time limits on very large instances.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Consumption devices represented with bid blocks and power consumption bounds.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Maximize total market surplus z over device powers, bus voltage angles, and switching variables.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Equality constraints G enforce power-balance and AC/DC network equations; inequality constraints H cover voltage limits, real/reactive power limits, reserves, ramping, switching, contingency, and device operation constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Device power pjt, bus voltage angle θit, switching status ujt, shunt conductance gshjt, branch flow limits smaxj, reserve factors σscrn, ramp-up Pru, ramp-down Prd, and mismatch penalty pit.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: DC subproblem solved as MILP with Gurobi; AC subproblem solved as NLP with IPOPT; large cases use sequential stage-wise optimization and selective contingency inclusion.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Evaluated on 300+ scenarios across 73 to 8316-bus networks from ARPA-E GO challenge datasets.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach achieved high scaled scores in most scenarios, with average scores around 0.983 on Scenario Set 3 and 0.9992 on Scenario Set 2, while meeting time limits.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalable, robust, high-quality solutions, full AC formulation. Limitation: solution quality varies by scenario and depends on available reserve abundance; large cases require sequential decomposition.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Applied to ARPA-E Grid Optimization Challenge 3 datasets and testing platform.

data_properties.hasMotivation: Classical OPF dispatch is rigid and can become inefficient or infeasible under renewable and load uncertainty, causing overloads and outages.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Robust and chance-constrained AC optimal power flow with uncertain loads and renewable generators.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How can AC-OPF be solved efficiently under uncertainty while limiting the probability of violating generation and transmission constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal controllable generation dispatch, generator voltage magnitudes, deployment vector, and corresponding bus voltage and line-flow-feasible operating point.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Scenario-with-certificates formulation combined with convex SDP relaxation of AC power flow.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power balance equations with voltage-magnitude and line-flow constraints via lifted matrix W.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period OPF repeated over hourly demand scenarios in experiments.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per solve; 24 hourly solves in simulation.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Probabilistic uncertainty in loads and renewable generation using scenario with certificates and chance constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Includes renewable generators, uncertain loads, generator participation factors, voltage limits, and transmission limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Convex relaxation plus randomized scenario-with-certificates sampling.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: A priori probabilistic guarantee on constraint-violation risk; exact for a restricted class of networks.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uncertain loads are explicitly modeled and balanced through generator deployment factors.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost f(u); in the penalized variant, worst-case cost adds reactive-power and line-loss penalties.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power balance equalities; generator active/reactive limits; voltage magnitude bounds; line-voltage-difference or apparent-flow limits; deployment factors sum to one and remain nonnegative.
data_properties.usesParameter: Uncertain complex load and renewable deviations δ; deployment vector α; bus-voltage matrix W split into Wu and Wx; risk levels ε and β; line admittances ylm; voltage and power limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Uses SDP lifting W=VV* and scenario-with-certificates sampling to solve a convex program; implemented with YALMIP and Mosek.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on the New England 39-bus system with Monte Carlo testing over 10,000 samples and comparison against nominal OPF and a prior probabilistic AC-OPF method.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method greatly reduced infeasible samples and line-flow violations versus nominal OPF, while using far fewer scenario samples than the compared parameterized approach.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: less conservative, probabilistic guarantees, computationally efficient, and exact for some networks. Limitation: exactness is only proven for a restrictive network class.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Can incorporate N-1 security constraints and outage probabilities within the same scenario framework.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve sequential real-time security-constrained optimal power flow with fast dispatch decisions under inaccurate environmental parameters.
data_properties.hasMotivation: ACOPF is nonconvex, time-coupled by ramping limits, and difficult to solve quickly and safely when system parameters are inaccurate or contingencies are unexperienced.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Sequential security-constrained AC optimal power flow for real-time operation with generator active/reactive dispatch and network security limits.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a hybrid knowledge-data-driven reinforcement learning method produce safe real-time OPF dispatches efficiently without relying on accurate environmental models?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Safe generator active and reactive power dispatch commands; resulting bus voltage magnitudes and branch active/reactive power flows within limits.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid knowledge-data-driven reinforcement learning with a safety-layer projection model and inactive-constraint identification.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow formulation with nonlinear nodal injections, branch flows, voltage magnitudes, and ramping-coupled generator limits.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Sequential multi-step dispatch with future load forecasts and ramping-coupled time dependence.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Real-time operation over time slots; forecasting horizon T steps.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Infinite-horizon sequential decision process terminated by grid failure/non-convergence.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses reinforcement learning for inaccurate environments and updates safety-layer parameters from latest measurements.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained ACOPF with coordinated active and reactive power dispatch, voltage and branch-flow security limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Improved SAC with SAM, prioritized replay, adaptive entropy, hybrid safety layer, and inactive-constraint elimination.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Claims faster decision-making and reduced security violations with comparable economic performance.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Includes forecasted net load demand in the state; no explicit demand response control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize cumulative generation operating cost, with quadratic cost coefficients for each generator over time.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power-balance equations, branch active/reactive flow equations, generator active/reactive limits, branch flow limits, voltage magnitude limits, and ramping-coupled generator bounds; safety-layer projection also enforces linearized security constraints and power balance.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients; generator active/reactive bounds and ramping limits; bus voltages; line conductance/susceptance or resistance/reactance; branch flow limits; load demand and forecasted load; slack-bus limits; penalty coefficients; SAC temperature and learning rates.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Sequential decisions are produced by an improved soft actor-critic policy, then projected by a linear security layer initialized from linearized power-flow knowledge and updated with data; inactive constraints are removed analytically.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 30-bus and larger systems, including contingency and parameter-error scenarios, with comparisons against penalty, constrained-policy, and pure data-driven safety-layer baselines.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The method maintains voltages and branch flows within safe ranges, reduces violation times in early training and contingencies, and scales to larger systems with low decision time.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: safe real-time dispatch, better robustness to inaccurate models, and high computational efficiency. Limitation: safety layer uses linearized power-flow approximation and may need conservative limits to offset approximation error.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper also evaluates scalability on 9-, 30-, 57-, 118-, and 1187-bus systems.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Review and compare online optimization techniques for power-system operation under high renewable penetration.

data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Which online optimization paradigms are most suitable for different power-system time scales and operational settings?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Not applicable; this is a review paper rather than a solved OPF model.

data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Covers single-period and multi-period formulations, plus fast dynamic-control time scales.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Seconds to minutes for dynamic control; single-period and multi-period decision settings.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single-period and multi-period; some Lyapunov examples use finite or infinite horizons.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Addresses renewable variability and uncertainty through online decision-making without relying on forecasts or historical distributions.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Frequency control, voltage regulation, OPF, economic dispatch, energy storage scheduling, demand response, and power markets.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Compares feedback-based, primal-dual, ADMM, Newton-Raphson, Lyapunov, and OCO methods; discusses distributed and asynchronous variants.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Emphasizes fast response, tracking of time-varying conditions, and reduced computational burden.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Includes controllable loads, demand response, electric vehicles, and load-side frequency control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Examples include minimizing generation cost in OPF, regulation cost in frequency control, and long-term average cost in Lyapunov/OCO formulations.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Power-flow equations, voltage limits, generation and reactive-power bounds, power-balance constraints, line congestion, storage SoC and charging/discharging limits, ramping and other coupled constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generation cost coefficients ai, bi; voltage bounds vi; power injection bounds Pi, Qi; line parameters rij, xij, Bij; storage queue/SoC Qt; Lyapunov weight ρ; stepsize η; control gains.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: The paper reviews algorithmic frameworks and representative formulations; it does not present a single new solved OPF instance.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: No dedicated validation of a new OPF model; cites prior experimental and numerical studies in the reviewed literature.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: Online optimization is useful for volatile power systems because it can track changing conditions and avoid reliance on inaccurate forecasts.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: fast, measurement-driven, and suitable for time-varying systems. Limitations: problem-dependent, often lacks a unified theory, and some methods need communication or predictions.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper is a survey and taxonomy of online optimization methods in power systems.

top_rows.Requirement text: I need a dispatch model that can be applied to both day-ahead OPF and real-time OPF, in order to handle rapid variations of wind power, solar power, and load within the scheduling period. Traditional DA-OPF is usually calculated based on a one-hour static snapshot, and RT-OPF is usually calculated based on a 5- to 15-minute static snapshot. However, between two consecutive scheduling points, wind power, solar power, and load continue to change, causing additional regulation costs and security risks. Re-optimizing at every shorter time scale would be accurate, but computationally too expensive. Therefore, a method based on “best-fit participation factors” is needed. It should optimize only once at the beginning of the scheduling period, while considering minute-level variations in RT-OPF and 15-minute-level variations in DA-OPF, and include voltage, reactive power, and line flow constraints in all sub-intervals, so that economy and system security can be improved without increasing the dimension of optimization variables.

requirement.requirement_text: I need a distributed OPF model for multi-terminal DC distribution grids, used for system-level control and active network management. With large-scale integration of power electronic converters and distributed energy resources, MTDC distribution grids need to update DC voltage setpoints and DER power setpoints at different nodes within short control periods. Different types of DERs have different dispatch objectives: conventional DERs are dispatched according to cost, RES needs to consider curtailment minimization, ESS needs to consider SoC, and controllable loads need to consider curtailment cost. Centralized OPF is not modular enough and has scalability, reliability, and data privacy issues. Therefore, a distributed OPF-for-ANM algorithm based on nodal formulation and ADMM is needed, so that each distributed control unit can use only local information and necessary communication to coordinate RES, ESS, controllable loads, and other DERs, and quickly and scalably realize system-level voltage and power control.

data_properties.hasModelName: Distributed System Level Control MTDC Grids
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Distributed OPF Algorithm for System-Level Control of Active Multi-Terminal DC Distribution Grids
data_properties.hasAuthor: Asimenia Korompili; Petros Pandis; Antonello Monti
data_properties.hasInstitution: Institute for Automation of Complex Power Systems, E.ON Energy Research Center, RWTH Aachen University, Aachen, Germany
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Distributed OPF-based system-level control of MTDC distribution grids with DER coordination.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Need fast, scalable, modular, privacy-preserving control for MTDC grids with high DER integration and changing operating conditions.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Distributed solution of a nodal OPF-for-ANM problem for MTDC grids using ADMM and sequential convex approximation.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a distributed OPF algorithm coordinate diverse DER and provide nodal voltage set-points fast enough for system-level control in MTDC grids?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal nodal voltage set-points and DER power dispatch set-points; in simulations, nodal voltages and conventional DER power outputs are reported.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Distributed, modular nodal formulation with ADMM coordination and local convexified subproblems.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Nodal DC power-flow formulation with current, power-flow, and voltage variables; nonlinear power equations linearized by first-order Taylor approximation.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Repeated at each control period.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single-period, receding control-period optimization.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses measured available RES power and current ESS SoC; no explicit stochastic or robust uncertainty model.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Multi-terminal DC distribution grids with DER, ESS, controllable loads, and interlinking converters.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: ADMM with sequential convex approximation and an added initialization step for time-varying DER parameters.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Evaluated for convergence speed, parallel computation time, communication time, scalability, and online cluster execution.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Controllable loads can curtail demand with quadratic curtailment costs and bounds.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize conventional DER operating costs plus ADMM consensus penalty terms; ANM schemes add RES priority terms, ESS virtual-cost terms, or load-curtailment cost terms.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Nodal current, line-current, nodal power balance, nonlinear power-flow equalities, and bounds on generation, line flows, voltages, ESS energy, ESS charge/discharge exclusivity, and load curtailment.
data_properties.usesParameter: Penalty parameter ρ; voltage and power tolerances εV and εP; RES availability p̄RES; ESS SoC EESS,Ti and thresholds; charging/discharging efficiencies nch, ndisch; nodal price prk; load-curtailment factors aCL, bCL, cCL; priority factors priorRES and priorESS.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Each DCU solves its local nodal subproblem, exchanges voltage copies with neighbors, updates consensus voltages and dual variables, and stops when voltage convergence and total power balance are satisfied.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on modified IEEE 14, 30, 57, and 118-node systems, including sequential and physically distributed HPC-cluster implementations.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The algorithm converges in a few hundred iterations, remains scalable across network sizes, and can dispatch diverse DER under different ANM schemes with acceptable voltage deviations from centralized solutions.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: distributed, modular, scalable, privacy-preserving, fast. Limitations: relies on linearized OPF, assumes normal communication operation, and communication time can dominate total execution time.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Suitable for system-level control of DER-dominated MTDC grids and adaptable to equivalent AC-grid OPF-for-ANM formulations.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Estimating Global Variables in Multi-agent Distributed OPF with Unreliable Communication
data_properties.hasAuthor: Masoud Bashari; Mikhak Samadi; Javad Zare; Ashkan Rahimi-Kian
data_properties.hasInstitution: IEMS Group Ltd.; University of Ottawa
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve distributed optimal power flow under unreliable communication by estimating exchanged global variables.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Communication link disruptions can prevent consensus exchange in distributed OPF and degrade convergence and feasibility.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Distributed OPF across multiple regions with lost or interrupted communication links between agents.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can predictive estimation of missing consensus messages preserve feasible D-OPF convergence when communication is interrupted?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Regional bus voltage magnitudes and phase angles, weighted-average global bus voltages, and convergence of D-OPF results across iterations.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Multi-agent distributed OPF with coordinator-agent consensus and predictive estimation of missing exchanged variables.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Region-based OPF coupled through tie-line voltage consensus and line power-flow equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Iterative multi-region consensus over repeated ADMM iterations.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Handles unreliable communication by estimating missing consensus messages with a trained DFNN.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: IEEE 14-bus transmission network partitioned into three regions with PV units and a BESS.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Extended ADMM combined with a shallow feedforward neural-network estimator for missing messages.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Faster convergence to actual global variables and feasible D-OPF results under interrupted links.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost for each region/sub-network.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Regional OPF constraints are enforced through bus-voltage and tie-line coupling; line power flows are updated from estimated voltages and consensus variables.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes and phase angles, tie-line voltages, line impedances, line currents, regional loads S_i,j^t, PV units, and BESS size.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: IEEE 14-bus case split into three areas; ADMM iterations compute regional OPF, estimate missing voltages with DFNN, average exchanged voltages, and update line flows.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Compared three scenarios: normal communication, lost bus-5 communication, and lost communication recovered by estimation; tested on IEEE 14-bus case.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: With DFNN-based estimation, interrupted-link cases converged closer to global voltages and faster than the unrecovered communication-loss case.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: improves distributed OPF feasibility and convergence under communication loss. Limitation: estimator still shows biased error and needs more training data.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: ANN/DFNN estimator trained on OPF data generated from 90%–100% loading scenarios.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve large-scale security-constrained optimal power flow with multiple time steps efficiently under strict time limits.

data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained optimal power flow with multiple time steps, including AC power flow, contingencies, reserves, device switching, and ramping constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a decomposition-based hybrid solver scale multi-timestep SCOPF to very large grids while maintaining high-quality feasible solutions?

data_properties.hasModelFeature: Two-stage DC/AC decomposition with sequential optimization for large networks.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: DC module uses linearized/MILP approximations; AC module solves full nonlinear AC power-flow equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Multiple time steps; sequential stage-wise optimization for large horizons.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Time-step based control horizon; exact interval length not specified.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Control horizon divided into stages for networks over 2000 buses.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Contingency constraints included; no stochastic or robust uncertainty model stated.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC OPF with reserves, ramping, device uptime/downtime, and switching constraints.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Problem reformulation, McCormick relaxation, slack variables, clique constraints, analytical derivatives, vectorization, and sequential bound updates.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Designed for scalability and strict time limits on very large instances.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Consumption devices represented with bid blocks and power consumption bounds.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Maximize total market surplus z over device powers, bus voltage angles, and switching variables.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Equality constraints G enforce power-balance and AC/DC network equations; inequality constraints H cover voltage limits, real/reactive power limits, reserves, ramping, switching, contingency, and device operation constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Device power pjt, bus voltage angle θit, switching status ujt, shunt conductance gshjt, branch flow limits smaxj, reserve factors σscrn, ramp-up Pru, ramp-down Prd, and mismatch penalty pit.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: DC subproblem solved as MILP with Gurobi; AC subproblem solved as NLP with IPOPT; large cases use sequential stage-wise optimization and selective contingency inclusion.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Evaluated on 300+ scenarios across 73 to 8316-bus networks from ARPA-E GO challenge datasets.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach achieved high scaled scores in most scenarios, with average scores around 0.983 on Scenario Set 3 and 0.9992 on Scenario Set 2, while meeting time limits.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalable, robust, high-quality solutions, full AC formulation. Limitation: solution quality varies by scenario and depends on available reserve abundance; large cases require sequential decomposition.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Applied to ARPA-E Grid Optimization Challenge 3 datasets and testing platform.
