data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve sequential real-time security-constrained optimal power flow with fast dispatch decisions under inaccurate environmental parameters.
data_properties.hasMotivation: ACOPF is nonconvex, time-coupled by ramping limits, and difficult to solve quickly and safely when system parameters are inaccurate or contingencies are unexperienced.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Sequential security-constrained AC optimal power flow for real-time operation with generator active/reactive dispatch and network security limits.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a hybrid knowledge-data-driven reinforcement learning method produce safe real-time OPF dispatches efficiently without relying on accurate environmental models?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Safe generator active and reactive power dispatch commands; resulting bus voltage magnitudes and branch active/reactive power flows within limits.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid knowledge-data-driven reinforcement learning with a safety-layer projection model and inactive-constraint identification.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow formulation with nonlinear nodal injections, branch flows, voltage magnitudes, and ramping-coupled generator limits.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Sequential multi-step dispatch with future load forecasts and ramping-coupled time dependence.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Real-time operation over time slots; forecasting horizon T steps.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Infinite-horizon sequential decision process terminated by grid failure/non-convergence.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses reinforcement learning for inaccurate environments and updates safety-layer parameters from latest measurements.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained ACOPF with coordinated active and reactive power dispatch, voltage and branch-flow security limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Improved SAC with SAM, prioritized replay, adaptive entropy, hybrid safety layer, and inactive-constraint elimination.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Claims faster decision-making and reduced security violations with comparable economic performance.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Includes forecasted net load demand in the state; no explicit demand response control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize cumulative generation operating cost, with quadratic cost coefficients for each generator over time.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power-balance equations, branch active/reactive flow equations, generator active/reactive limits, branch flow limits, voltage magnitude limits, and ramping-coupled generator bounds; safety-layer projection also enforces linearized security constraints and power balance.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients; generator active/reactive bounds and ramping limits; bus voltages; line conductance/susceptance or resistance/reactance; branch flow limits; load demand and forecasted load; slack-bus limits; penalty coefficients; SAC temperature and learning rates.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Sequential decisions are produced by an improved soft actor-critic policy, then projected by a linear security layer initialized from linearized power-flow knowledge and updated with data; inactive constraints are removed analytically.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 30-bus and larger systems, including contingency and parameter-error scenarios, with comparisons against penalty, constrained-policy, and pure data-driven safety-layer baselines.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The method maintains voltages and branch flows within safe ranges, reduces violation times in early training and contingencies, and scales to larger systems with low decision time.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: safe real-time dispatch, better robustness to inaccurate models, and high computational efficiency. Limitation: safety layer uses linearized power-flow approximation and may need conservative limits to offset approximation error.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper also evaluates scalability on 9-, 30-, 57-, 118-, and 1187-bus systems.

data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total cost including generation cost, load shedding cost, and wind/solar curtailment cost; minimize voltage deviation; maximize DR revenue, peak reduction, and user convenience.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Thermal unit active/reactive limits and ramping; load shedding bounds; ESS and EV charge/discharge and energy limits; wind/solar availability and curtailment; AC power balance and line flow limits; DR bounds and constant power-factor load shifting; HVAC temperature dynamics and comfort bounds.
data_properties.usesParameter: Fuel-cost coefficients bg,cg; VOLL, VOLW, VOLS; generator limits Pg/Qg and ramp rates; line susceptance b and impedance Zij; load baselines PL0, QL0; DR factor α; ESS/EV efficiencies and capacities; renewable availabilities wt, st; HVAC thermal coefficients k1–k4; temperature limits; LMP λ.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Formulated in GAMS as a mixed-integer nonlinear program and solved with CONOPT3; scenario results were weighted by probabilities and ranked with TOPSIS.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 24-bus and 118-bus systems using 12 renewable scenarios and DR steps from 0% to 25%.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: At 20% DR, the model achieved the best TOPSIS outcome, reducing total cost and peak demand while keeping voltages within limits.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: integrates AC OPF, DR, EV/HVAC aggregators, storage, and uncertainty. Limitation: aggregator placement was assumed, not optimized.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses both active and reactive demand response with user-convenience and comfort-aware flexible-load scheduling.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：与需求高度一致，明确面向多端直流配电网的系统级控制与主动网络管理，采用节点式分布式OPF和ADMM协调，并支持RES、ESS、可控负荷等多类DER的分层调度目标。 / English: Highly consistent with the requirement; it explicitly targets system-level control and active network management for MTDC distribution grids, uses nodal distributed OPF with ADMM coordination, and supports differentiated dispatch objectives for RES, ESS, and controllable loads.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：主要限制是采用线性化/顺序凸近似的DC潮流，精度上不如完整非线性模型，但这不构成与需求的根本冲突。 / English: Main limitation is the linearized/sequential convex DC power-flow approximation, which reduces fidelity versus a full nonlinear model, but this does not fundamentally conflict with the requirement.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：具备分布式OPF与ADMM协同、局部信息交换和通信受损下的协调能力，方向上相关；但其核心场景是分区输电网与通信丢包恢复，输出也主要是母线电压与相角，不是面向MTDC配电网的节点式DC电压设定与RES/ESS/可控负荷细粒度调度。 / English: It has distributed OPF with ADMM coordination, local information exchange, and resilience to communication loss, so it is directionally relevant; however, its core setting is partitioned transmission networks with communication-loss recovery, and its outputs are mainly bus voltages and angles rather than nodal DC-voltage setpoints and fine-grained RES/ESS/controllable-load dispatch for MTDC distribution grids.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：缺少对MTDC配电网、DC电压设定值更新以及多类DER按各自目标进行节点级协调的直接支持，因此与用户的关键应用场景不够贴合。 / English: It lacks direct support for MTDC distribution grids, DC-voltage setpoint updates, and node-level coordination of heterogeneous DERs under their respective objectives, so it does not fit the key application scenario closely enough.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它包含混合AC/DC网络、多时段协调、储能和柔性负荷，具有一定相关性；但当前实现是TSO-DSO灵活性市场清算的集中式模型，不是面向MTDC配电网的分布式节点式OPF，也没有明确的ADMM局部通信协调框架。 / English: It includes hybrid AC/DC networks, multi-period coordination, storage, and flexible loads, so it is somewhat related; however, the implemented model is a centralized TSO-DSO flexibility market clearing formulation, not a distributed nodal OPF for MTDC distribution grids, and it does not provide an explicit ADMM-based local communication coordination framework.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：还明确缺少无功灵活性，且与用户要求的短控制周期下更新DC电压与DER设定值的系统级控制目标不够直接。 / English: It also explicitly lacks reactive-power flexibility and is not directly aligned with the user’s short-control-period objective of updating DC-voltage and DER setpoints for system-level control.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：该模型强调大规模、多时段、安全约束OPF的可扩展求解，适合系统级调度，但其重点是集中式安全约束与分解加速，不是MTDC配电网的节点式分布式OPF，也没有ADMM协调或针对RES、ESS、可控负荷的差异化ANM控制。 / English: This model emphasizes scalable solution of large-scale multi-step security-constrained OPF and is suitable for system-level scheduling, but its focus is centralized security-constrained decomposition acceleration rather than nodal distributed OPF for MTDC distribution grids, and it lacks ADMM coordination or differentiated ANM control for RES, ESS, and controllable loads.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：与用户要求的MTDC配电网、分布式节点协同、短周期电压/功率控制之间存在明显场景偏离。 / English: There is a clear scenario mismatch with the requested MTDC distribution-grid setting, distributed nodal coordination, and short-period voltage/power control.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它确实覆盖VSC-MTDC混合AC/DC网络和可再生能源，网络形态相关；但它是单时段、集中式、启发式求解的OPF，不是基于节点式分布式ADMM的ANM算法，也没有明确的ESS、可控负荷和局部通信协调机制。 / English: It does cover VSC-MTDC hybrid AC/DC networks and renewables, so the network form is relevant; however, it is a single-period, centralized, heuristic-solved OPF rather than a nodal distributed ADMM-based ANM algorithm, and it lacks explicit ESS, controllable loads, and local communication coordination.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：缺少用户要求的分布式控制结构、短控制周期更新机制以及多类DER按不同目标协同调度。 / English: It misses the required distributed control structure, short-control-period update mechanism, and coordinated dispatch of heterogeneous DERs under different objectives.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它强调实时、安全约束和快速决策，具备运行控制相关性；但方法是强化学习驱动的集中式序列OPF，不是节点式分布式OPF，也没有ADMM通信协调，更不是专门针对MTDC配电网和多类DER差异化调度目标设计。 / English: It emphasizes real-time, security-constrained, fast decision-making and is relevant to operational control; however, the method is a reinforcement-learning-driven centralized sequential OPF, not a nodal distributed OPF, with no ADMM communication coordination, and it is not specifically designed for MTDC distribution grids or differentiated dispatch objectives across DER types.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：与用户要求的MTDC配电网分布式ANM框架、局部信息协同和DC电压/DER设定值快速更新不匹配。 / English: It does not match the requested distributed ANM framework for MTDC distribution grids, local-information coordination, or fast updating of DC-voltage and DER setpoints.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它覆盖AC OPF、储能、可再生能源和柔性负荷协调，且考虑短期调度与用户便利性，和主动网络管理有部分交集；但它是集中式MINLP日内/24小时调度，不是分布式ADMM节点式OPF，也不是面向MTDC配电网的DC电压与DER设定值快速协调。 / English: It covers AC OPF, storage, renewables, and flexible-load coordination with short-term scheduling and user convenience, so it partially overlaps with active network management; however, it is a centralized MINLP day-ahead/24-hour schedule, not a distributed ADMM nodal OPF, and it is not aimed at fast coordination of DC-voltage and DER setpoints in MTDC distribution grids.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：时间尺度偏长、控制结构偏集中，且没有针对MTDC配电网的节点级分布式通信与协调机制。 / English: Its time scale is too long and its control structure too centralized, with no node-level distributed communication and coordination mechanism for MTDC distribution grids.

raw_consistency.overall_summary: 中文：只有“Distributed_System_Level_Control_MTDC_Grids”与用户需求高度一致，适合作为后续详细重排序候选；其余候选都在网络类型、分布式ADMM结构、MTDC配电场景、短控制周期，或多类DER差异化调度目标方面存在明显偏离。 / English: Only “Distributed_System_Level_Control_MTDC_Grids” is highly consistent with the user requirement and is suitable for detailed reranking; the other candidates show clear mismatches in network type, distributed ADMM structure, MTDC distribution setting, short control periods, or differentiated dispatch objectives for heterogeneous DERs.

top_rows.Requirement text: I need a distributed OPF model for multi-terminal DC distribution grids, used for system-level control and active network management. With large-scale integration of power electronic converters and distributed energy resources, MTDC distribution grids need to update DC voltage setpoints and DER power setpoints at different nodes within short control periods. Different types of DERs have different dispatch objectives: conventional DERs are dispatched according to cost, RES needs to consider curtailment minimization, ESS needs to consider SoC, and controllable loads need to consider curtailment cost. Centralized OPF is not modular enough and has scalability, reliability, and data privacy issues. Therefore, a distributed OPF-for-ANM algorithm based on nodal formulation and ADMM is needed, so that each distributed control unit can use only local information and necessary communication to coordinate RES, ESS, controllable loads, and other DERs, and quickly and scalably realize system-level voltage and power control.

requirement.requirement_text: I need an optimization model suitable for distribution system DOPF that can accurately handle discrete control devices such as load tap changers (LTCs). In real distribution grids, LTCs and capacitor banks can only operate in discrete tap positions or states, rather than being continuously adjusted. However, many DOPF models relax integer variables into continuous variables to reduce computational difficulty, and then round the results to obtain tap positions. This approach may lead to infeasible or suboptimal solutions when the system operates close to its limits. With the integration of distributed PV, electric vehicles, storage, and advanced inverters, distribution grid voltage regulation becomes more dynamic. Therefore, a DOPF model is needed that preserves the discrete control characteristics of LTCs while maintaining computational tractability.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Distribution Grid Optimal Power Flow (D-OPF): Modeling, Analysis, and Benchmarking
data_properties.hasAuthor: Rahul Ranjan Jha; Adedoyin Inaolaji; Biswajit Dipan Biswas; Arun Suresh; Anamika Dubey; Sumit Paudyal; Sukumar Kamalasadan
data_properties.hasInstitution: Washington State University; Florida International University; University of North Carolina at Charlotte; ComEd
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Benchmark and compare distribution-grid OPF formulations for feasibility, optimality, and scalability.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Distribution OPF is nonconvex and different relaxations/approximations can be infeasible, inexact, or poorly scalable.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Distribution grid optimal power flow under loss minimization, PV hosting maximization, and voltage deviation minimization.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How do NLP, convex relaxation, and linearized D-OPF formulations compare in feasibility, optimality, and scalability across problem types and feeder sizes?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generation dispatch, DG active/reactive power dispatch, bus voltage profiles, branch power flows/current magnitudes, and PV hosting capacity.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Deterministic, continuous, single-period benchmarking of multiple D-OPF formulations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Bus injection and branch flow formulations; nonlinear, SOCP, SDP, and LinDistFlow variants.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single-period steady-state.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: None; deterministic formulation.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Radial distribution feeders with DGs, capacitor banks, voltage regulators, and substation bus.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Numerical benchmarking and visualization of feasible solution spaces; comparison across formulations and feeder sizes.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Assesses feasibility gap, exactness, solve time, scalability, and AC-feasibility.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Constant-power loads; no explicit demand response or flexible demand.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total power loss; maximize PV hosting capacity; minimize sum of voltage deviations from a setpoint.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC or approximate power-balance equations; voltage magnitude limits; branch current or apparent-power limits; DG apparent-power/reactive-power limits; PV unity-power-factor or reactive-power-control constraints; convex-relaxation PSD/rank or cone constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Load demands pL,i and qL,i; line impedances rij and xij; admittance Yij; voltage limits Vmin/Vmax; voltage setpoint vset; DG ratings sratedDG,i and pDG,max; branch current rating Iratedij; substation voltage Vsub.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Solved with IPOPT, Knitro, Gurobi, CVX, MOSEK, and CPLEX on 123-, 730-, and 2522-node feeders; validated with OpenDSS and MATPOWER.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Compared against OpenDSS substation power flows and MATPOWER; small cases matched closely for exact formulations, while relaxed/linear models were checked for feasibility gaps.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: SOCP and SDP are exact for loss minimization but often inexact for PV hosting and voltage-deviation objectives; NLP-BIM scales better than NLP-BFM; LinDistFlow can misestimate losses, voltages, and PV hosting.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: comprehensive, implementation-centric comparison across formulations and feeder sizes. Limitation: balanced single-phase, deterministic, single-period study; unbalanced multi-phase and richer PV-hosting constraints are not fully addressed.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Loss reduction in a windfarm participating in primary voltage control using an extension of the Convex DistFlow OPF
data_properties.hasAuthor: Benoît Martin; Philippe De Rua; Emmanuel De Jaeger; François Glineur
data_properties.hasInstitution: Université Catholique de Louvain (UCL), MEED/iMMC and CORE/ICTEAM
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Optimal reactive dispatch in a wind farm to reduce collector-grid losses while providing primary voltage control.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Current reactive power setpoint dispatch among wind turbines and switchable capacitor/inductor banks is suboptimal and causes extra energy losses.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: OPF for a radial wind-farm collector grid with transformers, line charging, OLTC, and discrete capacitor/inductor bank switching.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can an extended convex DistFlow OPF accurately and efficiently determine OLTC tap and reactive dispatch under primary voltage control?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal OLTC tap selection, reactive power dispatch of wind turbines and static units, bus voltages, branch power flows, and minimized active power losses.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Extended convex DistFlow with discrete OLTC and static bank switching; formulated as MISOCP and relaxed by linear outer approximation.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Convex DistFlow with π-line model, variable-ratio transformers, SOC relaxation, and convexified voltage-drop equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single operating point; repeated over many operating conditions.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: 10 min data used for yearly clustering; model itself is static per case.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single-period OPF per operating condition.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Radial wind-farm collector grid with DFIG turbines, capacitive cables, OLTC transformer, and switchable capacitor/inductor banks.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Linear outer approximation of SOC constraints using Ben-Tal–Nemirovski BTN relaxation.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Compared with Matpower; accuracy assessed by relaxation error and PF feasibility; faster for some cases but slower at higher BTN degree.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize active power exchange at the PCC, representing collector-grid losses, plus a penalty on reactive mismatch with the PCC setpoint.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Active/reactive nodal balances; branch loss and voltage-drop equations; thermal limits; WT capability curve; voltage bounds; angle-difference limits; PCC balance and voltage; reactive mismatch disjunction; single-choice OLTC tap and bank state constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Branch impedances and charging susceptances; transformer tap ratios and series elements; voltage bounds; thermal limits; WT reactive capability limits; PCC voltage and reactive setpoint; big-M constants; OLTC tap count; bank state count; mismatch penalty weight.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Solved as a MISOCP and further as a MILP via BTN outer approximation; validated by running Matpower power flows on the obtained setpoints; compared against Matpower MIPS over 147 discrete configurations and clustered yearly operating points.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Relaxation accuracy tested on six extreme operating cases and feasibility checked with Matpower PF; results compared against exact Matpower-based OPF across many clustered timesteps.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The relaxed model is often accurate when no reactive mismatch is expected, can outperform Matpower on a significant fraction of cases, and may be faster for moderate BTN degree.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: handles OLTC, shunt elements, and discrete banks in a convex framework; can be made arbitrarily accurate by increasing BTN degree. Limitation: accuracy degrades when loss minimization conflicts with reactive-setpoint tracking.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper studies a radial 78 MW wind farm with 39 DFIG turbines, 21 OLTC taps, and 7 static-unit states.

data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Maximize total market surplus z over device powers, bus voltage angles, and switching variables.

data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: DC subproblem solved as MILP with Gurobi; AC subproblem solved as NLP with IPOPT; large cases use sequential stage-wise optimization and selective contingency inclusion.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Evaluated on 300+ scenarios across 73 to 8316-bus networks from ARPA-E GO challenge datasets.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach achieved high scaled scores in most scenarios, with average scores around 0.983 on Scenario Set 3 and 0.9992 on Scenario Set 2, while meeting time limits.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalable, robust, high-quality solutions, full AC formulation. Limitation: solution quality varies by scenario and depends on available reserve abundance; large cases require sequential decomposition.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Applied to ARPA-E Grid Optimization Challenge 3 datasets and testing platform.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve multi-regional chance-constrained optimal power flow in a distributed, confidentiality-preserving way.

data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Centralized CC-OPF is unsuitable for multi-regional interconnected grids with confidential regional data.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can CC-OPF be solved exactly in a distributed manner while preserving each ISO’s confidential information?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal dispatchable generation schedules across regions; associated bus voltage and line-flow constraint satisfaction under chance constraints.

data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Multi-period day-ahead dispatch over T time slots.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Time slots; case studies use 24 hourly periods.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Day-ahead, 24 time slots in experiments.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Chance constraints with wind-power uncertainty modeled by Gaussian mixture distributions.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Multi-regional interconnected grid with dispatchable generators, wind farms, loads, voltages, and line flows.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Transformation-based encryption plus accelerated average consensus and privacy-preserving average consensus.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported exact optimality relative to centralized benchmark and high accuracy across system sizes and load levels.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost: sum over regions and time of quadratic and linear dispatchable-generation costs.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Capacity bounds, ramp-rate limits, supply-demand chance constraint, and chance constraints on voltages or line flows converted to deterministic inequalities.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generation cost coefficients, generator capacity bounds, ramp-rate bounds, wind-power quantiles from GMMs, chance limits εb and αS, and DLPF mapping coefficients.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Convert chance constraints to deterministic form, encrypt regional variables and coefficients, compute coupled coefficients and aggregated constants via distributed consensus, solve transformed QP, then decrypt regional optimal dispatch.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on multiple IEEE and PEGASE test systems; proposed method matched centralized solutions with very small relative errors.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The method achieves distributed CC-OPF without revealing confidential data and without optimality loss relative to the benchmark.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: exact optimality, no parameter tuning, confidentiality preservation. Limitation: relies on linearized power flow and is not directly full AC OPF.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Applicable to AGC-aware CC-OPF with deterministic participation factors and extendable to joint-chance-constrained OPF.

data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients a2i, a1i, a0i; admittance conductance Gij and susceptance Bij; demand PDi, QDi; limits on PGi, QGi, Vi, PFk; penalty factor C.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Training samples are generated by Monte Carlo simulation and an interior-point OPF solver, then used to train SELM networks in three stages with reinforcement and classification.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 39/57/118-bus and Polish 2383-bus systems; compared against original SELM, deep learning, and model-based OPF.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed approach achieved the best accuracy and much faster computation, and direct learning with original SELM was intractable for OPF.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: fast, few hyperparameters, extensible across systems. Limitation: direct deep learning and original SELM struggle with OPF complexity; future work targets field-data validation.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Sample pre-classification uses active-constraint critical regions to cluster similar OPF samples.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：与用户需求高度一致，明确是配电系统 DOPF，并且核心就是 LTC 的离散控制；同时直接回应了“连续松弛后取整可能导致不可行或次优”的问题。 / English: Highly consistent with the user need: it is a distribution-system DOPF model centered on discrete LTC control, and it directly addresses the infeasibility/suboptimality caused by relaxing discrete variables and rounding.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：主要局限是重点放在 LTC 离散控制，未明确把电容器组、EV、储能和高级逆变器的协同调压作为核心建模对象。 / English: Main limitation: it focuses on discrete LTC control and does not explicitly make coordinated capacitor-bank, EV, storage, and advanced-inverter voltage regulation the central modeling target.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：符合配电网 D-OPF 且包含离散设备建模，具备处理电容器组、调压器等设备的基础，因此可进入进一步筛选。 / English: It matches distribution-grid D-OPF and includes discrete-device modeling, with a basis for handling capacitor banks and voltage regulators, so it is feasible for further reranking.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：它更偏向模型基准比较与可扩展性分析，而不是专门为“严格保留 LTC 离散档位并兼顾实时可解性”设计的求解模型。 / English: It is more of a benchmarking and scalability-analysis study than a solver specifically designed to strictly preserve LTC discrete taps while remaining real-time tractable.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它确实面向配电网不平衡三相 OPF，并包含变压器分接头、无功补偿和分布式电源协调控制，和用户场景有较强相关性。 / English: It does target unbalanced three-phase distribution OPF and includes transformer tap ratios, reactive compensation, and coordinated DER control, so it is relevant to the user scenario.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：其方法更偏连续控制与迭代求解，没有突出对 LTC/电容器离散状态的严格整数保持，因此对“保留离散控制特性”只能部分满足。 / English: The method is oriented toward continuous control and iterative solving, without emphasizing strict integer preservation of LTC/capacitor discrete states, so it only partially satisfies the discrete-control requirement.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它明确建模了离散 OLTC 和可切换电容/电感组，并用 MISOCP 与线性外逼近保持可计算性，和“保留离散特性同时兼顾可解性”的要求相符。 / English: It explicitly models discrete OLTC and switchable capacitor/inductor banks, using MISOCP and linear outer approximation to preserve tractability, which aligns with the need to keep discrete characteristics while remaining solvable.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：主要应用对象是风电场集电网，而非典型配电网 DOPF；同时没有直接聚焦 EV、储能和高级逆变器参与的配电电压协同调节。 / English: Its main application is a wind-farm collector grid rather than a typical distribution DOPF, and it does not directly focus on coordinated distribution voltage regulation with EVs, storage, and advanced inverters.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它强调多时间步安全约束 OPF、储能、爬坡和设备切换，但不是面向配电网 DOPF 的专用模型，也没有突出 LTC 这类配电离散调压设备的精确建模。 / English: It emphasizes multi-step security-constrained OPF, storage, ramping, and device switching, but it is not a dedicated distribution DOPF model and does not specifically emphasize accurate modeling of LTC-style discrete distribution voltage-control devices.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：与用户要求的“配电系统 DOPF + LTC 离散档位精确保留”不够贴合，且核心场景更偏大规模安全约束调度/市场出清。 / English: It is not well aligned with the requested combination of distribution-system DOPF plus exact preservation of LTC discrete taps, and its core setting is large-scale security-constrained scheduling/market clearing.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它是分布式机会约束 OPF，重点在多区域协调与隐私保护，适合不确定性调度，但不是配电网 LTC 离散控制的专用模型。 / English: It is a distributed chance-constrained OPF focused on multi-regional coordination and privacy preservation, which is useful for uncertainty-aware dispatch but not a dedicated model for discrete LTC control in distribution grids.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：采用线性化潮流且面向多区域输电场景，对用户要求的“保留 LTC 离散特性并用于配电 DOPF”缺少直接匹配。 / English: It uses linearized power flow and targets a multi-regional transmission setting, so it lacks a direct match to preserving LTC discrete characteristics in distribution DOPF.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它面向含 PV 和储能的 UC-OPF，强调日 ahead 调度与可行性修正，和用户关注的配电网 DOPF 不是同一类问题。 / English: It targets UC-OPF for renewable-integrated systems, emphasizing day-ahead scheduling and feasibility correction, which is not the same problem class as distribution-grid DOPF.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：没有把 LTC 或电容器组的离散控制作为核心建模对象，因此无法满足“准确处理配电离散调压设备”的关键要求。 / English: It does not make LTC or capacitor-bank discrete control a core modeling object, so it cannot satisfy the key requirement of accurately handling discrete distribution voltage-control devices.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它是连续变量的学习型 AC-OPF 近似方法，重点在快速预测与大规模计算效率，不是显式保留 LTC/电容器离散状态的 DOPF 模型。 / English: It is a continuous-variable learning-based AC-OPF approximation focused on fast prediction and large-scale efficiency, not an explicit DOPF model that preserves discrete LTC/capacitor states.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：对用户最关键的“离散控制设备精确建模”不匹配，因此不适合作为该需求的候选模型。 / English: It does not match the user’s most critical requirement of exact discrete-device modeling, so it is not a suitable candidate for this need.

raw_consistency.overall_summary: 中文：最符合需求的是 Efficient_Distribution_System；Convex_DistFlow_Loss_Reduction 也具备离散 OLTC/电容切换与可解性平衡的特征，可进入后续比较。其余候选要么偏基准/连续近似，要么偏输电、UC 或学习型近似，和“配电系统 DOPF 中精确保留 LTC 离散控制特性”这一核心要求存在明显偏离。 / English: The best fit is Efficient_Distribution_System; Convex_DistFlow_Loss_Reduction also has discrete OLTC/capacitor switching with tractability balance and can proceed to later comparison. top_rows.Requirement text: I need an optimization model suitable for distribution system DOPF that can accurately handle discrete control devices such as load tap changers (LTCs). In real distribution grids, LTCs and capacitor banks can only operate in discrete tap positions or states, rather than being continuously adjusted. However, many DOPF models relax integer variables into continuous variables to reduce computational difficulty, and then round the results to obtain tap positions. This approach may lead to infeasible or suboptimal solutions when the system operates close to its limits. With the integration of distributed PV, electric vehicles, storage, and advanced inverters, distribution grid voltage regulation becomes more dynamic. Therefore, a DOPF model is needed that preserves the discrete control characteristics of LTCs while maintaining computational tractability.

requirement.requirement_text: I need a model for multi-agent distributed OPF that can maintain D-OPF convergence and feasibility even when communication links are unreliable or interrupted. With the development of DERs, microgrids, and transactive energy markets, centralized OPF may no longer be suitable for future distribution grid operation. Multiple regional agents or microgrid agents need to coordinate through distributed OPF. However, distributed ADMM-type algorithms rely on the exchange of consensus messages or global variables between regions. Once a communication link is lost, some global variables cannot be updated, which may slow convergence, cause results to deviate from global OPF, or make the solution infeasible. Therefore, a D-OPF framework is needed that can predict missing global variables during communication interruptions, for example by using ANN / DFNN to estimate missing voltage phasors or consensus information, so that feasible D-OPF solutions close to the global result can still be obtained under unreliable communication.

Multiple regional agents or microgrid agents need to coordinate through distributed OPF. However, distributed ADMM-type algorithms rely on the exchange of consensus messages or global variables between regions. Once a communication link is lost, some global variables cannot be updated, which may slow convergence, cause results to deviate from global OPF, or make the solution infeasible. Therefore, a D-OPF framework is needed that can predict missing global variables during communication interruptions, for example by using ANN / DFNN to estimate missing voltage phasors or consensus information, so that feasible D-OPF solutions close to the global result can still be obtained under unreliable communication.

data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Capacity bounds, ramp-rate limits, supply-demand chance constraint, and chance constraints on voltages or line flows converted to deterministic inequalities.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generation cost coefficients, generator capacity bounds, ramp-rate bounds, wind-power quantiles from GMMs, chance limits εb and αS, and DLPF mapping coefficients.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Convert chance constraints to deterministic form, encrypt regional variables and coefficients, compute coupled coefficients and aggregated constants via distributed consensus, solve transformed QP, then decrypt regional optimal dispatch.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on multiple IEEE and PEGASE test systems; proposed method matched centralized solutions with very small relative errors.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The method achieves distributed CC-OPF without revealing confidential data and without optimality loss relative to the benchmark.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: exact optimality, no parameter tuning, confidentiality preservation. Limitation: relies on linearized power flow and is not directly full AC OPF.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Applicable to AGC-aware CC-OPF with deterministic participation factors and extendable to joint-chance-constrained OPF.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Machine Learning-Aided Security Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Jubeyer Rahman; Cong Feng; Jie Zhang
data_properties.hasInstitution: The University of Texas at Dallas
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve security-constrained AC optimal power flow efficiently using a machine-learning-aided approach.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Full AC OPF is highly nonlinear and non-convex, making large-scale security-constrained solving computationally challenging.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained AC optimal power flow with switched shunt security constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a machine-learning-aided method predict key OPF variables and avoid running a physics-based OPF solver while preserving feasibility?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Bus voltage magnitudes and voltage angles; derived current injections, complex/real power injections, generator dispatch settings, and branch power flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid machine-learning-aided OPF using multi-input multi-output random forest plus physics-based network equations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with bus admittance matrix, current injection, apparent power, and nodal power balance.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period steady-state OPF.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Not specified; load samples from hourly ERCOT profile used for training/testing.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per case.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: No explicit uncertainty model; trained on sampled load cases.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC transmission OPF with generators, buses, branches, and switched shunts.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Multi-input multi-output random forest predicts voltages, then network equations recover remaining variables.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported zero constraint violation for the proposed method and much faster solution time than MATPOWER MIPS.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Load demand inputs Pd and Qd are used as predictors; no demand response model.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator costs represented by individual piece-wise linear cost functions.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Voltage magnitude and angle bounds; generator active/reactive power bounds; switched shunt susceptance bounds; real and reactive nodal power balance equations; branch apparent power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes vi and angles θi; generator outputs pg and qg; switched shunt susceptance bcs; real/reactive demands pd and qd; branch flow limit sf; bus admittance matrix Y; generator cost cg.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: RF is trained on converged MATPOWER solutions; case I predicts v and θ then computes injections and costs via network equations; case II predicts all OPF variables directly.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on a 500-bus GO competition network using 8,760 load samples; compared against MATPOWER MIPS and a pure ML baseline.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method closely matches MIPS voltage solutions, satisfies network constraints, and reduces total solution time from 2030.4 s to 35.26 s.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: fast and feasible OPF approximation without running a physics-based solver. Limitation: pure end-to-end ML still causes many equality-constraint violations.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Potentially useful for post-contingency analysis with many network topologies and load profiles.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：与需求高度一致，直接面向多智能体分布式 OPF，在通信不可靠或中断时用 DFNN 估计缺失的全局/一致性变量，并强调保持收敛与可行性。 / English: Highly consistent with the requirement; it directly targets multi-agent distributed OPF and uses a DFNN to estimate missing global/consensus variables under unreliable or interrupted communication, explicitly aiming to preserve convergence and feasibility.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：主要限制是对训练好的 DFNN 和相近运行工况有依赖，估计偏差可能影响与全局最优解的接近程度。 / English: Main limitation is dependence on a trained DFNN and similar operating conditions; estimator bias may affect closeness to the global optimum.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：具备分布式 OPF 和 ADMM 协调特征，但核心目标是 MTDC 配电网的系统级控制，并假设正常通信运行；没有针对通信链路中断时缺失变量预测或断链下的收敛/可行性保持机制。 / English: It has distributed OPF and ADMM coordination features, but its core goal is system-level control of MTDC distribution grids and it assumes normal communication operation; it does not address missing-variable prediction or convergence/feasibility preservation under link interruptions.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：场景偏向 MTDC 而非你描述的多区域/微电网代理式 D-OPF，且缺少 ANN/DFNN 补全消息的机制。 / English: The scenario is MTDC-focused rather than the multi-regional/microgrid agent-based D-OPF you described, and it lacks an ANN/DFNN mechanism for message completion.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它能用深度学习预测 AC-OPF 解并结合物理约束提升可行性，但本质上是单时段的集中式 AC-OPF 近似器，不是多智能体分布式 ADMM 框架，也没有专门处理通信中断下的消息补全与分布式收敛保证。 / English: It can predict AC-OPF solutions with deep learning and improve feasibility via physical constraints, but it is fundamentally a single-period centralized AC-OPF approximator, not a multi-agent distributed ADMM framework, and it does not specifically handle message completion or distributed convergence guarantees under communication loss.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：缺少面向分布式区域代理协同的结构，不能直接满足“通信中断时预测缺失全局变量以维持 D-OPF 收敛”的核心要求。 / English: It lacks the structure for coordinated regional agents and does not directly satisfy the core requirement of predicting missing global variables to maintain D-OPF convergence during communication interruptions.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：该模型适合做局部、可扩展的 AC-OPF 近似，但主要是模仿集中式求解器的学习模型，不是显式的多智能体分布式 OPF，也没有针对通信链路失效时的变量补全或鲁棒收敛设计。 / English: This model is suitable as a local, scalable AC-OPF approximator, but it is mainly a learning model that imitates a centralized solver rather than an explicit multi-agent distributed OPF method, and it has no design for variable completion or robust convergence when communication links fail.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：虽然具备局部消息传递特征，但不足以覆盖你要求的 ADMM 式区域协同、缺失全局变量预测和断链可行性保持。 / English: Although it has local message-passing traits, it is insufficient for the ADMM-style regional coordination, missing-global-variable prediction, and feasibility preservation under link outages that you require.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它确实是分布式多区域 OPF，但重点在机会约束与机密保护，而不是通信中断下的缺失变量估计；其线性化潮流与加密一致性流程也不同于你需要的 ANN/DFNN 补全机制。 / English: It is indeed a distributed multi-regional OPF method, but its focus is chance constraints and confidentiality preservation rather than estimating missing variables under communication loss; its linearized power flow and encrypted consensus workflow also differ from the ANN/DFNN completion mechanism you need.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：缺少对不可靠通信、消息丢失和基于学习的全局变量恢复的直接支持。 / English: It lacks direct support for unreliable communication, message loss, and learning-based recovery of global variables.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它采用机器学习结合物理方程来恢复变量并保持可行性，这一点与“补全缺失变量”有一定相关性，但目标是集中式安全约束 AC-OPF，不是多智能体分布式 D-OPF，也没有针对通信中断或 ADMM 一致性变量缺失的专门机制。 / English: It uses machine learning plus physical equations to recover variables and preserve feasibility, which is somewhat related to variable completion, but its target is centralized security-constrained AC-OPF rather than multi-agent distributed D-OPF, and it has no dedicated mechanism for communication interruptions or missing ADMM consensus variables.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：不能直接满足你对“分布式、通信不可靠、预测缺失全局变量以维持收敛”的核心场景。 / English: It does not directly satisfy your core scenario of distributed operation, unreliable communication, and predicting missing global variables to maintain convergence.

top_rows.Requirement text: I need a model for multi-agent distributed OPF that can maintain D-OPF convergence and feasibility even when communication links are unreliable or interrupted. With the development of DERs, microgrids, and transactive energy markets, centralized OPF may no longer be suitable for future distribution grid operation. Multiple regional agents or microgrid agents need to coordinate through distributed OPF. However, distributed ADMM-type algorithms rely on the exchange of consensus messages or global variables between regions. Once a communication link is lost, some global variables cannot be updated, which may slow convergence, cause results to deviate from global OPF, or make the solution infeasible. Therefore, a D-OPF framework is needed that can predict missing global variables during communication interruptions, for example by using ANN / DFNN to estimate missing voltage phasors or consensus information, so that feasible D-OPF solutions close to the global result can still be obtained under unreliable communication.

requirement.requirement_text: I need an OPF model or algorithm for feeder reconfiguration in distribution networks, which selects the on/off status of switches to reduce losses, improve load balancing, or optimize operating conditions. This problem is essentially a mixed-integer nonlinear problem with switch states, and is computationally difficult. Traditional formal methods require long computation times, while branch exchange heuristics may depend on the initial topology and have unstable iteration counts. Therefore, a feeder reconfiguration method based on AC-OPF convex relaxation, especially SOCP relaxation, is needed. It should quickly select the lines to be opened without complex parameter tuning or initialization, and obtain a radial distribution network configuration that is globally optimal or close to optimal as much as possible.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Optimize distribution feeder switch configurations for loss minimization or load balancing under radiality and power-flow constraints.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Probabilistically Robust AC Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Mohammadreza Chamanbaz; Fabrizio Dabbene; Constantino M. Lagoa
data_properties.hasInstitution: iTrust Center for Research in Cyber Security, Singapore University of Technology and Design; CNR-IEIIT, Torino, Italy; Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Penn State University
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Minimize generation cost in AC optimal power flow while satisfying network constraints under uncertain loads and renewable generation with probabilistic guarantees.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Classical OPF dispatch is rigid and can become inefficient or infeasible under renewable and load uncertainty, causing overloads and outages.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Robust and chance-constrained AC optimal power flow with uncertain loads and renewable generators.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How can AC-OPF be solved efficiently under uncertainty while limiting the probability of violating generation and transmission constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal controllable generation dispatch, generator voltage magnitudes, deployment vector, and corresponding bus voltage and line-flow-feasible operating point.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Scenario-with-certificates formulation combined with convex SDP relaxation of AC power flow.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power balance equations with voltage-magnitude and line-flow constraints via lifted matrix W.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period OPF repeated over hourly demand scenarios in experiments.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per solve; 24 hourly solves in simulation.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Probabilistic uncertainty in loads and renewable generation using scenario with certificates and chance constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Includes renewable generators, uncertain loads, generator participation factors, voltage limits, and transmission limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Convex relaxation plus randomized scenario-with-certificates sampling.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: A priori probabilistic guarantee on constraint-violation risk; exact for a restricted class of networks.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uncertain loads are explicitly modeled and balanced through generator deployment factors.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost f(u); in the penalized variant, worst-case cost adds reactive-power and line-loss penalties.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power balance equalities; generator active/reactive limits; voltage magnitude bounds; line-voltage-difference or apparent-flow limits; deployment factors sum to one and remain nonnegative.
data_properties.usesParameter: Uncertain complex load and renewable deviations δ; deployment vector α; bus-voltage matrix W split into Wu and Wx; risk levels ε and β; line admittances ylm; voltage and power limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Uses SDP lifting W=VV* and scenario-with-certificates sampling to solve a convex program; implemented with YALMIP and Mosek.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on the New England 39-bus system with Monte Carlo testing over 10,000 samples and comparison against nominal OPF and a prior probabilistic AC-OPF method.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method greatly reduced infeasible samples and line-flow violations versus nominal OPF, while using far fewer scenario samples than the compared parameterized approach.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: less conservative, probabilistic guarantees, computationally efficient, and exact for some networks. Limitation: exactness is only proven for a restrictive network class.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Can incorporate N-1 security constraints and outage probabilities within the same scenario framework.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：与用户需求高度一致，明确针对配电网馈线重构，直接优化开关开断状态以降损、负荷均衡并满足径向约束；同时采用 AC-OPF 的 SOCP 凸松弛与分支潮流结构，符合“快速、少参数调优、尽量全局最优或近优”的要求。/ English explanation: Highly consistent with the user need. It explicitly targets feeder reconfiguration in distribution networks, optimizes switch open/close states for loss reduction and load balancing under radiality, and uses AC-OPF SOCP convex relaxation with branch-flow structure, matching the need for fast, low-tuning, globally optimal or near-optimal reconfiguration.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：主要局限是单时段静态重构；如果用户需要多时段、强不确定性或动态场景，这一点不完全覆盖。/ English explanation: Main limitation is single-period static reconfiguration; it does not fully cover multi-period, strong uncertainty, or dynamic scenarios.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：它确实支持配电网 D-OPF，并比较了 SOCP 等凸松弛，说明在配电网优化上有方法参考价值；但它的核心是建模与基准对比，不是专门针对馈线重构的离散开关选线算法，因此对“选择打开哪些线以形成径向网络”的直接支持不足。/ English explanation: It does support distribution-grid D-OPF and compares SOCP and other relaxations, so it is methodologically relevant; however, its core is modeling and benchmarking rather than a dedicated discrete switch-opening feeder-reconfiguration algorithm, so direct support for selecting which lines to open to form a radial network is insufficient.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：缺少面向馈线重构的开关状态优化与径向化决策主线，更多是连续型 D-OPF 对比研究。/ English explanation: It lacks a primary switch-state optimization and radialization decision pipeline for feeder reconfiguration, and is mainly a continuous D-OPF comparison study.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：该候选展示了 SOCP-OPF 的高效性和较强的凸松弛能力，但对象是输电网的环网与循环角约束问题，不是配电网馈线重构；也没有明确的开关开断、径向结构选择或离散重构机制。/ English explanation: This candidate demonstrates efficient SOCP-OPF and strong convex-relaxation capability, but it is aimed at meshed transmission networks with cyclic angle constraints, not distribution feeder reconfiguration; it also lacks explicit switch open/close, radial topology selection, or discrete reconfiguration mechanisms.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：与用户要求的“配电馈线重构 + 开关状态选择 + 径向化”不匹配，且不是用户强调的配电场景。/ English explanation: It does not match the user’s required combination of distribution feeder reconfiguration, switch-state selection, and radialization, and it is not in the distribution setting emphasized by the user.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：它包含开关状态决策，并且强调可扩展的多时段安全约束 OPF，因此在“含开关的网络优化”上有一定相关性；但其核心目标是大规模安全约束调度与市场出清，采用的是两阶段 DC/MILP + AC/NLP 流程，不是面向配电馈线重构的 SOCP 凸松弛方法。/ English explanation: It includes switching-status decisions and scalable multi-step security-constrained OPF, so it is somewhat related to network optimization with switches; however, its core goal is large-scale security-constrained dispatch and market clearing, and it uses a two-stage DC/MILP + AC/NLP workflow rather than an SOCP-relaxed feeder-reconfiguration method.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：对“快速选线开断、无需复杂初始化、基于 SOCP 松弛得到径向配电网近优解”的匹配度不足。/ English explanation: It does not sufficiently match the need for fast line-opening selection, no complex initialization, and an SOCP-relaxed near-optimal radial distribution-network solution.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：它面向配电网不平衡三相 OPF，和配电运行优化相关，但重点是无功重调度、负荷削减与协调控制，并未明确优化开关开断状态，也不是基于 AC-OPF 凸松弛或 SOCP 的馈线重构算法。/ English explanation: It targets unbalanced three-phase distribution OPF and is related to distribution operation optimization, but its focus is reactive redispatch, load curtailment, and coordinated control; it does not explicitly optimize switch open/close states and is not an AC-OPF convex-relaxation or SOCP-based feeder-reconfiguration algorithm.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：缺少用户要求的离散开关重构、SOCP 凸松弛求解路径，以及径向拓扑选择机制。/ English explanation: It lacks the discrete switch-reconfiguration mechanism, the SOCP convex-relaxation solution path, and the radial topology selection mechanism required by the user.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文说明：它是带不确定性的 AC-OPF 凸松弛方法，强调概率约束与鲁棒性，方法上与“用凸松弛快速求近优解”有一定关联；但它主要解决不确定负荷/新能源下的鲁棒运行，不是馈线重构问题，也不是用户特别强调的 SOCP 松弛，而是 SDP 松弛。/ English explanation: It is a convex-relaxation AC-OPF method with uncertainty and probabilistic constraints, so it is methodologically related to fast near-optimal solving; however, it mainly addresses robust operation under uncertain loads and renewables, not feeder reconfiguration, and it uses SDP relaxation rather than the SOCP relaxation specifically emphasized by the user.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文说明：缺少开关状态选择与径向重构目标，且松弛类型与用户偏好的 SOCP 不一致。/ English explanation: It lacks switch-state selection and radial reconfiguration objectives, and its relaxation type is inconsistent with the user’s SOCP preference.

top_rows.Requirement text: I need an OPF model or algorithm for feeder reconfiguration in distribution networks, which selects the on/off status of switches to reduce losses, improve load balancing, or optimize operating conditions. This problem is essentially a mixed-integer nonlinear problem with switch states, and is computationally difficult. Traditional formal methods require long computation times, while branch exchange heuristics may depend on the initial topology and have unstable iteration counts. Therefore, a feeder reconfiguration method based on AC-OPF convex relaxation, especially SOCP relaxation, is needed. It should quickly select the lines to be opened without complex parameter tuning or initialization, and obtain a radial distribution network configuration that is globally optimal or close to optimal as much as possible.

requirement.requirement_name: Grid Foundation Model for power systems
requirement.requirement_text: I need a Grid Foundation Model (GridFM) for power systems to deal with the large-scale complexity and uncertainty brought by the energy transition. Future power grids will include massive renewable energy, distributed energy resources, electric vehicles, inverter-based devices, climate-driven uncertain loads, and more complex operating scenarios. Traditional simulation and optimization methods will face insufficient computational capability in real-time analysis, large-scale scenario analysis, N-1 / N-2 contingency analysis, OPF, state estimation, and planning. Meanwhile, existing AI models are often trained only for a single task or a single system, with limited transferability. Therefore, a GridFM is needed that can be pre-trained on large amounts of multi-topology, multi-operating-condition, and multimodal grid data, and then adapted to different grids and tasks through small-scale fine-tuning. It is especially needed for accelerating downstream applications such as power flow, optimal power flow, and contingency analysis, while maintaining physical consistency and significantly improving computational speed.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To advocate and outline grid foundation models for power-system operations, planning, and control.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Increasing grid complexity and uncertainty from the energy transition, climate change, aging infrastructure, and cybersecurity threats.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Lack of scalable, transferable AI methods for diverse power-grid tasks and power-flow-related applications.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can foundation models be developed for electric power grids to generalize across grid data and accelerate downstream applications such as power flow and OPF?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: No OPF model is solved in this paper; it proposes a GridFM-v0 concept for reconstructing power-flow states and, in discussed downstream use, optimal generation dispatch and objective values.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Graph neural network-based foundation model concept; masked autoencoder pre-training on graph-structured grid data.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow reconstruction on graph nodes with bus variables and line/transformer edges.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Initially single-time-step power-flow data; extendable to multiple consecutive time steps for forecasting.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Single time step in the near-term model; high-resolution PMU data mentioned for dynamic extensions.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Not specified; near-term focus is static power-flow applications.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses diverse topologies, load conditions, perturbations, and synthetic scenarios; discusses scenario trees and stochastic programming.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Transmission and distribution grid applications including power flow, OPF, contingency analysis, state estimation, stability, control, planning, and cybersecurity.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Self-supervised masked graph autoencoding with physics-informed loss; intended to speed up power-flow-related computation.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Projected 3–4 orders-of-magnitude speed-up over conventional power-flow solvers; less than 1% error cited from related GNN work.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Mentions load conditions, load forecasting, electric vehicles, heating electrification, and demand uncertainty.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: For OPF use, minimize generation costs by reconstructing generator power; the paper does not present a full OPF mathematical formulation.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Reconstructed node variables must satisfy power-flow equations and bounds such as generator capacity constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus active power, reactive power, voltage magnitude, voltage angle; line and transformer connectivity; topology, load conditions, and power-flow solutions.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: GridFM-v0 is proposed as a masked graph autoencoder pre-trained on solved power-flow cases from multiple topologies and load conditions, then fine-tuned for downstream tasks.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: No direct model validation results are reported for GridFM-v0; validation is proposed on open datasets and later on utility data behind firewalls.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The paper argues GridFMs could generalize across grid tasks and substantially accelerate power-system analysis, especially power-flow-related applications.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalability, adaptability, and simulation acceleration. Limitations: data availability, privacy, trust, and difficulty accessing operational grid data.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper is a perspective proposing a roadmap rather than presenting a completed OPF solver.

data_properties.hasModelName: Scalable Security Constrained Multi Step OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Scalable Solutions for Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow With Multiple Time Steps
data_properties.hasAuthor: Hussein Sharadga; Javad Mohammadi; Constance Crozier; Kyri Baker
data_properties.hasInstitution: Texas A&M International University; University of Texas at Austin; Georgia Institute of Technology; University of Colorado Boulder
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve large-scale security-constrained optimal power flow with multiple time steps efficiently under strict time limits.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Large SCOPF instances contain millions of continuous/integer variables and nonlinear nonconvex constraints, making them difficult to solve within challenge time limits.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained optimal power flow with multiple time steps, including AC power flow, contingencies, reserves, device switching, and ramping constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a decomposition-based hybrid solver scale multi-timestep SCOPF to very large grids while maintaining high-quality feasible solutions?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generation and consumption dispatch, device switching status, bus voltage angles, AC power-flow feasible operating point, and reserve allocations.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Two-stage DC/AC decomposition with sequential optimization for large networks.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: DC module uses linearized/MILP approximations; AC module solves full nonlinear AC power-flow equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Multiple time steps; sequential stage-wise optimization for large horizons.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Time-step based control horizon; exact interval length not specified.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Control horizon divided into stages for networks over 2000 buses.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Contingency constraints included; no stochastic or robust uncertainty model stated.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC OPF with reserves, ramping, device uptime/downtime, and switching constraints.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Problem reformulation, McCormick relaxation, slack variables, clique constraints, analytical derivatives, vectorization, and sequential bound updates.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Designed for scalability and strict time limits on very large instances.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Consumption devices represented with bid blocks and power consumption bounds.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Maximize total market surplus z over device powers, bus voltage angles, and switching variables.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Equality constraints G enforce power-balance and AC/DC network equations; inequality constraints H cover voltage limits, real/reactive power limits, reserves, ramping, switching, contingency, and device operation constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Device power pjt, bus voltage angle θit, switching status ujt, shunt conductance gshjt, branch flow limits smaxj, reserve factors σscrn, ramp-up Pru, ramp-down Prd, and mismatch penalty pit.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: DC subproblem solved as MILP with Gurobi; AC subproblem solved as NLP with IPOPT; large cases use sequential stage-wise optimization and selective contingency inclusion.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Evaluated on 300+ scenarios across 73 to 8316-bus networks from ARPA-E GO challenge datasets.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach achieved high scaled scores in most scenarios, with average scores around 0.983 on Scenario Set 3 and 0.9992 on Scenario Set 2, while meeting time limits.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalable, robust, high-quality solutions, full AC formulation. Limitation: solution quality varies by scenario and depends on available reserve abundance; large cases require sequential decomposition.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Applied to ARPA-E Grid Optimization Challenge 3 datasets and testing platform.

data_properties.hasModelName: Real Time Sequential Security Constrained OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Real-Time Sequential Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow: A Hybrid Knowledge-Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning Approach
data_properties.hasAuthor: Zhongkai Yi; Xue Wang; Cheng Yang; Chao Yang; Mengyang Niu; Wotao Yin
data_properties.hasInstitution: Alibaba DAMO Academy; Alibaba US; Tsinghua University; Harbin Institute of Technology
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve sequential real-time security-constrained optimal power flow with fast dispatch decisions under inaccurate environmental parameters.
data_properties.hasMotivation: ACOPF is nonconvex, time-coupled by ramping limits, and difficult to solve quickly and safely when system parameters are inaccurate or contingencies are unexperienced.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Sequential security-constrained AC optimal power flow for real-time operation with generator active/reactive dispatch and network security limits.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a hybrid knowledge-data-driven reinforcement learning method produce safe real-time OPF dispatches efficiently without relying on accurate environmental models?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Safe generator active and reactive power dispatch commands; resulting bus voltage magnitudes and branch active/reactive power flows within limits.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid knowledge-data-driven reinforcement learning with a safety-layer projection model and inactive-constraint identification.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow formulation with nonlinear nodal injections, branch flows, voltage magnitudes, and ramping-coupled generator limits.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Sequential multi-step dispatch with future load forecasts and ramping-coupled time dependence.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Real-time operation over time slots; forecasting horizon T steps.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Infinite-horizon sequential decision process terminated by grid failure/non-convergence.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses reinforcement learning for inaccurate environments and updates safety-layer parameters from latest measurements.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained ACOPF with coordinated active and reactive power dispatch, voltage and branch-flow security limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Improved SAC with SAM, prioritized replay, adaptive entropy, hybrid safety layer, and inactive-constraint elimination.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Claims faster decision-making and reduced security violations with comparable economic performance.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Includes forecasted net load demand in the state; no explicit demand response control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize cumulative generation operating cost, with quadratic cost coefficients for each generator over time.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power-balance equations, branch active/reactive flow equations, generator active/reactive limits, branch flow limits, voltage magnitude limits, and ramping-coupled generator bounds; safety-layer projection also enforces linearized security constraints and power balance.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients; generator active/reactive bounds and ramping limits; bus voltages; line conductance/susceptance or resistance/reactance; branch flow limits; load demand and forecasted load; slack-bus limits; penalty coefficients; SAC temperature and learning rates.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Sequential decisions are produced by an improved soft actor-critic policy, then projected by a linear security layer initialized from linearized power-flow knowledge and updated with data; inactive constraints are removed analytically.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 30-bus and larger systems, including contingency and parameter-error scenarios, with comparisons against penalty, constrained-policy, and pure data-driven safety-layer baselines.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The method maintains voltages and branch flows within safe ranges, reduces violation times in early training and contingencies, and scales to larger systems with low decision time.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: safe real-time dispatch, better robustness to inaccurate models, and high computational efficiency. Limitation: safety layer uses linearized power-flow approximation and may need conservative limits to offset approximation error.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper also evaluates scalability on 9-, 30-, 57-, 118-, and 1187-bus systems.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Probabilistically Robust AC Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Mohammadreza Chamanbaz; Fabrizio Dabbene; Constantino M. Lagoa

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Minimize generation cost in AC optimal power flow while satisfying network constraints under uncertain loads and renewable generation with probabilistic guarantees.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Classical OPF dispatch is rigid and can become inefficient or infeasible under renewable and load uncertainty, causing overloads and outages.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Robust and chance-constrained AC optimal power flow with uncertain loads and renewable generators.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How can AC-OPF be solved efficiently under uncertainty while limiting the probability of violating generation and transmission constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal controllable generation dispatch, generator voltage magnitudes, deployment vector, and corresponding bus voltage and line-flow-feasible operating point.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Scenario-with-certificates formulation combined with convex SDP relaxation of AC power flow.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power balance equations with voltage-magnitude and line-flow constraints via lifted matrix W.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period OPF repeated over hourly demand scenarios in experiments.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per solve; 24 hourly solves in simulation.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Probabilistic uncertainty in loads and renewable generation using scenario with certificates and chance constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Includes renewable generators, uncertain loads, generator participation factors, voltage limits, and transmission limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Convex relaxation plus randomized scenario-with-certificates sampling.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: A priori probabilistic guarantee on constraint-violation risk; exact for a restricted class of networks.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uncertain loads are explicitly modeled and balanced through generator deployment factors.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost f(u); in the penalized variant, worst-case cost adds reactive-power and line-loss penalties.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power balance equalities; generator active/reactive limits; voltage magnitude bounds; line-voltage-difference or apparent-flow limits; deployment factors sum to one and remain nonnegative.
data_properties.usesParameter: Uncertain complex load and renewable deviations δ; deployment vector α; bus-voltage matrix W split into Wu and Wx; risk levels ε and β; line admittances ylm; voltage and power limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Uses SDP lifting W=VV* and scenario-with-certificates sampling to solve a convex program; implemented with YALMIP and Mosek.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on the New England 39-bus system with Monte Carlo testing over 10,000 samples and comparison against nominal OPF and a prior probabilistic AC-OPF method.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method greatly reduced infeasible samples and line-flow violations versus nominal OPF, while using far fewer scenario samples than the compared parameterized approach.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: less conservative, probabilistic guarantees, computationally efficient, and exact for some networks. Limitation: exactness is only proven for a restrictive network class.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Can incorporate N-1 security constraints and outage probabilities within the same scenario framework.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve security-constrained AC optimal power flow efficiently using a machine-learning-aided approach.

data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with bus admittance matrix, current injection, apparent power, and nodal power balance.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period steady-state OPF.

data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per case.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: No explicit uncertainty model; trained on sampled load cases.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC transmission OPF with generators, buses, branches, and switched shunts.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Multi-input multi-output random forest predicts voltages, then network equations recover remaining variables.

data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Load demand inputs Pd and Qd are used as predictors; no demand response model.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator costs represented by individual piece-wise linear cost functions.

data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method closely matches MIPS voltage solutions, satisfies network constraints, and reduces total solution time from 2030.4 s to 35.26 s.

data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: None explicit; random cost-function test instances only.

data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported 99% test accuracy; feasibility improved to 100% with epsilon adjustment.

data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Generator active/reactive limits, voltage magnitude limits, line-flow limits, AC power balance, preventive generator set-point equality across contingencies, eigenvalue-based small-signal stability damping ratio constraints.

data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach obtained cost-optimal solutions satisfying both static and dynamic security constraints; epsilon increased feasibility to 100% with small cost increase.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: tractable MILP approximation and improved feasibility. Limitations: approximation error may cause optimality loss and separate networks are needed for different grids.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses a conservative feasibility margin epsilon to trade off feasibility and optimality.

top_rows.Requirement name: Grid Foundation Model for power systems
top_rows.Requirement text: I need a Grid Foundation Model (GridFM) for power systems to deal with the large-scale complexity and uncertainty brought by the energy transition. Future power grids will include massive renewable energy, distributed energy resources, electric vehicles, inverter-based devices, climate-driven uncertain loads, and more complex operating scenarios. Traditional simulation and optimization methods will face insufficient computational capability in real-time analysis, large-scale scenario analysis, N-1 / N-2 contingency analysis, OPF, state estimation, and planning.
