data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Day-Ahead and Real Time Optimal Power Flow considering Renewable Energy Resources
data_properties.hasAuthor: S. Surender Reddy; P.R. Bijwe
data_properties.hasInstitution: Woosong University; Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To schedule generation economically while maintaining security in day-ahead and real-time OPF with renewable variability.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Conventional DA-OPF and RT-OPF use static snapshots and ignore renewable/load variability within scheduling intervals.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Optimal power flow for thermal-wind-solar systems with renewable variability, voltage, reactive power, line-flow, and ramp constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can participation factors evaluated once at the start of each interval capture intra-interval renewable variability without increasing optimization dimensionality?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generator dispatch schedules, renewable generation schedules, interval costs/profits, and voltage stability index values.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Single optimization with 'best-fit' participation factors over sub-interval variability.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with voltage magnitude/angle, reactive power, and line-flow constraints.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Day-ahead and real-time multi-interval scheduling with 15-min and 1-min sub-intervals.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: RT-OPF: 1 min sub-intervals within 10-min intervals; DA-OPF: 15 min sub-sub-intervals within 1 h intervals.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: RT-OPF over 60 min; DA-OPF over 24 h.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses forecasted solar, wind, and load variability within intervals; no explicit stochastic or robust formulation.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Thermal generators with wind and solar PV injections, AGC participation factors, ramp limits, and voltage stability index.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Evaluates 'best-fit' participation factors once to avoid separate optimization for every sub-interval.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported lower total cost and improved voltage stability versus conventional interval-by-interval OPF.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Forecasted load demand varies within sub-intervals and is included in imbalance calculations.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost over RT sub-intervals; maximize total profit over DA intervals as revenue minus generation cost.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Active and reactive nodal power balance, generator output limits with ramp-up/down limits, renewable output caps, bus-voltage limits, line-flow limits, and demand-supply balance constraint in DA-OPF.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients; energy price; wind and solar direct cost coefficients; bus admittance Gij/Bij; ramp limits; voltage and line-flow limits; forecasted load, wind, and solar outputs; participation factors.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: MATLAB Optimization Toolbox FMINCON was used on the IEEE 30-bus system with wind at bus 11 and solar PV at bus 13.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Compared conventional and proposed RT-OPF/DA-OPF on IEEE 30-bus test system using 60-min RT and 24-h DA schedules.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed approach reduced RT total cost and increased DA profit while keeping optimization size unchanged and improving voltage stability.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: captures intra-interval variability with little added computational burden. Limitation: relies on forecast availability and fixed participation factors within each interval.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Voltage stability was assessed using the L-index/VSEI.

data_properties.hasModelName: Scalable Security Constrained Multi Step OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Scalable Solutions for Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow With Multiple Time Steps
data_properties.hasAuthor: Hussein Sharadga; Javad Mohammadi; Constance Crozier; Kyri Baker
data_properties.hasInstitution: Texas A&M International University; University of Texas at Austin; Georgia Institute of Technology; University of Colorado Boulder
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve large-scale security-constrained optimal power flow with multiple time steps efficiently under strict time limits.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Large SCOPF instances contain millions of continuous/integer variables and nonlinear nonconvex constraints, making them difficult to solve within challenge time limits.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained optimal power flow with multiple time steps, including AC power flow, contingencies, reserves, device switching, and ramping constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a decomposition-based hybrid solver scale multi-timestep SCOPF to very large grids while maintaining high-quality feasible solutions?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generation and consumption dispatch, device switching status, bus voltage angles, AC power-flow feasible operating point, and reserve allocations.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Two-stage DC/AC decomposition with sequential optimization for large networks.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: DC module uses linearized/MILP approximations; AC module solves full nonlinear AC power-flow equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Multiple time steps; sequential stage-wise optimization for large horizons.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Time-step based control horizon; exact interval length not specified.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Control horizon divided into stages for networks over 2000 buses.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Contingency constraints included; no stochastic or robust uncertainty model stated.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC OPF with reserves, ramping, device uptime/downtime, and switching constraints.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Problem reformulation, McCormick relaxation, slack variables, clique constraints, analytical derivatives, vectorization, and sequential bound updates.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Designed for scalability and strict time limits on very large instances.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Consumption devices represented with bid blocks and power consumption bounds.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Maximize total market surplus z over device powers, bus voltage angles, and switching variables.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Equality constraints G enforce power-balance and AC/DC network equations; inequality constraints H cover voltage limits, real/reactive power limits, reserves, ramping, switching, contingency, and device operation constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Device power pjt, bus voltage angle θit, switching status ujt, shunt conductance gshjt, branch flow limits smaxj, reserve factors σscrn, ramp-up Pru, ramp-down Prd, and mismatch penalty pit.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: DC subproblem solved as MILP with Gurobi; AC subproblem solved as NLP with IPOPT; large cases use sequential stage-wise optimization and selective contingency inclusion.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Evaluated on 300+ scenarios across 73 to 8316-bus networks from ARPA-E GO challenge datasets.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach achieved high scaled scores in most scenarios, with average scores around 0.983 on Scenario Set 3 and 0.9992 on Scenario Set 2, while meeting time limits.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalable, robust, high-quality solutions, full AC formulation. Limitation: solution quality varies by scenario and depends on available reserve abundance; large cases require sequential decomposition.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Applied to ARPA-E Grid Optimization Challenge 3 datasets and testing platform.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Sizing and Placement of Community Energy Storage Systems using Multi-Period Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Marcel Böhringer; Soham Choudhury; Sebastian Weck; Jutta Hanson
data_properties.hasInstitution: Technical University of Darmstadt, Department of Electrical Power Supply with Integration of Renewable Energy (E5), Darmstadt, Germany
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Size and place community energy storage and photovoltaic systems in a low-voltage district using multi-period optimal power flow.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Improve district self-sufficiency and reduce costs while respecting network constraints and PV/storage interactions.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Optimal sizing of CES and PV, and optimal CES placement in a residential low-voltage network under cost scenarios and self-sufficiency constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How do PV sizing, CES sizing, feed-in tariffs, and self-sufficiency requirements affect optimal storage placement and district economics?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal PV installation size, optimal CES capacity, CES placement node, time-resolved grid import and export, and network losses.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Multi-period OPF with sizing variables for PV and CES and placement analysis.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Low-voltage network OPF with real and reactive power outputs, voltages, phase angles, and network constraints.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Time-coupled multi-period formulation with inter-temporal storage energy balance.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Planning horizon over T periods; case study uses a day-resolved time series.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Residential low-voltage CIGRÉ network with PV, community storage, grid import/export, and self-sufficiency constraints.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Dimensioning strategy and receding-horizon placement strategy.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Placement mode minimizes network losses; sizing mode is cost-optimized.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Household load profiles are included and self-sufficiency limits grid import from community demand.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total imported-energy cost minus export revenue over time, plus amortized CES capacity cost and PV investment cost.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: CES energy balance, state-of-charge bounds, charge/discharge power limits, PV generation limits from irradiation and efficiency, self-sufficiency lower bound on grid import, and standard OPF network constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Grid import/export prices, CES CAPEX/OPEX, PV CAPEX/OPEX, interest rate, operating life, charging/discharging efficiencies, PV efficiency, irradiation profiles, household load profiles, and self-sufficiency rate.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Implemented in MATLAB R2019b with MATPOWER 7.0; MP-OPF adapted with added variables and constraints for the LV-CIGRÉ test grid.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on the CIGRÉ low-voltage residential subnetwork using synthetic load profiles, PV irradiation profiles, and three cost scenarios.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: High feed-in tariffs favor maximum PV and no CES; lower costs favor larger CES and smaller PV; optimal CES placement shifts with self-sufficiency level toward central low-impedance nodes.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Captures time-coupled storage and placement effects in LV grids, but omits seasonal variation, heat pumps, EVs, and alternative storage technologies.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses self-sufficiency rate to progressively exclude grid-supplied households from CES placement consideration.

data_properties.hasMotivation: Reduce total system cost and peak demand while preserving user convenience and accommodating renewable and demand uncertainty.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Multi-objective AC OPF with demand response, EV/HVAC aggregators, ESS, and renewable curtailment under network constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How can AC OPF coordinate demand response and flexible-load aggregators to lower cost and peaks without violating grid and comfort constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generation dispatch, demand response schedule, EV charging/discharging schedule, HVAC power consumption schedule, bus voltage profile, line power flows, load shedding, and renewable curtailment.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Multi-objective AC OPF coordinated with demand response, EV and HVAC aggregators, ESS, and renewable generation.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow with active/reactive balance, bus voltages, line flow limits, and transmission impedance equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: 24-hour scheduling with hourly intervals.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Scenario-based renewable uncertainty and LSTM-based load forecasting; EV energy and travel distance modeled with normal distribution.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Smart grid transmission network with thermal units, wind, solar, ESS, EVs, HVACs, and load shedding.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Solved as MINLP in GAMS with CONOPT3; TOPSIS used to select the preferred DR step.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Evaluated on modified IEEE 24-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems; reports cost, peak reduction, voltage variation, and execution time.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Demand response for large flexible loads plus aggregated EV and HVAC loads with comfort and participation limits.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total cost including generation cost, load shedding cost, and wind/solar curtailment cost; minimize voltage deviation; maximize DR revenue, peak reduction, and user convenience.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Thermal unit active/reactive limits and ramping; load shedding bounds; ESS and EV charge/discharge and energy limits; wind/solar availability and curtailment; AC power balance and line flow limits; DR bounds and constant power-factor load shifting; HVAC temperature dynamics and comfort bounds.
data_properties.usesParameter: Fuel-cost coefficients bg,cg; VOLL, VOLW, VOLS; generator limits Pg/Qg and ramp rates; line susceptance b and impedance Zij; load baselines PL0, QL0; DR factor α; ESS/EV efficiencies and capacities; renewable availabilities wt, st; HVAC thermal coefficients k1–k4; temperature limits; LMP λ.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Formulated in GAMS as a mixed-integer nonlinear program and solved with CONOPT3; scenario results were weighted by probabilities and ranked with TOPSIS.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 24-bus and 118-bus systems using 12 renewable scenarios and DR steps from 0% to 25%.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: At 20% DR, the model achieved the best TOPSIS outcome, reducing total cost and peak demand while keeping voltages within limits.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: integrates AC OPF, DR, EV/HVAC aggregators, storage, and uncertainty. Limitation: aggregator placement was assumed, not optimized.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses both active and reactive demand response with user-convenience and comfort-aware flexible-load scheduling.

data_properties.hasModelName: Distributed System Level Control MTDC Grids
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Distributed OPF Algorithm for System-Level Control of Active Multi-Terminal DC Distribution Grids
data_properties.hasAuthor: Asimenia Korompili; Petros Pandis; Antonello Monti
data_properties.hasInstitution: Institute for Automation of Complex Power Systems, E.ON Energy Research Center, RWTH Aachen University, Aachen, Germany
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Distributed OPF-based system-level control of MTDC distribution grids with DER coordination.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Need fast, scalable, modular, privacy-preserving control for MTDC grids with high DER integration and changing operating conditions.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Distributed solution of a nodal OPF-for-ANM problem for MTDC grids using ADMM and sequential convex approximation.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a distributed OPF algorithm coordinate diverse DER and provide nodal voltage set-points fast enough for system-level control in MTDC grids?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal nodal voltage set-points and DER power dispatch set-points; in simulations, nodal voltages and conventional DER power outputs are reported.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Distributed, modular nodal formulation with ADMM coordination and local convexified subproblems.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Nodal DC power-flow formulation with current, power-flow, and voltage variables; nonlinear power equations linearized by first-order Taylor approximation.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Repeated at each control period.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single-period, receding control-period optimization.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses measured available RES power and current ESS SoC; no explicit stochastic or robust uncertainty model.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Multi-terminal DC distribution grids with DER, ESS, controllable loads, and interlinking converters.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: ADMM with sequential convex approximation and an added initialization step for time-varying DER parameters.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Evaluated for convergence speed, parallel computation time, communication time, scalability, and online cluster execution.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Controllable loads can curtail demand with quadratic curtailment costs and bounds.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize conventional DER operating costs plus ADMM consensus penalty terms; ANM schemes add RES priority terms, ESS virtual-cost terms, or load-curtailment cost terms.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Nodal current, line-current, nodal power balance, nonlinear power-flow equalities, and bounds on generation, line flows, voltages, ESS energy, ESS charge/discharge exclusivity, and load curtailment.
data_properties.usesParameter: Penalty parameter ρ; voltage and power tolerances εV and εP; RES availability p̄RES; ESS SoC EESS,Ti and thresholds; charging/discharging efficiencies nch, ndisch; nodal price prk; load-curtailment factors aCL, bCL, cCL; priority factors priorRES and priorESS.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Each DCU solves its local nodal subproblem, exchanges voltage copies with neighbors, updates consensus voltages and dual variables, and stops when voltage convergence and total power balance are satisfied.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on modified IEEE 14, 30, 57, and 118-node systems, including sequential and physically distributed HPC-cluster implementations.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The algorithm converges in a few hundred iterations, remains scalable across network sizes, and can dispatch diverse DER under different ANM schemes with acceptable voltage deviations from centralized solutions.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: distributed, modular, scalable, privacy-preserving, fast. Limitations: relies on linearized OPF, assumes normal communication operation, and communication time can dominate total execution time.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Suitable for system-level control of DER-dominated MTDC grids and adaptable to equivalent AC-grid OPF-for-ANM formulations.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：与用户需求高度一致，明确满足多时段混合AC/DC-OPF、灵活性市场清算、TSO-DSO协调，以及分布网侧SOC-ACOPF与输电网侧DC-OPF的分层结构，并显式包含电池、灵活负荷、负荷转移和负荷削减。 / English: Highly consistent with the user requirement; it explicitly satisfies multi-period hybrid AC/DC-OPF, flexibility market clearing, TSO-DSO coordination, and the layered SOC-ACOPF on the distribution side with DC-OPF on the transmission side, while explicitly including batteries, flexible loads, load shifting, and load shedding.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：主要限制是采用集中式两阶段日前/15分钟优化，且未进一步扩展到多DSO或无功灵活性交换。 / English: Main limitation is that it uses a centralized two-stage day-ahead/15-minute optimization and does not extend to multiple DSOs or reactive-power flexibility exchange.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：仅部分符合多时段调度这一点，但核心是常规AC-OPF日前/实时调度，不满足用户明确要求的传输网DC-OPF与配电网SOC-ACOPF混合结构，也未显式建模电池、负荷转移和负荷削减作为灵活性资源。 / English: It only partially matches the multi-interval scheduling aspect, but its core is a conventional AC-OPF day-ahead/real-time scheduling model, which does not meet the explicit requirement for a transmission DC-OPF plus distribution SOC-ACOPF hybrid structure, and it does not explicitly model batteries, load shifting, and load shedding as flexibility resources.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：缺少用户要求的混合传输-配电分层OPF结构，并且灵活性资源建模不完整。 / English: It lacks the requested hybrid transmission-distribution layered OPF structure, and its flexibility-resource modeling is incomplete.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：满足多时间步与跨时段安全约束OPF的方向，但它是DC/AC分解的安全约束OPF，不是用户要求的“输电网DC-OPF + 配电网SOC-ACOPF”混合协调模型，也没有面向灵活性市场清算的电池、柔性负荷、负荷转移/削减的显式建模重点。 / English: It matches the multi-time-step and security-constrained OPF direction, but it is a DC/AC decomposition SCOPF rather than the requested hybrid transmission DC-OPF plus distribution SOC-ACOPF coordination model, and it does not focus on explicit batteries, flexible loads, load shifting, or load shedding for flexibility market clearing.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：缺少明确的传输-配电混合分层结构，且灵活性市场清算与需求侧灵活资源建模不足。 / English: It lacks the explicit transmission-distribution hybrid layered structure, and its flexibility market-clearing plus demand-side flexibility modeling is insufficient.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：具备多时段与储能时序耦合，能覆盖部分灵活性资源调度需求，但其目标是低压配电网中的储能/PV选址定容，不是用户要求的传输-配电协同混合AC/DC-OPF，也没有SOC-ACOPF/DC-OPF分层结构或灵活性市场清算机制。 / English: It has multi-period coupling and storage temporal dynamics, covering part of the flexibility-resource scheduling need, but its purpose is storage/PV sizing and placement in a low-voltage distribution grid, not the requested transmission-distribution hybrid AC/DC-OPF, and it does not provide SOC-ACOPF/DC-OPF layering or flexibility market-clearing mechanics.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：应用场景与模型结构都偏离用户要求，缺少输电侧DC-OPF、协调清算和完整灵活性资源集合。 / English: Both the application setting and model structure deviate from the user requirement, lacking transmission-side DC-OPF, coordinated clearing, and the full flexibility-resource set.

checked_candidates.consistency_check: 中文：它很好地覆盖了需求响应、储能、EV/HVAC聚合器、负荷削减和负荷转移等灵活性资源，并且是多时段优化，但仍然是单一AC-OPF需求响应模型，不满足用户明确要求的传输网DC-OPF与配电网SOC-ACOPF混合耦合以及TSO-DSO协调市场清算。 / English: It covers demand response, storage, EV/HVAC aggregators, load shedding, and load shifting very well, and it is multi-period, but it remains a single AC-OPF demand-response model and does not satisfy the explicit requirement for a hybrid transmission DC-OPF plus distribution SOC-ACOPF coupling with TSO-DSO coordination and market clearing.
checked_candidates.violation_or_gap: 中文：灵活性资源较全，但缺少用户要求的混合传输-配电OPF架构与协调清算机制。 / English: The flexibility resources are broad, but it lacks the requested hybrid transmission-distribution OPF architecture and coordinated clearing mechanism.

requirement.requirement_name: Dynamic security-constrained AC-OPF with neural encoding
requirement.requirement_text: A model capable of handling dynamic security-constrained AC-OPF is needed. Traditional AC-OPF can consider static constraints, but directly adding dynamic security constraints such as small-signal stability and transient stability makes the problem difficult to solve. Therefore, neural networks are needed to encode the feasible region and transform it into a MILP for solution.

data_properties.hasModelName: Neural Networks Encoding Dynamic Security Constrained AC OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Neural Networks for Encoding Dynamic Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Ilgiz Murzakhanov; Andreas Venzke; George S. Misyris; Spyros Chatzivasileiadis
data_properties.hasInstitution: Technical University of Denmark
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Encode dynamic security constraints into a tractable optimization model for AC optimal power flow.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Directly including dynamic security constraints makes AC-OPF intractable; the paper seeks a scalable alternative.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: AC optimal power flow with N-1 security and small-signal stability constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can neural networks encode the feasible space of dynamic security-constrained AC-OPF so it can be solved as a MILP?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Cost-optimal generator dispatch satisfying N-1 security and small-signal stability, with corresponding bus voltages and line flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Classification neural network encodes feasible operating points; exact mixed-integer reformulation with ReLU activations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow balance for the intact system; contingency-wise AC constraints for N-1 security.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single operating point; no multi-period horizon.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single snapshot dispatch.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: None explicit; random cost-function test instances only.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: N-1 security and small-signal stability constraints on an IEEE 14-bus system.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Neural-network feasibility encoding, exact MILP reformulation, and iterative linearization of power losses.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported 99% test accuracy; feasibility improved to 100% with epsilon adjustment.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost of the intact system state.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Generator active/reactive limits, voltage magnitude limits, line-flow limits, AC power balance, preventive generator set-point equality across contingencies, eigenvalue-based small-signal stability damping ratio constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator active and reactive limits, voltage limits, line-flow limits, contingency set C, damping threshold gamma_min, neural-network weights and biases, ReLU bounds, epsilon conservativeness parameter, loss-linearization threshold rho.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Train a ReLU classification network on feasible/infeasible operating points, reformulate it exactly as MILP, and iteratively linearize AC losses to solve MILPs with Gurobi.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 14-bus system with 45,000 labeled samples; 99% test accuracy; compared against AC-OPF and N-1 security-constrained AC-OPF.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach obtained cost-optimal solutions satisfying both static and dynamic security constraints; epsilon increased feasibility to 100% with small cost increase.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: tractable MILP approximation and improved feasibility. Limitations: approximation error may cause optimality loss and separate networks are needed for different grids.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses a conservative feasibility margin epsilon to trade off feasibility and optimality.

data_properties.hasModelName: Real Time Sequential Security Constrained OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Real-Time Sequential Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow: A Hybrid Knowledge-Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning Approach
data_properties.hasAuthor: Zhongkai Yi; Xue Wang; Cheng Yang; Chao Yang; Mengyang Niu; Wotao Yin
data_properties.hasInstitution: Alibaba DAMO Academy; Alibaba US; Tsinghua University; Harbin Institute of Technology
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve sequential real-time security-constrained optimal power flow with fast dispatch decisions under inaccurate environmental parameters.
data_properties.hasMotivation: ACOPF is nonconvex, time-coupled by ramping limits, and difficult to solve quickly and safely when system parameters are inaccurate or contingencies are unexperienced.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Sequential security-constrained AC optimal power flow for real-time operation with generator active/reactive dispatch and network security limits.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a hybrid knowledge-data-driven reinforcement learning method produce safe real-time OPF dispatches efficiently without relying on accurate environmental models?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Safe generator active and reactive power dispatch commands; resulting bus voltage magnitudes and branch active/reactive power flows within limits.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid knowledge-data-driven reinforcement learning with a safety-layer projection model and inactive-constraint identification.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow formulation with nonlinear nodal injections, branch flows, voltage magnitudes, and ramping-coupled generator limits.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Sequential multi-step dispatch with future load forecasts and ramping-coupled time dependence.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Real-time operation over time slots; forecasting horizon T steps.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Infinite-horizon sequential decision process terminated by grid failure/non-convergence.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses reinforcement learning for inaccurate environments and updates safety-layer parameters from latest measurements.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained ACOPF with coordinated active and reactive power dispatch, voltage and branch-flow security limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Improved SAC with SAM, prioritized replay, adaptive entropy, hybrid safety layer, and inactive-constraint elimination.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Claims faster decision-making and reduced security violations with comparable economic performance.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Includes forecasted net load demand in the state; no explicit demand response control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize cumulative generation operating cost, with quadratic cost coefficients for each generator over time.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power-balance equations, branch active/reactive flow equations, generator active/reactive limits, branch flow limits, voltage magnitude limits, and ramping-coupled generator bounds; safety-layer projection also enforces linearized security constraints and power balance.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients; generator active/reactive bounds and ramping limits; bus voltages; line conductance/susceptance or resistance/reactance; branch flow limits; load demand and forecasted load; slack-bus limits; penalty coefficients; SAC temperature and learning rates.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Sequential decisions are produced by an improved soft actor-critic policy, then projected by a linear security layer initialized from linearized power-flow knowledge and updated with data; inactive constraints are removed analytically.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 30-bus and larger systems, including contingency and parameter-error scenarios, with comparisons against penalty, constrained-policy, and pure data-driven safety-layer baselines.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The method maintains voltages and branch flows within safe ranges, reduces violation times in early training and contingencies, and scales to larger systems with low decision time.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: safe real-time dispatch, better robustness to inaccurate models, and high computational efficiency. Limitation: safety layer uses linearized power-flow approximation and may need conservative limits to offset approximation error.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper also evaluates scalability on 9-, 30-, 57-, 118-, and 1187-bus systems.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Machine Learning-Aided Security Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Jubeyer Rahman; Cong Feng; Jie Zhang
data_properties.hasInstitution: The University of Texas at Dallas
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve security-constrained AC optimal power flow efficiently using a machine-learning-aided approach.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Full AC OPF is highly nonlinear and non-convex, making large-scale security-constrained solving computationally challenging.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained AC optimal power flow with switched shunt security constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a machine-learning-aided method predict key OPF variables and avoid running a physics-based OPF solver while preserving feasibility?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Bus voltage magnitudes and voltage angles; derived current injections, complex/real power injections, generator dispatch settings, and branch power flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid machine-learning-aided OPF using multi-input multi-output random forest plus physics-based network equations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with bus admittance matrix, current injection, apparent power, and nodal power balance.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period steady-state OPF.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Not specified; load samples from hourly ERCOT profile used for training/testing.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per case.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: No explicit uncertainty model; trained on sampled load cases.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC transmission OPF with generators, buses, branches, and switched shunts.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Multi-input multi-output random forest predicts voltages, then network equations recover remaining variables.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported zero constraint violation for the proposed method and much faster solution time than MATPOWER MIPS.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Load demand inputs Pd and Qd are used as predictors; no demand response model.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator costs represented by individual piece-wise linear cost functions.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Voltage magnitude and angle bounds; generator active/reactive power bounds; switched shunt susceptance bounds; real and reactive nodal power balance equations; branch apparent power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes vi and angles θi; generator outputs pg and qg; switched shunt susceptance bcs; real/reactive demands pd and qd; branch flow limit sf; bus admittance matrix Y; generator cost cg.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: RF is trained on converged MATPOWER solutions; case I predicts v and θ then computes injections and costs via network equations; case II predicts all OPF variables directly.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on a 500-bus GO competition network using 8,760 load samples; compared against MATPOWER MIPS and a pure ML baseline.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method closely matches MIPS voltage solutions, satisfies network constraints, and reduces total solution time from 2030.4 s to 35.26 s.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: fast and feasible OPF approximation without running a physics-based solver. Limitation: pure end-to-end ML still causes many equality-constraint violations.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Potentially useful for post-contingency analysis with many network topologies and load profiles.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Minimize generation cost in AC optimal power flow while satisfying network constraints under uncertain loads and renewable generation with probabilistic guarantees.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Classical OPF dispatch is rigid and can become inefficient or infeasible under renewable and load uncertainty, causing overloads and outages.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Robust and chance-constrained AC optimal power flow with uncertain loads and renewable generators.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How can AC-OPF be solved efficiently under uncertainty while limiting the probability of violating generation and transmission constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal controllable generation dispatch, generator voltage magnitudes, deployment vector, and corresponding bus voltage and line-flow-feasible operating point.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Scenario-with-certificates formulation combined with convex SDP relaxation of AC power flow.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power balance equations with voltage-magnitude and line-flow constraints via lifted matrix W.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period OPF repeated over hourly demand scenarios in experiments.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per solve; 24 hourly solves in simulation.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Probabilistic uncertainty in loads and renewable generation using scenario with certificates and chance constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Includes renewable generators, uncertain loads, generator participation factors, voltage limits, and transmission limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Convex relaxation plus randomized scenario-with-certificates sampling.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: A priori probabilistic guarantee on constraint-violation risk; exact for a restricted class of networks.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uncertain loads are explicitly modeled and balanced through generator deployment factors.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost f(u); in the penalized variant, worst-case cost adds reactive-power and line-loss penalties.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power balance equalities; generator active/reactive limits; voltage magnitude bounds; line-voltage-difference or apparent-flow limits; deployment factors sum to one and remain nonnegative.
data_properties.usesParameter: Uncertain complex load and renewable deviations δ; deployment vector α; bus-voltage matrix W split into Wu and Wx; risk levels ε and β; line admittances ylm; voltage and power limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Uses SDP lifting W=VV* and scenario-with-certificates sampling to solve a convex program; implemented with YALMIP and Mosek.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on the New England 39-bus system with Monte Carlo testing over 10,000 samples and comparison against nominal OPF and a prior probabilistic AC-OPF method.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method greatly reduced infeasible samples and line-flow violations versus nominal OPF, while using far fewer scenario samples than the compared parameterized approach.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: less conservative, probabilistic guarantees, computationally efficient, and exact for some networks. Limitation: exactness is only proven for a restrictive network class.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Can incorporate N-1 security constraints and outage probabilities within the same scenario framework.

requirement.requirement_name: Scalable N-k SCOPF with adversarial robustness
requirement.requirement_text: A scalable N-k SCOPF method is needed so that dispatch decisions can withstand multiple simultaneous equipment failures. Traditional N-k SCOPF becomes difficult to solve because contingency combinations explode combinatorially. Therefore, the model should treat contingencies as adversarial attacks and use minimax optimization with implicit differentiation to find more robust dispatch decisions.

data_properties.hasInstitution: iTrust Center for Research in Cyber Security, Singapore University of Technology and Design; CNR-IEIIT, Torino, Italy; Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Penn State University
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Minimize generation cost in AC optimal power flow while satisfying network constraints under uncertain loads and renewable generation with probabilistic guarantees.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Classical OPF dispatch is rigid and can become inefficient or infeasible under renewable and load uncertainty, causing overloads and outages.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Robust and chance-constrained AC optimal power flow with uncertain loads and renewable generators.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How can AC-OPF be solved efficiently under uncertainty while limiting the probability of violating generation and transmission constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal controllable generation dispatch, generator voltage magnitudes, deployment vector, and corresponding bus voltage and line-flow-feasible operating point.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Scenario-with-certificates formulation combined with convex SDP relaxation of AC power flow.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power balance equations with voltage-magnitude and line-flow constraints via lifted matrix W.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period OPF repeated over hourly demand scenarios in experiments.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per solve; 24 hourly solves in simulation.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Probabilistic uncertainty in loads and renewable generation using scenario with certificates and chance constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Includes renewable generators, uncertain loads, generator participation factors, voltage limits, and transmission limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Convex relaxation plus randomized scenario-with-certificates sampling.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: A priori probabilistic guarantee on constraint-violation risk; exact for a restricted class of networks.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uncertain loads are explicitly modeled and balanced through generator deployment factors.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost f(u); in the penalized variant, worst-case cost adds reactive-power and line-loss penalties.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power balance equalities; generator active/reactive limits; voltage magnitude bounds; line-voltage-difference or apparent-flow limits; deployment factors sum to one and remain nonnegative.
data_properties.usesParameter: Uncertain complex load and renewable deviations δ; deployment vector α; bus-voltage matrix W split into Wu and Wx; risk levels ε and β; line admittances ylm; voltage and power limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Uses SDP lifting W=VV* and scenario-with-certificates sampling to solve a convex program; implemented with YALMIP and Mosek.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on the New England 39-bus system with Monte Carlo testing over 10,000 samples and comparison against nominal OPF and a prior probabilistic AC-OPF method.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method greatly reduced infeasible samples and line-flow violations versus nominal OPF, while using far fewer scenario samples than the compared parameterized approach.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: less conservative, probabilistic guarantees, computationally efficient, and exact for some networks. Limitation: exactness is only proven for a restrictive network class.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Can incorporate N-1 security constraints and outage probabilities within the same scenario framework.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To advocate and outline grid foundation models for power-system operations, planning, and control.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Increasing grid complexity and uncertainty from the energy transition, climate change, aging infrastructure, and cybersecurity threats.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Lack of scalable, transferable AI methods for diverse power-grid tasks and power-flow-related applications.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can foundation models be developed for electric power grids to generalize across grid data and accelerate downstream applications such as power flow and OPF?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: No OPF model is solved in this paper; it proposes a GridFM-v0 concept for reconstructing power-flow states and, in discussed downstream use, optimal generation dispatch and objective values.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Graph neural network-based foundation model concept; masked autoencoder pre-training on graph-structured grid data.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow reconstruction on graph nodes with bus variables and line/transformer edges.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Initially single-time-step power-flow data; extendable to multiple consecutive time steps for forecasting.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Single time step in the near-term model; high-resolution PMU data mentioned for dynamic extensions.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Not specified; near-term focus is static power-flow applications.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses diverse topologies, load conditions, perturbations, and synthetic scenarios; discusses scenario trees and stochastic programming.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Transmission and distribution grid applications including power flow, OPF, contingency analysis, state estimation, stability, control, planning, and cybersecurity.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Self-supervised masked graph autoencoding with physics-informed loss; intended to speed up power-flow-related computation.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Projected 3–4 orders-of-magnitude speed-up over conventional power-flow solvers; less than 1% error cited from related GNN work.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Mentions load conditions, load forecasting, electric vehicles, heating electrification, and demand uncertainty.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: For OPF use, minimize generation costs by reconstructing generator power; the paper does not present a full OPF mathematical formulation.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Reconstructed node variables must satisfy power-flow equations and bounds such as generator capacity constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus active power, reactive power, voltage magnitude, voltage angle; line and transformer connectivity; topology, load conditions, and power-flow solutions.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: GridFM-v0 is proposed as a masked graph autoencoder pre-trained on solved power-flow cases from multiple topologies and load conditions, then fine-tuned for downstream tasks.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: No direct model validation results are reported for GridFM-v0; validation is proposed on open datasets and later on utility data behind firewalls.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The paper argues GridFMs could generalize across grid tasks and substantially accelerate power-system analysis, especially power-flow-related applications.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalability, adaptability, and simulation acceleration. Limitations: data availability, privacy, trust, and difficulty accessing operational grid data.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper is a perspective proposing a roadmap rather than presenting a completed OPF solver.

removed_candidates.removal_reason: 仅支持单时段的N-1安全约束AC SCOPF，并未体现将多重同时故障作为对抗攻击进行minimax优化或通过隐式微分求解，因此与用户要求的可扩展N-k对抗鲁棒SCOPF不一致 / It only supports single-period N-1 security-constrained AC SCOPF and does not implement contingencies as adversarial attacks with minimax optimization or implicit differentiation, so it does not match the requested scalable N-k adversarially robust SCOPF.

该模型面向N-1动态安全约束与小信号稳定性，并通过神经网络编码后转化为MILP求解，没有针对多重同时故障的N-k SCOPF，也没有对抗式minimax与隐式微分机制 / This model targets N-1 dynamic security constraints and small-signal stability, reformulates the problem as a MILP via neural-network encoding, and does not address multi-outage N-k SCOPF or adversarial minimax with implicit differentiation.

该方法是基于DRL的预防式N-1 SCOPF快速求解器，核心是离线训练加在线推理，并未将多重故障建模为对抗攻击，也未采用minimax优化或隐式微分来处理N-k组合爆炸 / This method is a DRL-based preventive N-1 SCOPF fast solver with offline training and online inference, but it does not model multiple failures as adversarial attacks or use minimax optimization and implicit differentiation to handle N-k combinatorial explosion.

该模型处理的是不确定负荷和可再生出力下的概率鲁棒AC-OPF，属于机会约束/场景法框架，不是针对多设备同时失效的N-k SCOPF对抗式最坏情形优化 / This model addresses probabilistically robust AC-OPF under uncertain loads and renewable generation using chance-constraint/scenario methods, not adversarial worst-case optimization for multiple simultaneous equipment failures in N-k SCOPF.

该记录是面向电网基础模型的研究构想，并未给出可执行的SCOPF求解器，更没有针对N-k安全约束、对抗攻击建模、minimax优化或隐式微分的具体方法 / This record is a foundation-model concept for power grids and does not provide an executable SCOPF solver, nor a concrete method for N-k security constraints, adversarial attack modeling, minimax optimization, or implicit differentiation.

raw_consistency.overall_summary: 保留的候选中，Adversarially_Robust_Learning_Security_Constrained_Optimal_Power_Flow 与用户要求最一致，因为它明确面向N-k SCOPF的组合爆炸问题，并采用对抗式鲁棒学习框架；其余被移除的模型要么仅覆盖N-1安全约束，要么是概率鲁棒/多时段/基础模型构想，缺少用户要求的多重故障对抗式minimax与隐式微分核心能力 / Among the candidates, Adversarially_Robust_Learning_Security_Constrained_Optimal_Power_Flow is the most consistent with the request because it explicitly targets the combinatorial N-k SCOPF problem with an adversarially robust learning framework; the removed models either only cover N-1 security, or are probabilistic robust/multi-step/foundation-model concepts lacking the requested core adversarial minimax and implicit-differentiation capability.

top_rows.Requirement name: Scalable N-k SCOPF with adversarial robustness
top_rows.Requirement text: A scalable N-k SCOPF method is needed so that dispatch decisions can withstand multiple simultaneous equipment failures. Traditional N-k SCOPF becomes difficult to solve because contingency combinations explode combinatorially. Therefore, the model should treat contingencies as adversarial attacks and use minimax optimization with implicit differentiation to find more robust dispatch decisions.

top_rows.Recommendation reason: 该模型在“可扩展性”和“安全约束 OPF”方面很强，适合大规模、多时间步的 SCOPF 场景；其 hasConstraintFunction 明确包含 ContingencyPostContingencyOperationConstraint，说明它考虑了故障后的运行约束。不过它的核心方法是两阶段 DC/AC 分解与顺序优化，而不是把 contingencies 作为 adversarial attacks 的 minimax 鲁棒建模，因此与用户要求的算法思想只有部分重合。 / This model is strong on scalability and security-constrained OPF, making it suitable for large multi-time-step SCOPF settings; its hasConstraintFunction explicitly includes ContingencyPostContingencyOperationConstraint, showing post-contingency operating constraints are considered. However, its core method is two-stage DC/AC decomposition and sequential optimization rather than minimax robust modeling that treats contingencies as adversarial attacks, so it only partially matches the requested algorithmic idea.
top_rows.Matched needs: 匹配 scalable、SCOPF、多时间步、故障后约束、适合大规模系统 / Matches scalability, SCOPF, multi-time-step operation, post-contingency constraints, and large-system applicability.
top_rows.Strengths: hasPrimaryPurpose 强调在严格时间限制下高效求解大规模 SCOPF；hasFurtherProperty 指出可用于 2000+ bus 网络；hasSolutionDetailsSummary 采用 DC MILP + AC NLP 的分解与顺序阶段优化，体现强扩展性；hasConstraintFunction 覆盖 contingency、reserve、ramping、switching 与 AC power flow，说明它能处理复杂运行约束。 / hasPrimaryPurpose emphasizes efficient solution of large-scale SCOPF under strict time limits; hasFurtherProperty indicates applicability to 2000+ bus networks; hasSolutionDetailsSummary uses DC MILP + AC NLP decomposition and sequential stage-wise optimization, demonstrating strong scalability; hasConstraintFunction covers contingencies, reserves, ramping, switching, and AC power flow, indicating it handles rich operational constraints.
top_rows.Limitations: 该模型的 contingency 处理更偏向显式约束与分解求解，没有体现将 contingency 视为对抗攻击的鲁棒最小最大结构；同时其目标是市场剩余最大化而非直接面向“更鲁棒的调度对抗优化”，因此在用户指定的鲁棒建模范式上不如第一候选贴合。 / Its contingency handling is more about explicit constraints and decomposition-based solving, without showing an adversarial-attack-based robust minimax structure; additionally, its objective is market surplus maximization rather than directly targeting robust adversarial dispatch optimization, so it is less aligned with the requested robust modeling paradigm than the first candidate.
top_rows.Objective text: Maximize total market surplus z over device powers, bus voltage angles, and switching variables.
top_rows.Constraint text: Equality constraints G enforce power-balance and AC/DC network equations; inequality constraints H cover voltage limits, real/reactive power limits, reserves, ramping, switching, contingency, and device operation constraints.
top_rows.Parameter text: Device power pjt, bus voltage angle θit, switching status ujt, shunt conductance gshjt, branch flow limits smaxj, reserve factors σscrn, ramp-up Pru, ramp-down Prd, and mismatch penalty pit.
top_rows.Mathematical problem types: MixedIntegerLinearProgrammingProblem | Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Problem; NonlinearProgrammingProblem | Nonlinear Programming Problem

top_rows.Requirement name: Scalable N-k SCOPF with adversarial robustness
top_rows.Requirement text: A scalable N-k SCOPF method is needed so that dispatch decisions can withstand multiple simultaneous equipment failures. Traditional N-k SCOPF becomes difficult to solve because contingency combinations explode combinatorially. Therefore, the model should treat contingencies as adversarial attacks and use minimax optimization with implicit differentiation to find more robust dispatch decisions.
top_rows.Model name: Real Time Sequential Security Constrained OPF
top_rows.Paper title: Real-Time Sequential Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow: A Hybrid Knowledge-Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning Approach
top_rows.Recommendation reason: 该模型适合实时、序列式安全约束 OPF，并且强调在参数不准确和未见过的工况下保持安全，具有一定鲁棒性；但它的重点是强化学习与安全层投影，而不是 N-k 多重故障的对抗式 minimax 建模，因此与用户需求的核心方法差距最大。 / This model is suitable for real-time sequential security-constrained OPF and emphasizes safety under inaccurate parameters and unseen conditions, giving it some robustness; however, its focus is reinforcement learning with a safety-layer projection rather than adversarial minimax modeling for N-k multiple contingencies, so it is the furthest from the user's core method requirement.
top_rows.Matched needs: 匹配实时调度、序列决策、对不准确参数的鲁棒性、AC 安全约束 / Matches real-time dispatch, sequential decision-making, robustness to inaccurate parameters, and AC security constraints.
top_rows.Strengths: hasPrimaryPurpose 指向实时快速调度；hasTimeHorizonFeature 与 hasOptimizationHorizon 支持多步序列决策；hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature 说明可应对不准确环境；hasConstraintFunction 包含 ACPowerBalanceConstraint、LineFlowAndCapacityConstraint、VoltageAngleOperatingBoundaryConstraint 与 ContingencyPostContingencyOperationConstraint，说明它确实考虑安全与故障后约束。 / hasPrimaryPurpose targets fast real-time dispatch; hasTimeHorizonFeature and hasOptimizationHorizon support multi-step sequential decisions; hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature indicates it can handle inaccurate environments; hasConstraintFunction includes ACPowerBalanceConstraint, LineFlowAndCapacityConstraint, VoltageAngleOperatingBoundaryConstraint, and ContingencyPostContingencyOperationConstraint, showing it does consider security and post-contingency constraints.
top_rows.Limitations: 该模型的核心是 hybrid reinforcement learning + safety layer，而不是针对 N-k contingency 的显式鲁棒优化；其 hasSolutionDetailsSummary 也表明安全层依赖线性化潮流近似，这与用户希望的“把 contingencies 当作 adversarial attacks 并用 minimax 优化”不一致，且对多重同时故障的专门建模不突出。 / The core is hybrid reinforcement learning plus a safety layer rather than explicit robust optimization for N-k contingencies; its hasSolutionDetailsSummary also shows the safety layer relies on linearized power-flow approximation, which does not match the user's desired “treat contingencies as adversarial attacks and use minimax optimization” approach, and it does not prominently model multiple simultaneous outages.
top_rows.Objective text: Minimize cumulative generation operating cost, with quadratic cost coefficients for each generator over time.
top_rows.Constraint text: AC power-balance equations, branch active/reactive flow equations, generator active/reactive limits, branch flow limits, voltage magnitude limits, and ramping-coupled generator bounds; safety-layer projection also enforces linearized security constraints and power balance.
top_rows.Parameter text: Generator cost coefficients; generator active/reactive bounds and ramping limits; bus voltages; line conductance/susceptance or resistance/reactance; branch flow limits; load demand and forecasted load; slack-bus limits; penalty coefficients; SAC temperature and learning rates.

requirement.requirement_text: An online optimization framework is needed for power systems with high renewable penetration. Wind, photovoltaic generation, and controllable loads fluctuate strongly, while offline optimization based on forecasts or historical data can produce suboptimal, infeasible, or unstable decisions. Therefore, the model should update with real-time operating states through online optimization.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Online Optimization in Power Systems With High Penetration of Renewable Generation: Advances and Prospects
data_properties.hasAuthor: Zhaojian Wang; Wei Wei; John Zhen Fu Pang; Feng Liu; Bo Yang; Xinping Guan; Shengwei Mei
data_properties.hasInstitution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Tsinghua University; Institute of High Performance Computing (A*STAR), Singapore
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Review and compare online optimization techniques for power-system operation under high renewable penetration.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Increasing renewable variability and controllable loads make offline optimization less reliable for real-time power-system operation.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: How to classify and apply online optimization methods to dynamic control, single-period OPF/voltage regulation, and multi-period energy management problems.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Which online optimization paradigms are most suitable for different power-system time scales and operational settings?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Not applicable; this is a review paper rather than a solved OPF model.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Review of optimization-guided dynamic control, feedback optimization, Lyapunov optimization, and online convex optimization.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Discusses AC bus-injection and branch-flow models; linearized DC power flow and DistFlow approximations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Covers single-period and multi-period formulations, plus fast dynamic-control time scales.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Seconds to minutes for dynamic control; single-period and multi-period decision settings.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single-period and multi-period; some Lyapunov examples use finite or infinite horizons.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Addresses renewable variability and uncertainty through online decision-making without relying on forecasts or historical distributions.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Frequency control, voltage regulation, OPF, economic dispatch, energy storage scheduling, demand response, and power markets.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Compares feedback-based, primal-dual, ADMM, Newton-Raphson, Lyapunov, and OCO methods; discusses distributed and asynchronous variants.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Emphasizes fast response, tracking of time-varying conditions, and reduced computational burden.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Includes controllable loads, demand response, electric vehicles, and load-side frequency control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Examples include minimizing generation cost in OPF, regulation cost in frequency control, and long-term average cost in Lyapunov/OCO formulations.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Power-flow equations, voltage limits, generation and reactive-power bounds, power-balance constraints, line congestion, storage SoC and charging/discharging limits, ramping and other coupled constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generation cost coefficients ai, bi; voltage bounds vi; power injection bounds Pi, Qi; line parameters rij, xij, Bij; storage queue/SoC Qt; Lyapunov weight ρ; stepsize η; control gains.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: The paper reviews algorithmic frameworks and representative formulations; it does not present a single new solved OPF instance.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: No dedicated validation of a new OPF model; cites prior experimental and numerical studies in the reviewed literature.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: Online optimization is useful for volatile power systems because it can track changing conditions and avoid reliance on inaccurate forecasts.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: fast, measurement-driven, and suitable for time-varying systems. Limitations: problem-dependent, often lacks a unified theory, and some methods need communication or predictions.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper is a survey and taxonomy of online optimization methods in power systems.
data_properties.hasSourceFileName: Online Optimization in Power Systems With.pdf

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Estimating Global Variables in Multi-agent Distributed OPF with Unreliable Communication
data_properties.hasAuthor: Masoud Bashari; Mikhak Samadi; Javad Zare; Ashkan Rahimi-Kian
data_properties.hasInstitution: IEMS Group Ltd.; University of Ottawa
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve distributed optimal power flow under unreliable communication by estimating exchanged global variables.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Communication link disruptions can prevent consensus exchange in distributed OPF and degrade convergence and feasibility.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Distributed OPF across multiple regions with lost or interrupted communication links between agents.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can predictive estimation of missing consensus messages preserve feasible D-OPF convergence when communication is interrupted?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Regional bus voltage magnitudes and phase angles, weighted-average global bus voltages, and convergence of D-OPF results across iterations.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Multi-agent distributed OPF with coordinator-agent consensus and predictive estimation of missing exchanged variables.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Region-based OPF coupled through tie-line voltage consensus and line power-flow equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Iterative multi-region consensus over repeated ADMM iterations.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Handles unreliable communication by estimating missing consensus messages with a trained DFNN.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: IEEE 14-bus transmission network partitioned into three regions with PV units and a BESS.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Extended ADMM combined with a shallow feedforward neural-network estimator for missing messages.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Faster convergence to actual global variables and feasible D-OPF results under interrupted links.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost for each region/sub-network.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Regional OPF constraints are enforced through bus-voltage and tie-line coupling; line power flows are updated from estimated voltages and consensus variables.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes and phase angles, tie-line voltages, line impedances, line currents, regional loads S_i,j^t, PV units, and BESS size.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: IEEE 14-bus case split into three areas; ADMM iterations compute regional OPF, estimate missing voltages with DFNN, average exchanged voltages, and update line flows.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Compared three scenarios: normal communication, lost bus-5 communication, and lost communication recovered by estimation; tested on IEEE 14-bus case.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: With DFNN-based estimation, interrupted-link cases converged closer to global voltages and faster than the unrecovered communication-loss case.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: improves distributed OPF feasibility and convergence under communication loss. Limitation: estimator still shows biased error and needs more training data.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: ANN/DFNN estimator trained on OPF data generated from 90%–100% loading scenarios.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Optimal Power Flow Using Graph Neural Networks
data_properties.hasAuthor: Damian Owerko; Fernando Gama; Alejandro Ribeiro
data_properties.hasInstitution: University of Pennsylvania, Department of Electrical and Systems Engineering
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Approximate AC optimal power flow solutions with a local, scalable graph neural network trained by imitation learning.
data_properties.hasMotivation: ACOPF is non-convex and costly to solve, and existing approximate methods do not scale well to large power networks.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: AC optimal power flow on power networks, using IEEE-30 and IEEE-118 test cases.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a graph neural network learn to imitate optimal ACOPF solutions accurately and efficiently in a decentralized, scalable way?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Estimated optimal generator active power outputs; evaluated against IPOPT ACOPF solutions.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Graph neural network parametrization with local message passing and scalable architecture.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow equations with nonlinear active and reactive power balance.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Training uses randomly sampled load scenarios from uniform ranges around reference loads.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Generator dispatch, bus voltages, active/reactive loads, and network topology on IEEE test systems.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Imitation learning with GNNs trained on IPOPT-generated optimal solutions.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported relative RMSE and much faster inference than IPOPT.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Loads are sampled as inputs; model predicts generator dispatch to meet demand.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator cost depending on active power output.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Active and reactive power balance equations p=P(v,δ;W), q=Q(v,δ;W), plus elementwise bounds Xmin ⪯ X ⪯ Xmax on voltages, angles, active and reactive powers.
data_properties.usesParameter: Network adjacency/weights W from line impedances; node states X=[v,δ,p,q]; generator selection matrix G; load vectors pL and qL; generator cost functions cm(pm).
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: IPOPT is used to solve ACOPF and generate training targets; GNNs are trained with MSE using ADAM on IEEE-30 and IEEE-118 datasets.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Evaluated on held-out test sets from IEEE-30 and IEEE-118; compared against global/local GNN and MLP baselines using relative RMSE.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: GNNs outperform MLP baselines, especially on the larger IEEE-118 case, and provide orders-of-magnitude faster inference than IPOPT.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: local, scalable, permutation-equivariant, and stable to graph perturbations. Limitation: trained to imitate IPOPT solutions rather than solve OPF exactly.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses graph convolution layers with K-hop neighborhood aggregation.

data_properties.hasModelName: Distributed System Level Control MTDC Grids
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Distributed OPF Algorithm for System-Level Control of Active Multi-Terminal DC Distribution Grids
data_properties.hasAuthor: Asimenia Korompili; Petros Pandis; Antonello Monti
data_properties.hasInstitution: Institute for Automation of Complex Power Systems, E.ON Energy Research Center, RWTH Aachen University, Aachen, Germany
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Distributed OPF-based system-level control of MTDC distribution grids with DER coordination.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Need fast, scalable, modular, privacy-preserving control for MTDC grids with high DER integration and changing operating conditions.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Distributed solution of a nodal OPF-for-ANM problem for MTDC grids using ADMM and sequential convex approximation.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a distributed OPF algorithm coordinate diverse DER and provide nodal voltage set-points fast enough for system-level control in MTDC grids?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal nodal voltage set-points and DER power dispatch set-points; in simulations, nodal voltages and conventional DER power outputs are reported.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Distributed, modular nodal formulation with ADMM coordination and local convexified subproblems.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Nodal DC power-flow formulation with current, power-flow, and voltage variables; nonlinear power equations linearized by first-order Taylor approximation.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Repeated at each control period.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single-period, receding control-period optimization.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses measured available RES power and current ESS SoC; no explicit stochastic or robust uncertainty model.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Multi-terminal DC distribution grids with DER, ESS, controllable loads, and interlinking converters.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: ADMM with sequential convex approximation and an added initialization step for time-varying DER parameters.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Evaluated for convergence speed, parallel computation time, communication time, scalability, and online cluster execution.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Controllable loads can curtail demand with quadratic curtailment costs and bounds.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize conventional DER operating costs plus ADMM consensus penalty terms; ANM schemes add RES priority terms, ESS virtual-cost terms, or load-curtailment cost terms.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Nodal current, line-current, nodal power balance, nonlinear power-flow equalities, and bounds on generation, line flows, voltages, ESS energy, ESS charge/discharge exclusivity, and load curtailment.
data_properties.usesParameter: Penalty parameter ρ; voltage and power tolerances εV and εP; RES availability p̄RES; ESS SoC EESS,Ti and thresholds; charging/discharging efficiencies nch, ndisch; nodal price prk; load-curtailment factors aCL, bCL, cCL; priority factors priorRES and priorESS.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Each DCU solves its local nodal subproblem, exchanges voltage copies with neighbors, updates consensus voltages and dual variables, and stops when voltage convergence and total power balance are satisfied.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on modified IEEE 14, 30, 57, and 118-node systems, including sequential and physically distributed HPC-cluster implementations.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The algorithm converges in a few hundred iterations, remains scalable across network sizes, and can dispatch diverse DER under different ANM schemes with acceptable voltage deviations from centralized solutions.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: distributed, modular, scalable, privacy-preserving, fast. Limitations: relies on linearized OPF, assumes normal communication operation, and communication time can dominate total execution time.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Suitable for system-level control of DER-dominated MTDC grids and adaptable to equivalent AC-grid OPF-for-ANM formulations.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: A Hybrid Data-Driven Method for Fast Solution of Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Ziming Yan; Yan Xu
data_properties.hasInstitution: Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Fast solution of preventive security-constrained optimal power flow using a hybrid data-driven DRL method
data_properties.hasMotivation: Conventional SCOPF solvers are computationally burdensome for online applications under contingencies and volatile operating conditions
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Preventive security-constrained optimal power flow with N-1 contingency constraints
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a hybrid model-assisted DRL method solve SCOPF rapidly while satisfying security constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal base-case dispatch decisions, including generator active power setpoints and generator-bus voltage setpoints, with contingency-feasible bus voltages and branch flows
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid data-driven, model-assisted deep reinforcement learning with primal-dual DDPG and interior-point/KKT gradient derivation
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations for base case and contingencies; sparse Jacobians and Hessians
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single operating point with multiple contingency scenarios
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Base case plus all considered contingencies
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Monte Carlo load-scenario generation for training data; no explicit stochastic optimization
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security constraints on generator limits, bus voltage magnitudes, and transmission line flows
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Closed-form actor gradients from KKT conditions; sparse matrix formulation; interior-point updates
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Real-time online inference after offline training; high-quality feasible solutions
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, defined as the sum of quadratic generator cost functions over the base case
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Equality constraints enforce AC power balance for base case and contingencies; inequality constraints enforce generator capacity, bus-voltage bounds, and transmission-line flow limits
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes and angles; generator active and reactive powers; base-case control variables vg and pg; contingency index k; contingency line outages; load states p and q; Lagrange multipliers; slack variables; learning rate
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Offline supervised initialization followed by DRL training using power-flow evaluations, KKT-based Newton steps, and sparse Jacobian/Hessian calculations; online stage outputs SCOPF controls directly
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on modified IEEE 57-bus, modified IEEE 300-bus, and ACTIVSg2000 systems with Monte Carlo load scenarios and critical contingencies
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method achieves near-benchmark operating cost, satisfies security constraints much better than supervised learning, and is orders of magnitude faster than IPOPT-based SCOPF
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: fast, constraint-aware, scalable to larger systems. Limitations: still slightly higher cost than IPOPT and some reactive-power violations may remain under contingencies
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Preventive SCOPF; model-assisted RL; contingency filtering used in experiments
