data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Probabilistically Robust AC Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Mohammadreza Chamanbaz; Fabrizio Dabbene; Constantino M. Lagoa
data_properties.hasInstitution: iTrust Center for Research in Cyber Security, Singapore University of Technology and Design; CNR-IEIIT, Torino, Italy; Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Penn State University
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Minimize generation cost in AC optimal power flow while satisfying network constraints under uncertain loads and renewable generation with probabilistic guarantees.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Classical OPF dispatch is rigid and can become inefficient or infeasible under renewable and load uncertainty, causing overloads and outages.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Robust and chance-constrained AC optimal power flow with uncertain loads and renewable generators.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How can AC-OPF be solved efficiently under uncertainty while limiting the probability of violating generation and transmission constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal controllable generation dispatch, generator voltage magnitudes, deployment vector, and corresponding bus voltage and line-flow-feasible operating point.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Scenario-with-certificates formulation combined with convex SDP relaxation of AC power flow.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power balance equations with voltage-magnitude and line-flow constraints via lifted matrix W.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period OPF repeated over hourly demand scenarios in experiments.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per solve; 24 hourly solves in simulation.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Probabilistic uncertainty in loads and renewable generation using scenario with certificates and chance constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Includes renewable generators, uncertain loads, generator participation factors, voltage limits, and transmission limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Convex relaxation plus randomized scenario-with-certificates sampling.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: A priori probabilistic guarantee on constraint-violation risk; exact for a restricted class of networks.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uncertain loads are explicitly modeled and balanced through generator deployment factors.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost f(u); in the penalized variant, worst-case cost adds reactive-power and line-loss penalties.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power balance equalities; generator active/reactive limits; voltage magnitude bounds; line-voltage-difference or apparent-flow limits; deployment factors sum to one and remain nonnegative.
data_properties.usesParameter: Uncertain complex load and renewable deviations δ; deployment vector α; bus-voltage matrix W split into Wu and Wx; risk levels ε and β; line admittances ylm; voltage and power limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Uses SDP lifting W=VV* and scenario-with-certificates sampling to solve a convex program; implemented with YALMIP and Mosek.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on the New England 39-bus system with Monte Carlo testing over 10,000 samples and comparison against nominal OPF and a prior probabilistic AC-OPF method.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method greatly reduced infeasible samples and line-flow violations versus nominal OPF, while using far fewer scenario samples than the compared parameterized approach.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: less conservative, probabilistic guarantees, computationally efficient, and exact for some networks. Limitation: exactness is only proven for a restrictive network class.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Can incorporate N-1 security constraints and outage probabilities within the same scenario framework.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To schedule generation economically while maintaining security in day-ahead and real-time OPF with renewable variability.

data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: RT-OPF over 60 min; DA-OPF over 24 h.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses forecasted solar, wind, and load variability within intervals; no explicit stochastic or robust formulation.

data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Evaluates 'best-fit' participation factors once to avoid separate optimization for every sub-interval.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported lower total cost and improved voltage stability versus conventional interval-by-interval OPF.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Forecasted load demand varies within sub-intervals and is included in imbalance calculations.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost over RT sub-intervals; maximize total profit over DA intervals as revenue minus generation cost.

data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Compared conventional and proposed RT-OPF/DA-OPF on IEEE 30-bus test system using 60-min RT and 24-h DA schedules.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed approach reduced RT total cost and increased DA profit while keeping optimization size unchanged and improving voltage stability.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: captures intra-interval variability with little added computational burden. Limitation: relies on forecast availability and fixed participation factors within each interval.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve sequential real-time security-constrained optimal power flow with fast dispatch decisions under inaccurate environmental parameters.

requirement.requirement_text: A local and scalable GNN-based ACOPF approximation model is needed. ACOPF is nonconvex and difficult to solve quickly; DCOPF is insufficiently accurate in heavily loaded networks; and ordinary MLPs lack locality and scalability. Therefore, the model should exploit the grid graph structure and train graph neural networks to approximate optimal OPF solutions.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Approximate AC optimal power flow solutions with a local, scalable graph neural network trained by imitation learning.
data_properties.hasMotivation: ACOPF is non-convex and costly to solve, and existing approximate methods do not scale well to large power networks.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: AC optimal power flow on power networks, using IEEE-30 and IEEE-118 test cases.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a graph neural network learn to imitate optimal ACOPF solutions accurately and efficiently in a decentralized, scalable way?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Estimated optimal generator active power outputs; evaluated against IPOPT ACOPF solutions.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Graph neural network parametrization with local message passing and scalable architecture.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow equations with nonlinear active and reactive power balance.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Training uses randomly sampled load scenarios from uniform ranges around reference loads.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Generator dispatch, bus voltages, active/reactive loads, and network topology on IEEE test systems.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Imitation learning with GNNs trained on IPOPT-generated optimal solutions.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported relative RMSE and much faster inference than IPOPT.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Loads are sampled as inputs; model predicts generator dispatch to meet demand.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator cost depending on active power output.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Active and reactive power balance equations p=P(v,δ;W), q=Q(v,δ;W), plus elementwise bounds Xmin ⪯ X ⪯ Xmax on voltages, angles, active and reactive powers.
data_properties.usesParameter: Network adjacency/weights W from line impedances; node states X=[v,δ,p,q]; generator selection matrix G; load vectors pL and qL; generator cost functions cm(pm).
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: IPOPT is used to solve ACOPF and generate training targets; GNNs are trained with MSE using ADAM on IEEE-30 and IEEE-118 datasets.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Evaluated on held-out test sets from IEEE-30 and IEEE-118; compared against global/local GNN and MLP baselines using relative RMSE.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: GNNs outperform MLP baselines, especially on the larger IEEE-118 case, and provide orders-of-magnitude faster inference than IPOPT.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: local, scalable, permutation-equivariant, and stable to graph perturbations. Limitation: trained to imitate IPOPT solutions rather than solve OPF exactly.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses graph convolution layers with K-hop neighborhood aggregation.

data_properties.hasModelName: Data driven ACOPF Physics informed Learning Calibration
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Data-driven AC Optimal Power Flow with Physics-informed Learning and Calibrations
data_properties.hasAuthor: Junfei Wang; Pirathayini Srikantha
data_properties.hasInstitution: York University
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Generate ACOPF solutions using physics-informed deep learning and feasibility calibration.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Need for a more efficient and reliable ACOPF solver because ACOPF is nonconvex, NP-hard, and difficult to solve quickly in modern grids.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: AC optimal power flow on IEEE bus-14 and bus-118 benchmark systems.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a data-driven ACOPF model produce near-optimal solutions while improving feasibility without relying on traditional solvers?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal bus voltage magnitudes and phase angles, generator active/reactive power dispatch, and calibrated feasible ACOPF solutions.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Two-stage physics-informed DNN prediction followed by iterative feasibility calibration.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with complex bus injections and Y-bus network model.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Generator buses, load buses, voltage magnitude/phase angle limits, and line flow limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Physics-informed loss, cycle-consistency reconstruction, and Gauss-Seidel-style calibration with warm starts.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported 0.67% optimality gap on IEEE 14-bus and 0.15% on IEEE 118-bus; calibration converged on all 14-bus tests and 92.2% on 118-bus.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uses active and reactive power demand at all buses as input.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator cost functions Cg(PGg) typically convex quadratic in active power generation.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Generator active/reactive limits; AC power-balance equations at each bus; voltage magnitude and phase-angle bounds; line apparent-power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Active and reactive demand PDi, QDi; generator outputs PGg, QGg; bus voltages |Vi|, ϕi; Y-bus admittance matrix; voltage and flow bounds; calibration stop threshold ρ and maximum epochs E.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: A CNN predicts voltages and angles from demand; power-flow equations reconstruct generator outputs and demand; an iterative calibration loop updates load-bus voltages and generator injections until imbalance is below ρ or E is reached.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Trained and tested on 100K MATPOWER-generated samples for IEEE 14-bus and 118-bus systems, using 80/20 split; compared against supervised learning and DeepOPF-V.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method achieved lower feasibility error and smaller optimality gaps than baselines, with strong convergence on both benchmark systems.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve security-constrained AC optimal power flow efficiently using a machine-learning-aided approach.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Full AC OPF is highly nonlinear and non-convex, making large-scale security-constrained solving computationally challenging.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained AC optimal power flow with switched shunt security constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a machine-learning-aided method predict key OPF variables and avoid running a physics-based OPF solver while preserving feasibility?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Bus voltage magnitudes and voltage angles; derived current injections, complex/real power injections, generator dispatch settings, and branch power flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid machine-learning-aided OPF using multi-input multi-output random forest plus physics-based network equations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with bus admittance matrix, current injection, apparent power, and nodal power balance.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period steady-state OPF.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Not specified; load samples from hourly ERCOT profile used for training/testing.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per case.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: No explicit uncertainty model; trained on sampled load cases.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC transmission OPF with generators, buses, branches, and switched shunts.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Multi-input multi-output random forest predicts voltages, then network equations recover remaining variables.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported zero constraint violation for the proposed method and much faster solution time than MATPOWER MIPS.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Load demand inputs Pd and Qd are used as predictors; no demand response model.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator costs represented by individual piece-wise linear cost functions.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Voltage magnitude and angle bounds; generator active/reactive power bounds; switched shunt susceptance bounds; real and reactive nodal power balance equations; branch apparent power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes vi and angles θi; generator outputs pg and qg; switched shunt susceptance bcs; real/reactive demands pd and qd; branch flow limit sf; bus admittance matrix Y; generator cost cg.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: RF is trained on converged MATPOWER solutions; case I predicts v and θ then computes injections and costs via network equations; case II predicts all OPF variables directly.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on a 500-bus GO competition network using 8,760 load samples; compared against MATPOWER MIPS and a pure ML baseline.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method closely matches MIPS voltage solutions, satisfies network constraints, and reduces total solution time from 2030.4 s to 35.26 s.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: fast and feasible OPF approximation without running a physics-based solver. Limitation: pure end-to-end ML still causes many equality-constraint violations.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Potentially useful for post-contingency analysis with many network topologies and load profiles.

evidence_package.main_risk_or_gap: 主要是可行域编码与 MILP 重构，不是 GNN-based ACOPF 近似；且重点在动态安全约束而非图结构局部消息传递。/ It is feasibility encoding plus MILP reformulation, not a GNN-based ACOPF approximation; the focus is dynamic security constraints rather than graph-local message passing.

data_properties.hasModelName: Neural Networks Encoding Dynamic Security Constrained AC OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Neural Networks for Encoding Dynamic Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Ilgiz Murzakhanov; Andreas Venzke; George S. Misyris; Spyros Chatzivasileiadis
data_properties.hasInstitution: Technical University of Denmark
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Encode dynamic security constraints into a tractable optimization model for AC optimal power flow.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Directly including dynamic security constraints makes AC-OPF intractable; the paper seeks a scalable alternative.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: AC optimal power flow with N-1 security and small-signal stability constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can neural networks encode the feasible space of dynamic security-constrained AC-OPF so it can be solved as a MILP?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Cost-optimal generator dispatch satisfying N-1 security and small-signal stability, with corresponding bus voltages and line flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Classification neural network encodes feasible operating points; exact mixed-integer reformulation with ReLU activations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow balance for the intact system; contingency-wise AC constraints for N-1 security.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single operating point; no multi-period horizon.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single snapshot dispatch.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: None explicit; random cost-function test instances only.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: N-1 security and small-signal stability constraints on an IEEE 14-bus system.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Neural-network feasibility encoding, exact MILP reformulation, and iterative linearization of power losses.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported 99% test accuracy; feasibility improved to 100% with epsilon adjustment.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost of the intact system state.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Generator active/reactive limits, voltage magnitude limits, line-flow limits, AC power balance, preventive generator set-point equality across contingencies, eigenvalue-based small-signal stability damping ratio constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator active and reactive limits, voltage limits, line-flow limits, contingency set C, damping threshold gamma_min, neural-network weights and biases, ReLU bounds, epsilon conservativeness parameter, loss-linearization threshold rho.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Train a ReLU classification network on feasible/infeasible operating points, reformulate it exactly as MILP, and iteratively linearize AC losses to solve MILPs with Gurobi.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 14-bus system with 45,000 labeled samples; 99% test accuracy; compared against AC-OPF and N-1 security-constrained AC-OPF.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach obtained cost-optimal solutions satisfying both static and dynamic security constraints; epsilon increased feasibility to 100% with small cost increase.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: tractable MILP approximation and improved feasibility. Limitations: approximation error may cause optimality loss and separate networks are needed for different grids.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses a conservative feasibility margin epsilon to trade off feasibility and optimality.

removed_candidates.removal_reason: 该模型是面向电网基础模型与下游任务的概念性框架，并未直接提出或训练一个用于近似 ACOPF 的 GNN-ACOPF 模型；其核心不是针对 ACOPF 的局部可扩展图神经网络求解器。 / This model is a conceptual foundation-model framework for grid tasks and downstream applications, not a directly trained GNN-based ACOPF approximation model; its core is not a local, scalable graph neural network solver for ACOPF.

该模型采用 CNN 和拓扑标签来处理不同运行模式下的 ACOPF，并非利用电网图结构的图神经网络方法，因此与“GNN-based”要求不一致。 / This model uses a CNN with topology labels for ACOPF under different operation patterns, rather than a graph neural network exploiting the grid graph structure, so it does not match the GNN-based requirement.

该模型基于前馈深度网络与拉格朗日对偶/热启动机制预测 ACOPF，不是利用图神经网络和图局部消息传递来建模电网拓扑，因此不符合用户对 GNN 局部性与可扩展性的核心要求。 / This model relies on feed-forward deep networks with Lagrangian dual and hot-start mechanisms to predict ACOPF, not graph neural networks with local message passing over the grid topology, so it misses the user's core GNN locality and scalability requirement.

该模型解决的是带 N-1 约束的安全约束 OPF（SCOPF），核心目标包含故障后安全性与强化学习控制，而不是用户所需的面向普通 ACOPF 的 GNN 近似模型。 / This model addresses security-constrained OPF (SCOPF) with N-1 contingencies, focusing on post-contingency security and reinforcement-learning control rather than the requested GNN approximation model for standard ACOPF.

该模型面向安全约束 ACOPF/SCOPF，并使用随机森林与物理方程恢复变量，不是基于图神经网络的 ACOPF 近似方法，因此与用户要求的 GNN-based ACOPF 模型不一致。 / This model targets security-constrained ACOPF/SCOPF and uses random forests plus physics equations to recover variables, not a graph-neural-network-based ACOPF approximation, so it is inconsistent with the requested GNN-based ACOPF model.

该模型编码的是动态安全约束 ACOPF，并将问题转化为 MILP 进行求解，重点在动态安全与可行域编码，而不是利用图神经网络直接近似普通 ACOPF 解。 / This model encodes dynamic security-constrained ACOPF and reformulates it as a MILP, focusing on dynamic security and feasible-space encoding rather than directly approximating standard ACOPF solutions with a graph neural network.

raw_consistency.overall_summary: 保留的候选中，Graph_Neural_Networks_ACOPF 与用户要求高度一致：它明确使用图神经网络、局部消息传递和可扩展架构来近似 ACOPF。其余被移除的模型要么不是 GNN 方法，要么主要解决 SCOPF/动态安全约束问题，或是更偏基础模型/概念框架而非直接的 GNN-ACOPF 近似器。 / Among the remaining candidates, Graph_Neural_Networks_ACOPF aligns closely with the user's requirement: it explicitly uses graph neural networks, local message passing, and a scalable architecture to approximate ACOPF. The removed models either are not GNN methods, mainly address SCOPF/dynamic security constraints, or are more of a foundation-model concept/framework rather than a direct GNN-ACOPF approximator.

top_rows.Requirement text: A local and scalable GNN-based ACOPF approximation model is needed. ACOPF is nonconvex and difficult to solve quickly; DCOPF is insufficiently accurate in heavily loaded networks; and ordinary MLPs lack locality and scalability. Therefore, the model should exploit the grid graph structure and train graph neural networks to approximate optimal OPF solutions.

   risk: 模型是通用物理信息深度学习而非明确的 GNN；其可扩展性主要来自学习框架与校准流程，不是显式图消息传递 / It is a physics-informed deep learning model rather than an explicit GNN; scalability comes from the learning/calibration pipeline, not graph message passing.
3. Data_Driven_Physics_Informed_SELM_OPF | score=88.0
   why: 明确针对非线性、非凸 OPF 的数据驱动近似，覆盖大规模系统并强调快速计算，适合做 ACOPF 近似求解器 / Explicitly targets nonlinear, nonconvex OPF with a data-driven approximation, covering large-scale systems and fast computation, suitable as an ACOPF surrogate solver.
   risk: 方法是 physics-informed SELM 回归与样本预分类，不是 GNN；对网格局部性与图结构的显式利用较弱 / The method is physics-informed SELM regression with sample pre-classification, not a GNN; explicit exploitation of locality and graph structure is limited.
4. GridFM_v0 | score=88.0
   why: 明确面向电网图结构的基础模型，并提到可用于 OPF / AC power flow 相关下游任务。/ Explicitly targets graph-structured grid foundation models and mentions downstream OPF / AC power-flow tasks.
   risk: 更偏向基础模型与预训练路线，而非已完成的 GNN-based ACOPF 近似求解器；对“直接训练 GNN 逼近最优 ACOPF 解”的落地程度有限。/ More of a foundation-model and pretraining roadmap than a completed GNN-based ACOPF approximation solver; direct end-to-end ACOPF approximation is limited.
5. ConvOPF_DOP | score=82.0
   why: 这是 AC-OPF 数据驱动近似模型，输入包含负荷与拓扑标签，输出电压并通过潮流重构其余变量，具备一定网络结构感知能力 / This is a data-driven AC-OPF approximation model; it uses load and topology labels, predicts voltages, and reconstructs remaining variables via power flow, giving some network-structure awareness.
   risk: 核心是 CNN 而非 GNN，图局部消息传递与严格的网格图归纳偏置不足；更偏向模式分类后的监督预测 / The core is CNN rather than GNN, so graph-local message passing and strong grid-graph inductive bias are lacking; it is more pattern-classification-based supervised prediction.
6. Predicting_AC_Optimal_Power_Flows | score=82.0
   why: 面向AC-OPF预测，使用深度学习结合拉格朗日对偶与约束惩罚来逼近最优潮流解，且覆盖大规模IEEE/NESTA系统 / Targets AC-OPF prediction and combines deep learning with Lagrangian dual methods and constraint penalties to approximate optimal flows, validated on large IEEE/NESTA systems.
   risk: 主体是通用前馈深度网络而非GNN，因此对“利用网格图结构、局部性和可扩展性”的契合度弱于专门的GNN模型 / The main model is a generic feed-forward deep network rather than a GNN, so it is weaker on exploiting grid graph locality and scalability than a dedicated GNN approach.
7. Security_Constrained_Optimal_Power_Flow | score=74.0
   why: 采用 AC 潮流并实现快速 SCOPF 求解，适合需要安全约束下的 OPF 近似加速 / Uses AC power flow and fast SCOPF solving, fitting the need for accelerated OPF approximation under security constraints.
   risk: 重点是安全约束 SCOPF 与 DRL 加速，不是面向一般 ACOPF 的图神经网络近似；与用户强调的 GNN/locality/scalability 不完全一致 / It focuses on security-constrained SCOPF with DRL acceleration, not a general ACOPF GNN surrogate; it does not directly match the user's emphasis on GNN/locality/scalability.
8. Machine_Learning_Aided_SCOPF | score=74.0
   why: 使用机器学习预测 OPF 关键变量，并结合网络方程恢复其余变量，具备快速近似 AC OPF 的思路。/ Uses machine learning to predict key OPF variables and recover the rest with network equations, fitting the idea of fast AC OPF approximation.
   risk: 方法核心是随机森林而非 GNN，且重点是 security-constrained OPF，不是强调利用图神经网络的局部性与可扩展性。/ The core method is random forest rather than GNN, and it focuses on security-constrained OPF rather than exploiting GNN locality and scalability.
9. Neural_Networks_Encoding_Dynamic_Security_Constrained_AC_OPF | score=68.0
   why: 明确将神经网络用于编码 AC OPF 可行域，并求解 AC OPF 相关问题，属于神经网络辅助的快速近似路线。/ Explicitly uses neural networks to encode the feasible space of AC OPF and solve an AC-OPF-related problem, fitting a neural approximation route.
   risk: 主要是可行域编码与 MILP 重构，不是 GNN-based ACOPF 近似；且重点在动态安全约束而非图结构局部消息传递。/ It is feasibility encoding plus MILP reformulation, not a GNN-based ACOPF approximation; the focus is dynamic security constraints rather than graph-local message passing.

requirement.requirement_text: A physics-informed neural network framework is needed so that learning results can still exploit governing physical equations when data are limited. For problems governed by nonlinear physical laws, ordinary deep learning may lack robustness. Therefore, differential equations, conservation laws, and other physics knowledge should be embedded into the loss function to solve or discover physical-system models.

prefilter_result.user_requirement: A physics-informed neural network framework is needed so that learning results can still exploit governing physical equations when data are limited. For problems governed by nonlinear physical laws, ordinary deep learning may lack robustness. Therefore, differential equations, conservation laws, and other physics knowledge should be embedded into the loss function to solve or discover physical-system models.

selected_candidates.why_matched: 直接满足物理信息神经网络框架需求 / Directly matches the need for a physics-informed neural network framework. 该模型通过物理约束损失把非线性PDE的残差、初始/边界条件嵌入训练 / It embeds nonlinear PDE residuals and initial/boundary conditions into the training loss. 在小数据和噪声数据下仍可用于求解与发现物理系统模型 / It is designed for small-data and noisy-data regimes for solving and discovering physical-system models.
selected_candidates.main_risk_or_gap: 主要适用于偏微分方程类物理系统，而非专门面向电力系统OPF / Mainly targets PDE-governed physical systems rather than OPF-specific power-system problems. 若用户需要电网OPF场景中的PINN化建模，则需额外迁移到电力方程 / If the user needs PINN-style modeling for OPF, additional adaptation to power-flow equations is required.
supporting_evidence: hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve forward and inverse problems governed by nonlinear partial differential equations using physics-informed neural networks.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Physics-informed neural networks: A deep learning framework for solving forward and inverse problems involving nonlinear partial differential equations

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve forward and inverse problems governed by nonlinear partial differential equations using physics-informed neural networks.

data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can deep neural networks be constrained by PDE physics to infer hidden states and identify governing parameters from limited data?

data_properties.hasModelFeature: Continuous-time and discrete-time physics-informed neural network formulations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Uses automatic differentiation to enforce PDE residuals at collocation points or Runge–Kutta stage equations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-step and multi-step time evolution; continuous-time and discrete-time formulations.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Uses sparse snapshots, initial/boundary data, and collocation points; discrete-time examples use large time steps.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Trains on available snapshots and collocation points over the modeled time interval.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: No explicit uncertainty quantification; mentions noisy data robustness only.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: None; the paper addresses general nonlinear PDEs in fluids, quantum mechanics, reaction-diffusion, and shallow-water waves.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Physics-informed loss functions with automatic differentiation; implicit Runge–Kutta-based discrete-time formulation.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported accurate predictions with low relative L2 error and robust parameter identification under noisy data.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: None.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize mean squared error or sum of squared errors combining data mismatch and PDE residuals; in discrete time, match Runge–Kutta stage outputs and boundary/snapshot data.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Enforce governing PDE residuals, initial conditions, boundary conditions, periodicity, divergence-free incompressibility, and Runge–Kutta stage relations.
data_properties.usesParameter: Neural-network weights and biases; PDE parameters λ; collocation points; initial/boundary data; Runge–Kutta coefficients aij, bj, cj; time step Δt; number of stages q.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Uses feed-forward neural networks with tanh activations, automatic differentiation, and L-BFGS; discrete-time models leverage implicit Runge–Kutta schemes.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on Schrödinger, Allen–Cahn, Navier–Stokes, KdV, and Burgers examples against spectral/finite-element reference solutions.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: Physics-informed neural networks can recover accurate PDE solutions and identify unknown coefficients from sparse, noisy data.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: data-efficient, physics-constrained, robust to noise, handles forward and inverse problems. Limitations: collocation cost grows in higher dimensions; architecture and training sensitivity remain.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Open-source code and datasets were provided on GitHub.

data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported 0.67% optimality gap on IEEE 14-bus and 0.15% on IEEE 118-bus; calibration converged on all 14-bus tests and 92.2% on 118-bus.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uses active and reactive power demand at all buses as input.

data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method achieved lower feasibility error and smaller optimality gaps than baselines, with strong convergence on both benchmark systems.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: improved feasibility with near-optimal solutions and no traditional solver in the prediction stage. Limitation: calibration did not converge for all 118-bus test cases.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Future work mentions robust learning under input uncertainties and unsupervised or semi-supervised learning without labeled ACOPF solver data.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To advocate and outline grid foundation models for power-system operations, planning, and control.

data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can foundation models be developed for electric power grids to generalize across grid data and accelerate downstream applications such as power flow and OPF?

data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Not specified; near-term focus is static power-flow applications.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses diverse topologies, load conditions, perturbations, and synthetic scenarios; discusses scenario trees and stochastic programming.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Transmission and distribution grid applications including power flow, OPF, contingency analysis, state estimation, stability, control, planning, and cybersecurity.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Self-supervised masked graph autoencoding with physics-informed loss; intended to speed up power-flow-related computation.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Projected 3–4 orders-of-magnitude speed-up over conventional power-flow solvers; less than 1% error cited from related GNN work.

data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: For OPF use, minimize generation costs by reconstructing generator power; the paper does not present a full OPF mathematical formulation.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Reconstructed node variables must satisfy power-flow equations and bounds such as generator capacity constraints.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: A Deep Neural Network-based Frequency Predictor for Frequency-Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Fan Jiang; Xingpeng Li; Pascal Van Hentenryck
data_properties.hasInstitution: University of Houston; Georgia Institute of Technology
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Real-time frequency-constrained optimal power flow with DNN-based RoCoF and frequency nadir constraints.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Accurate RoCoF and frequency nadir constraints are complex to compute, yet needed for fast real-time FCOPF.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Traditional OPF lacks frequency security; linearized FCOPF can be inaccurate for RoCoF and frequency nadir.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a DNN predictor replace simplified frequency constraints in FCOPF while improving accuracy and maintaining solvability?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generator dispatch with associated RoCoF and frequency nadir values under contingencies.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: FCOPF augmented with a DNN-based frequency predictor and mixed-integer linearized ReLU constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: DC power flow with nodal balance, line flow equations, generator limits, and thermal limits.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period real-time dispatch; no multi-period horizon.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Real-time OPF, described as run about every 5 minutes.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Scenario-based EMT training data across varying loads, generator outputs, and outage locations; no explicit stochastic optimization.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Frequency security constraints for low-inertia grids using RoCoF and frequency nadir.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: DNN predictor linearized with mixed-integer constraints and solved with Gurobi.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Compared solve time and frequency-metric accuracy against T-OPF and linear FCOPF.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Load variations are included as scenario inputs; no explicit demand response or load control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost using quadratic generator cost functions, sum_i(c2_i Pg_i^2 + c1_i Pg_i + c0_i).
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Nodal power balance, DC line flow equations, generator output bounds, transmission line thermal limits, and frequency constraints on RoCoF and frequency nadir.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients c2_i, c1_i, c0_i; line reactance x_k; generator and line limits; system inertia H_sys; base power P_base; base frequency f0; RoCoF and frequency thresholds; DNN weights, biases, and ReLU bounds.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Implemented in Python 3.9 with Gurobi; DNN trained on PSCAD/EMTDC simulation data and embedded as mixed-integer linear constraints.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated against PSCAD/EMTDC simulations on a modified IEEE 9-bus system under normal and high-load contingencies.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: DNN-FCOPF produced frequency metrics much closer to EMT simulations than linear FCOPF, with modest extra cost and longer solve time.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Improves frequency-security accuracy over linear FCOPF, but adds mixed-integer complexity and depends on training-data coverage.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Evaluated under multiple load profiles and contingencies, including out-of-distribution high-load cases.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Machine Learning-Aided Security Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Jubeyer Rahman; Cong Feng; Jie Zhang
data_properties.hasInstitution: The University of Texas at Dallas
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve security-constrained AC optimal power flow efficiently using a machine-learning-aided approach.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Full AC OPF is highly nonlinear and non-convex, making large-scale security-constrained solving computationally challenging.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Security-constrained AC optimal power flow with switched shunt security constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a machine-learning-aided method predict key OPF variables and avoid running a physics-based OPF solver while preserving feasibility?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Bus voltage magnitudes and voltage angles; derived current injections, complex/real power injections, generator dispatch settings, and branch power flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Hybrid machine-learning-aided OPF using multi-input multi-output random forest plus physics-based network equations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with bus admittance matrix, current injection, apparent power, and nodal power balance.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period steady-state OPF.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Not specified; load samples from hourly ERCOT profile used for training/testing.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per case.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: No explicit uncertainty model; trained on sampled load cases.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Security-constrained AC transmission OPF with generators, buses, branches, and switched shunts.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Multi-input multi-output random forest predicts voltages, then network equations recover remaining variables.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported zero constraint violation for the proposed method and much faster solution time than MATPOWER MIPS.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Load demand inputs Pd and Qd are used as predictors; no demand response model.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost, with generator costs represented by individual piece-wise linear cost functions.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Voltage magnitude and angle bounds; generator active/reactive power bounds; switched shunt susceptance bounds; real and reactive nodal power balance equations; branch apparent power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus voltage magnitudes vi and angles θi; generator outputs pg and qg; switched shunt susceptance bcs; real/reactive demands pd and qd; branch flow limit sf; bus admittance matrix Y; generator cost cg.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: RF is trained on converged MATPOWER solutions; case I predicts v and θ then computes injections and costs via network equations; case II predicts all OPF variables directly.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on a 500-bus GO competition network using 8,760 load samples; compared against MATPOWER MIPS and a pure ML baseline.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method closely matches MIPS voltage solutions, satisfies network constraints, and reduces total solution time from 2030.4 s to 35.26 s.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: fast and feasible OPF approximation without running a physics-based solver. Limitation: pure end-to-end ML still causes many equality-constraint violations.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Potentially useful for post-contingency analysis with many network topologies and load profiles.

data_properties.hasModelName: Neural Networks Encoding Dynamic Security Constrained AC OPF
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Neural Networks for Encoding Dynamic Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Ilgiz Murzakhanov; Andreas Venzke; George S. Misyris; Spyros Chatzivasileiadis
data_properties.hasInstitution: Technical University of Denmark
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Encode dynamic security constraints into a tractable optimization model for AC optimal power flow.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Directly including dynamic security constraints makes AC-OPF intractable; the paper seeks a scalable alternative.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: AC optimal power flow with N-1 security and small-signal stability constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can neural networks encode the feasible space of dynamic security-constrained AC-OPF so it can be solved as a MILP?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Cost-optimal generator dispatch satisfying N-1 security and small-signal stability, with corresponding bus voltages and line flows.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Classification neural network encodes feasible operating points; exact mixed-integer reformulation with ReLU activations.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow balance for the intact system; contingency-wise AC constraints for N-1 security.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single operating point; no multi-period horizon.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single snapshot dispatch.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: None explicit; random cost-function test instances only.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: N-1 security and small-signal stability constraints on an IEEE 14-bus system.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Neural-network feasibility encoding, exact MILP reformulation, and iterative linearization of power losses.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported 99% test accuracy; feasibility improved to 100% with epsilon adjustment.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost of the intact system state.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Generator active/reactive limits, voltage magnitude limits, line-flow limits, AC power balance, preventive generator set-point equality across contingencies, eigenvalue-based small-signal stability damping ratio constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator active and reactive limits, voltage limits, line-flow limits, contingency set C, damping threshold gamma_min, neural-network weights and biases, ReLU bounds, epsilon conservativeness parameter, loss-linearization threshold rho.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Train a ReLU classification network on feasible/infeasible operating points, reformulate it exactly as MILP, and iteratively linearize AC losses to solve MILPs with Gurobi.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on IEEE 14-bus system with 45,000 labeled samples; 99% test accuracy; compared against AC-OPF and N-1 security-constrained AC-OPF.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The approach obtained cost-optimal solutions satisfying both static and dynamic security constraints; epsilon increased feasibility to 100% with small cost increase.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: tractable MILP approximation and improved feasibility. Limitations: approximation error may cause optimality loss and separate networks are needed for different grids.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Uses a conservative feasibility margin epsilon to trade off feasibility and optimality.

top_rows.Requirement text: A physics-informed neural network framework is needed so that learning results can still exploit governing physical equations when data are limited. For problems governed by nonlinear physical laws, ordinary deep learning may lack robustness. Therefore, differential equations, conservation laws, and other physics knowledge should be embedded into the loss function to solve or discover physical-system models.
top_rows.Paper title: Physics-informed neural networks: A deep learning framework for solving forward and inverse problems involving nonlinear partial differential equations
top_rows.Recommendation reason: 该模型与用户需求高度一致：论文明确提出 Physics-Informed Neural Networks，并将偏微分方程残差、初始条件和边界条件直接写入损失函数，用自动微分约束网络学习。它专门面向非线性 PDE 的正问题与反问题，正好对应“数据有限时仍利用物理方程、将微分方程和守恒律嵌入损失函数”的需求。 / This model matches the request very closely: the paper explicitly proposes Physics-Informed Neural Networks and embeds PDE residuals, initial conditions, and boundary conditions into the loss via automatic differentiation. It targets forward and inverse problems governed by nonlinear PDEs, directly aligning with the need to exploit governing equations under limited data and to encode differential equations and conservation laws into the loss.
top_rows.Matched needs: 物理信息神经网络框架 / Physics-informed neural network framework；将物理方程嵌入损失函数 / embed physics into the loss；适用于非线性物理规律 / suitable for nonlinear physical laws；小样本与噪声数据下仍可学习 / data-limited and noisy-data learning；用于求解或发现物理系统模型 / solve or discover physical-system models。
top_rows.Strengths: 论文的核心机制非常明确：hasObjectiveFunction 采用数据误差与 PDE residual 的联合最小化，hasConstraintFunction 包括 governing PDE residuals、initial conditions、boundary conditions、periodicity 和 incompressibility；hasSolutionDetailsSummary 说明使用 feed-forward neural networks、tanh 激活、automatic differentiation 和 L-BFGS；hasFindingsSummary 表明可从 sparse/noisy observations 中恢复 PDE 解并识别未知参数。 / The core mechanism is explicit: hasObjectiveFunction minimizes a combination of data mismatch and PDE residuals, while hasConstraintFunction includes governing PDE residuals, initial conditions, boundary conditions, periodicity, and incompressibility; hasSolutionDetailsSummary states it uses feed-forward neural networks, tanh activations, automatic differentiation, and L-BFGS; hasFindingsSummary shows it can recover PDE solutions and identify unknown parameters from sparse/noisy observations.
top_rows.Limitations: 该模型主要面向连续时间/离散时间 PDE 问题，论文验证集中在 Schrödinger、Allen–Cahn、Navier–Stokes、KdV、Burgers 等通用非线性 PDE，并未针对电力系统 OPF 这类离散网络优化问题专门设计；同时其 hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary 指出高维时 collocation 成本会上升，训练对架构和超参数较敏感。 / The model is mainly designed for continuous-time/discrete-time PDE problems and was validated on general nonlinear PDEs such as Schrödinger, Allen–Cahn, Navier–Stokes, KdV, and Burgers, not specifically for discrete network optimization problems like power-system OPF; its hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary also notes collocation cost grows in higher dimensions and training is sensitive to architecture and hyperparameters.

requirement.requirement_text: A fast and physics-friendly data-driven AC-OPF model is needed. Traditional AC-OPF is nonlinear and nonconvex, making it hard to solve frequently in real-time operation or large-scale simulation; DC-OPF is fast but may be economically suboptimal and violate AC physics. Therefore, the model should use historical similar states or previous solutions to quickly predict generator active power outputs and voltage setpoints, while using Lagrangian constraint penalties to improve AC-OPF feasibility.

data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To advocate and outline grid foundation models for power-system operations, planning, and control.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Increasing grid complexity and uncertainty from the energy transition, climate change, aging infrastructure, and cybersecurity threats.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Lack of scalable, transferable AI methods for diverse power-grid tasks and power-flow-related applications.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can foundation models be developed for electric power grids to generalize across grid data and accelerate downstream applications such as power flow and OPF?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: No OPF model is solved in this paper; it proposes a GridFM-v0 concept for reconstructing power-flow states and, in discussed downstream use, optimal generation dispatch and objective values.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Graph neural network-based foundation model concept; masked autoencoder pre-training on graph-structured grid data.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow reconstruction on graph nodes with bus variables and line/transformer edges.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Initially single-time-step power-flow data; extendable to multiple consecutive time steps for forecasting.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Single time step in the near-term model; high-resolution PMU data mentioned for dynamic extensions.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Not specified; near-term focus is static power-flow applications.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses diverse topologies, load conditions, perturbations, and synthetic scenarios; discusses scenario trees and stochastic programming.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Transmission and distribution grid applications including power flow, OPF, contingency analysis, state estimation, stability, control, planning, and cybersecurity.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Self-supervised masked graph autoencoding with physics-informed loss; intended to speed up power-flow-related computation.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Projected 3–4 orders-of-magnitude speed-up over conventional power-flow solvers; less than 1% error cited from related GNN work.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Mentions load conditions, load forecasting, electric vehicles, heating electrification, and demand uncertainty.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: For OPF use, minimize generation costs by reconstructing generator power; the paper does not present a full OPF mathematical formulation.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Reconstructed node variables must satisfy power-flow equations and bounds such as generator capacity constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus active power, reactive power, voltage magnitude, voltage angle; line and transformer connectivity; topology, load conditions, and power-flow solutions.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: GridFM-v0 is proposed as a masked graph autoencoder pre-trained on solved power-flow cases from multiple topologies and load conditions, then fine-tuned for downstream tasks.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: No direct model validation results are reported for GridFM-v0; validation is proposed on open datasets and later on utility data behind firewalls.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The paper argues GridFMs could generalize across grid tasks and substantially accelerate power-system analysis, especially power-flow-related applications.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalability, adaptability, and simulation acceleration. Limitations: data availability, privacy, trust, and difficulty accessing operational grid data.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper is a perspective proposing a roadmap rather than presenting a completed OPF solver.

data_properties.hasModelName: Real Time Lagrangian Deep Reinforcement Learning
data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Real-Time Optimal Power Flow: A Lagrangian Based Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
data_properties.hasAuthor: Ziming Yan; Yan Xu
data_properties.hasInstitution: School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Real-time optimal power flow decision-making under operating constraints using deep reinforcement learning.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Need faster OPF to respond to rapid uncertainties from renewable generation and stochastic loads.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Real-time OPF with generator cost minimization subject to power balance, limits, ramping, voltage, and line-flow constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can a Lagrangian-based deep reinforcement learning agent produce near-optimal RT-OPF decisions in real time while satisfying constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generator active power dispatch and generator voltage magnitude setpoints; resulting operating cost and constraint-compliant operating points.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Deep reinforcement learning with Lagrangian relaxation and continuous-action control.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power balance equations with reactive power, voltage magnitudes, and line-flow limits.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single dispatch interval repeated over real-time intervals.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Per-interval real-time optimization.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses real-time load and renewable variability as state inputs; no explicit stochastic optimization.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Generator limits, ramping limits, bus voltage limits, and branch apparent-power limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Deep deterministic policy gradient with analytically derived deterministic gradient and Lagrangian penalties.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported high solution optimality, constraint compliance, and large time savings versus IP method.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Real-time net load input includes active and reactive demand; no explicit demand response control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost over each dispatch interval, using generator fuel cost functions.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Nodal active and reactive power balance; generator active-power bounds with ramping limits; bus voltage magnitude bounds; branch apparent-power flow limits.
data_properties.usesParameter: Active and reactive load, previous generator output, generator cost coefficients, ramp-up/down limits, voltage limits, branch flow limits, admittance matrix entries, learning rate, memory buffer size.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Offline training of a DNN actor with replay memory and exploration noise; online inference outputs [P_G^t, V_G^t] for RT-OPF.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Tested on a modified IEEE 118-bus system with random net-load variation; compared against IP, DC OPF, and supervised learning.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method achieved near-IP optimal cost, satisfied operating constraints, and ran in real time with about 99.8% average time saving over IP.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: real-time operation, constraint-aware learning, good optimality. Limitation: evaluated on one test system and relies on trained data-driven policy.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Continuous-action DRL formulation for RT-OPF; critic network not used.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Online Optimization in Power Systems With High Penetration of Renewable Generation: Advances and Prospects
data_properties.hasAuthor: Zhaojian Wang; Wei Wei; John Zhen Fu Pang; Feng Liu; Bo Yang; Xinping Guan; Shengwei Mei
data_properties.hasInstitution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Tsinghua University; Institute of High Performance Computing (A*STAR), Singapore
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Review and compare online optimization techniques for power-system operation under high renewable penetration.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Increasing renewable variability and controllable loads make offline optimization less reliable for real-time power-system operation.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: How to classify and apply online optimization methods to dynamic control, single-period OPF/voltage regulation, and multi-period energy management problems.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Which online optimization paradigms are most suitable for different power-system time scales and operational settings?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Not applicable; this is a review paper rather than a solved OPF model.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Review of optimization-guided dynamic control, feedback optimization, Lyapunov optimization, and online convex optimization.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Discusses AC bus-injection and branch-flow models; linearized DC power flow and DistFlow approximations.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Covers single-period and multi-period formulations, plus fast dynamic-control time scales.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Seconds to minutes for dynamic control; single-period and multi-period decision settings.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single-period and multi-period; some Lyapunov examples use finite or infinite horizons.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Addresses renewable variability and uncertainty through online decision-making without relying on forecasts or historical distributions.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Frequency control, voltage regulation, OPF, economic dispatch, energy storage scheduling, demand response, and power markets.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Compares feedback-based, primal-dual, ADMM, Newton-Raphson, Lyapunov, and OCO methods; discusses distributed and asynchronous variants.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Emphasizes fast response, tracking of time-varying conditions, and reduced computational burden.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Includes controllable loads, demand response, electric vehicles, and load-side frequency control.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Examples include minimizing generation cost in OPF, regulation cost in frequency control, and long-term average cost in Lyapunov/OCO formulations.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Power-flow equations, voltage limits, generation and reactive-power bounds, power-balance constraints, line congestion, storage SoC and charging/discharging limits, ramping and other coupled constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generation cost coefficients ai, bi; voltage bounds vi; power injection bounds Pi, Qi; line parameters rij, xij, Bij; storage queue/SoC Qt; Lyapunov weight ρ; stepsize η; control gains.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: The paper reviews algorithmic frameworks and representative formulations; it does not present a single new solved OPF instance.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: No dedicated validation of a new OPF model; cites prior experimental and numerical studies in the reviewed literature.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: Online optimization is useful for volatile power systems because it can track changing conditions and avoid reliance on inaccurate forecasts.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: fast, measurement-driven, and suitable for time-varying systems. Limitations: problem-dependent, often lacks a unified theory, and some methods need communication or predictions.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper is a survey and taxonomy of online optimization methods in power systems.
data_properties.hasSourceFileName: Online Optimization in Power Systems With.pdf

ranked_candidates.strengths: 模型输出与需求完全对齐：primary output 明确包含 generator active power setpoints 和 bus voltage magnitudes，扩展模型还包含 voltage angles 与 reactive generation；solution details 中给出 feed-forward ReLU 子网络、SGD/Adam、subgradient 更新 Lagrangian multipliers；validation 在多个 IEEE/NESTA 系统上进行，并报告相对 AC-OPF 与 DC 近似的显著加速。 / The outputs align exactly with the need: primary outputs explicitly include generator active power setpoints and bus voltage magnitudes, with extended outputs for voltage angles and reactive generation; the solution details specify feed-forward ReLU subnetworks, SGD/Adam, and subgradient updates of Lagrangian multipliers; validation spans multiple IEEE/NESTA systems and reports major speedups over AC-OPF and DC approximation.
ranked_candidates.limitations: 该方法依赖相似历史状态与热启动样本，且主要在基准规模系统上验证；当运行状态与训练分布差异较大时，预测可行性与精度可能下降。 / The method relies on similar historical states and hot-start samples, and it is mainly validated on benchmark-scale systems; feasibility and accuracy may degrade when operating conditions differ substantially from the training distribution.

requirement.requirement_text: A probabilistically robust AC-OPF model is needed to handle renewable generation and load uncertainty. Wind, photovoltaic generation, and load fluctuations can make deterministic dispatch based on forecasts cause line overloads or constraint violations, while fully robust optimization may be too conservative and costly. Therefore, a chance-constrained or probabilistically robust AC-OPF is needed to minimize generation cost while controlling constraint-violation risk within a specified small probability and maintaining generation and transmission security.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Probabilistically Robust AC Optimal Power Flow
data_properties.hasAuthor: Mohammadreza Chamanbaz; Fabrizio Dabbene; Constantino M. Lagoa
data_properties.hasInstitution: iTrust Center for Research in Cyber Security, Singapore University of Technology and Design; CNR-IEIIT, Torino, Italy; Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Penn State University
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Minimize generation cost in AC optimal power flow while satisfying network constraints under uncertain loads and renewable generation with probabilistic guarantees.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Classical OPF dispatch is rigid and can become inefficient or infeasible under renewable and load uncertainty, causing overloads and outages.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Robust and chance-constrained AC optimal power flow with uncertain loads and renewable generators.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: How can AC-OPF be solved efficiently under uncertainty while limiting the probability of violating generation and transmission constraints?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal controllable generation dispatch, generator voltage magnitudes, deployment vector, and corresponding bus voltage and line-flow-feasible operating point.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Scenario-with-certificates formulation combined with convex SDP relaxation of AC power flow.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power balance equations with voltage-magnitude and line-flow constraints via lifted matrix W.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Single-period OPF repeated over hourly demand scenarios in experiments.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Single operating snapshot per solve; 24 hourly solves in simulation.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Probabilistic uncertainty in loads and renewable generation using scenario with certificates and chance constraints.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Includes renewable generators, uncertain loads, generator participation factors, voltage limits, and transmission limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Convex relaxation plus randomized scenario-with-certificates sampling.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: A priori probabilistic guarantee on constraint-violation risk; exact for a restricted class of networks.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Uncertain loads are explicitly modeled and balanced through generator deployment factors.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize generation cost f(u); in the penalized variant, worst-case cost adds reactive-power and line-loss penalties.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: AC power balance equalities; generator active/reactive limits; voltage magnitude bounds; line-voltage-difference or apparent-flow limits; deployment factors sum to one and remain nonnegative.
data_properties.usesParameter: Uncertain complex load and renewable deviations δ; deployment vector α; bus-voltage matrix W split into Wu and Wx; risk levels ε and β; line admittances ylm; voltage and power limits.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Uses SDP lifting W=VV* and scenario-with-certificates sampling to solve a convex program; implemented with YALMIP and Mosek.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Validated on the New England 39-bus system with Monte Carlo testing over 10,000 samples and comparison against nominal OPF and a prior probabilistic AC-OPF method.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed method greatly reduced infeasible samples and line-flow violations versus nominal OPF, while using far fewer scenario samples than the compared parameterized approach.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: less conservative, probabilistic guarantees, computationally efficient, and exact for some networks. Limitation: exactness is only proven for a restrictive network class.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Can incorporate N-1 security constraints and outage probabilities within the same scenario framework.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Chance-Constrained OPF: A Distributed Method With Confidentiality Preservation
data_properties.hasAuthor: Mengshuo Jia; Gabriela Hug; Yifan Su; Chen Shen
data_properties.hasInstitution: ETH Zurich; Tsinghua University
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: Solve multi-regional chance-constrained optimal power flow in a distributed way while preserving confidentiality of regional data.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Centralized CC-OPF requires sharing confidential generation costs, loads, topologies, and line parameters across regional ISOs.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Global chance-constrained OPF for a multi-regional interconnected grid with confidential regional information.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can CC-OPF be solved exactly in a distributed manner without revealing regional confidential data?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal dispatchable generation schedules across regions; implied bus voltage and line-flow constraint satisfaction through the solved CC-OPF.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Distributed chance-constrained OPF with confidentiality-preserving transformations and privacy-preserving aggregation.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: Uses decoupled linearized power flow to express voltages and line flows as linear functions of injections.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Multi-time-slot formulation with inter-temporal ramp-rate constraints.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Time slots; day-ahead dispatch in experiments with T = 24.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Finite horizon over T time slots.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Chance constraints with wind-power uncertainty modeled by Gaussian mixture distributions and quantile conversion.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Multi-regional interconnected grid with dispatchable generators, wind farms, loads, nodal voltages, and line flows.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Transformation-based encryption, accelerated average consensus, and privacy-preserving average consensus.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Claims exact global optimal dispatch recovery, high accuracy, and no parameter tuning or convergence issues.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Loads are included as fixed demand; load uncertainty is ignored.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost over all regions and time slots: sum of quadratic and linear dispatchable-generation costs.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Capacity bounds and ramp-rate limits on generators; chance-constrained supply-demand balance; chance-constrained state limits for voltages or line flows; deterministic linearized power-flow-based mappings.
data_properties.usesParameter: Quadratic and linear generator cost coefficients; generation upper/lower bounds; ramp-rate bounds; wind-power quantiles; state upper bounds; DLPF mapping coefficients; line admittance/topology data.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: Transforms the CC-OPF into a quadratic program, encrypts regional variables and coefficients with private matrices, computes coupled coefficients and aggregated constants via distributed consensus, then solves and decrypts locally.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Tested on multiple benchmark systems from 39-bus to 1354-bus with 24 time slots; proposed method matched centralized benchmark with very small relative errors.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The method reproduces centralized optimal dispatch accurately, scales to larger systems, and outperforms compared obfuscation approaches in solution quality.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: exact optimality preservation, confidentiality preservation, no tuning, robust convergence. Limitation: relies on linearized power flow and is not directly full AC OPF; TE fails in a single-period single-generator global-balance case.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Can be extended to AGC-aware and joint-chance-constrained OPF problems.

Martins; Alban Puech; Anna Varbella; Jonas Weiss; Juan Bernabe-Moreno; Alexandre Blondin Masse; Seong Lok Choi; Ian Foster; Bri-Mathias Hodge; Rishabh Jain; Kibaek Kim; Vincent Mai; François Miralles; Martin De Montigny; Octavio Ramos-Leanos; Hussein Suprême; Le Xie; El-Nasser S. Youssef; Arnaud Zinflou; Alexander Belyi; Ricardo J. Bessa; Bishnu Prasad Bhattarai; Johannes Schmude; Stanislav Sobolevsky
data_properties.hasInstitution: IBM Research; IBM Research - Europe; Equilibrium Energy, Inc.; ETH Zürich; EPFL; National Renewable Energy Laboratory; Argonne National Laboratory; U.S. Department of Energy; INESC TEC; Harvard University; Hydro-Québec; University of Chicago; University of Colorado; New York University; Masaryk University
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To advocate and outline grid foundation models for power-system operations, planning, and control.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Increasing grid complexity and uncertainty from the energy transition, climate change, aging infrastructure, and cybersecurity threats.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Lack of scalable, transferable AI methods for diverse power-grid tasks and power-flow-related applications.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can foundation models be developed for electric power grids to generalize across grid data and accelerate downstream applications such as power flow and OPF?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: No OPF model is solved in this paper; it proposes a GridFM-v0 concept for reconstructing power-flow states and, in discussed downstream use, optimal generation dispatch and objective values.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Graph neural network-based foundation model concept; masked autoencoder pre-training on graph-structured grid data.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power flow reconstruction on graph nodes with bus variables and line/transformer edges.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Initially single-time-step power-flow data; extendable to multiple consecutive time steps for forecasting.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: Single time step in the near-term model; high-resolution PMU data mentioned for dynamic extensions.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: Not specified; near-term focus is static power-flow applications.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses diverse topologies, load conditions, perturbations, and synthetic scenarios; discusses scenario trees and stochastic programming.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Transmission and distribution grid applications including power flow, OPF, contingency analysis, state estimation, stability, control, planning, and cybersecurity.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Self-supervised masked graph autoencoding with physics-informed loss; intended to speed up power-flow-related computation.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Projected 3–4 orders-of-magnitude speed-up over conventional power-flow solvers; less than 1% error cited from related GNN work.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Mentions load conditions, load forecasting, electric vehicles, heating electrification, and demand uncertainty.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: For OPF use, minimize generation costs by reconstructing generator power; the paper does not present a full OPF mathematical formulation.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Reconstructed node variables must satisfy power-flow equations and bounds such as generator capacity constraints.
data_properties.usesParameter: Bus active power, reactive power, voltage magnitude, voltage angle; line and transformer connectivity; topology, load conditions, and power-flow solutions.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: GridFM-v0 is proposed as a masked graph autoencoder pre-trained on solved power-flow cases from multiple topologies and load conditions, then fine-tuned for downstream tasks.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: No direct model validation results are reported for GridFM-v0; validation is proposed on open datasets and later on utility data behind firewalls.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The paper argues GridFMs could generalize across grid tasks and substantially accelerate power-system analysis, especially power-flow-related applications.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strengths: scalability, adaptability, and simulation acceleration. Limitations: data availability, privacy, trust, and difficulty accessing operational grid data.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: The paper is a perspective proposing a roadmap rather than presenting a completed OPF solver.

data_properties.hasPaperTitle: Day-Ahead and Real Time Optimal Power Flow considering Renewable Energy Resources
data_properties.hasAuthor: S. Surender Reddy; P.R. Bijwe
data_properties.hasInstitution: Woosong University; Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
data_properties.hasPrimaryPurpose: To schedule generation economically while maintaining security in day-ahead and real-time OPF with renewable variability.
data_properties.hasMotivation: Conventional DA-OPF and RT-OPF use static snapshots and ignore renewable/load variability within scheduling intervals.
data_properties.hasSolvedProblem: Optimal power flow for thermal-wind-solar systems with renewable variability, voltage, reactive power, line-flow, and ramp constraints.
data_properties.hasResearchQuestion: Can participation factors evaluated once at the start of each interval capture intra-interval renewable variability without increasing optimization dimensionality?
data_properties.hasPrimaryOutput: Optimal generator dispatch schedules, renewable generation schedules, interval costs/profits, and voltage stability index values.
data_properties.hasModelFeature: Single optimization with 'best-fit' participation factors over sub-interval variability.
data_properties.hasPowerFlowFormulationFeature: AC power-flow equations with voltage magnitude/angle, reactive power, and line-flow constraints.
data_properties.hasTimeHorizonFeature: Day-ahead and real-time multi-interval scheduling with 15-min and 1-min sub-intervals.
data_properties.hasTemporalResolution: RT-OPF: 1 min sub-intervals within 10-min intervals; DA-OPF: 15 min sub-sub-intervals within 1 h intervals.
data_properties.hasOptimizationHorizon: RT-OPF over 60 min; DA-OPF over 24 h.
data_properties.hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Uses forecasted solar, wind, and load variability within intervals; no explicit stochastic or robust formulation.
data_properties.hasPowerSystemDomainFeature: Thermal generators with wind and solar PV injections, AGC participation factors, ramp limits, and voltage stability index.
data_properties.hasSolutionMethodEnhancementFeature: Evaluates 'best-fit' participation factors once to avoid separate optimization for every sub-interval.
data_properties.hasModelPerformanceFeature: Reported lower total cost and improved voltage stability versus conventional interval-by-interval OPF.
data_properties.hasDemandSideFeature: Forecasted load demand varies within sub-intervals and is included in imbalance calculations.
data_properties.hasObjectiveFunction: Minimize total generation cost over RT sub-intervals; maximize total profit over DA intervals as revenue minus generation cost.
data_properties.hasConstraintFunction: Active and reactive nodal power balance, generator output limits with ramp-up/down limits, renewable output caps, bus-voltage limits, line-flow limits, and demand-supply balance constraint in DA-OPF.
data_properties.usesParameter: Generator cost coefficients; energy price; wind and solar direct cost coefficients; bus admittance Gij/Bij; ramp limits; voltage and line-flow limits; forecasted load, wind, and solar outputs; participation factors.
data_properties.hasSolutionDetailsSummary: MATLAB Optimization Toolbox FMINCON was used on the IEEE 30-bus system with wind at bus 11 and solar PV at bus 13.
data_properties.hasModelValidationSummary: Compared conventional and proposed RT-OPF/DA-OPF on IEEE 30-bus test system using 60-min RT and 24-h DA schedules.
data_properties.hasFindingsSummary: The proposed approach reduced RT total cost and increased DA profit while keeping optimization size unchanged and improving voltage stability.
data_properties.hasStrengthsAndLimitationsSummary: Strength: captures intra-interval variability with little added computational burden. Limitation: relies on forecast availability and fixed participation factors within each interval.
data_properties.hasFurtherProperty: Voltage stability was assessed using the L-index/VSEI.

evidence_package.why_matched: 包含AC-OPF、线路约束、可再生能源与负荷灵活性，并使用场景集参数，适合含不确定性的多时段调度背景。/ Includes AC-OPF, line constraints, renewable integration and load flexibility, with scenario-set parameters suitable for uncertain multi-period scheduling.
evidence_package.main_risk_or_gap: 主要是TSO-DSO灵活性市场清算，且未形成明确的概率鲁棒/机会约束AC-OPF；重点也不在风光与负荷不确定性的违约概率控制。/ Primarily a TSO-DSO flexibility market clearing model, not an explicit probabilistic-robust/chance-constrained AC-OPF; it does not focus on violation-probability control for wind, PV, and load uncertainty.
supporting_evidence: hasPrimaryPurpose: Model flexibility market clearing and TSO-DSO coordination using a hybrid AC/DC optimal power flow formulation.
hasUncertaintyHandlingFeature: Scenario-based planning mentioned, but probabilistic scenarios are not developed in this paper.
